So these do not control for themselves harm, neither repelling it nor bringing it, nor do they control benefit either. The author says: (meaning: attracting it). That is, they cannot draw benefit to themselves. Is that right? I have here: (meaning: attracting it)?
* Student: Yes, (attracting it).
* The Shaykh: Yes, they cannot draw benefit to themselves, nor can they repel it from themselves, like the first. That is, we should take it in its general sense, although the situation may imply that a person wants to repel harm and seek benefit, or that anyone wants to repel harm and seek benefit; but keeping the verse general is better. That is: they can do nothing for themselves, and if they cannot do that for themselves, then all the more they cannot do it for their worshippers.
(﴿And they do not control death or life﴾, meaning: causing death for anyone or giving life to anyone; ﴿nor resurrection﴾, meaning: raising of the dead.)
﴿They do not control death or life﴾, meaning: they cannot cause death for anyone. (...) We know that the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord and said: ﴿I give life and cause death﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258] was a liar or truthful? A liar.
﴿They do not control death or life﴾, meaning: they cannot bring death to anyone or bring life to anyone, however much they gather for that.
If someone says: Is it not possible that they could kill someone?
The answer: this is the cause of death, not death itself. A person can do the cause of death, but cannot bring about death itself, and there is a difference between the two. That is why sometimes the cause of death exists and the person does not die, and sometimes a person dies without a cause; that is, without a known cause.
So these do not control death or life for anyone; they cannot give life to any of the dead, because that belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
As for the revival of the dead by Isa, it is not of this category; it is not the matter negated by Allah, because the one who truly gives life to the dead is Allah, and for this reason Allah restricted His giving life to the dead by His saying: ﴿by My permission﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 110]. He does not act independently in this; rather his word was a cause of the life that Allah creates. Is it clear?
﴿Nor life, nor resurrection﴾: resurrection is the raising of the dead and their dispersal. Their scattering means they are dispersed; they come out of their graves and spread through the earth, dispersing in it. So they control none of this at all.
So when their inherent and accidental powerlessness becomes clear, it becomes clear that they are not fit to be gods; there is in them inherent and accidental incapacity.
Now, what is the station or state of ﴿they do not control death or life or resurrection﴾ in relation to His saying: ﴿they create nothing﴾?
Its coordination with His saying ﴿they create nothing﴾ is by way of coordinating the specific with the general, or detail after summary.
You now see the noble verse ascending from the lower to the higher: ﴿harm or benefit﴾, then ﴿death﴾, ﴿life﴾, and ﴿resurrection﴾. This is known, because life is greater than death; that is, the existence of the cause of life, or the power to give life, is greater than death. Likewise harm and benefit: which of them is greater? Benefit; because harm... a person seeks from harm the repelling of a thing, and repelling a thing is easier than bringing it, because bringing is positive and repelling is negative, and generally the negative is easier than the positive. So Allah, glorified and exalted, moved, in explaining the powerlessness of these gods and that they are not fit, from the lower to the higher. This is with regard to detail; as for summary, He said: ﴿they create nothing﴾.
* Among the benefits of this: it indicates that a person should present to his opponent what he must acknowledge, so that the proof is established against him.
Could those who made them gods claim that they create? No.
Could they claim that they are uncreated? No, because they know they exist and did not exist before.
Could they claim that they benefit or harm? We say: they can claim that, and indeed they do claim that; they say the saints benefit and harm, and that whoever does not slaughter for this saint or make a vow to him will be harmed by him. This is a claim.
What are they required to produce if they make such claims? They are required to produce evidence. Yes, the evidence would be that someone says to them, for example: call upon this saint regarding a specific matter and see whether he brings you that or not, just as they demand specific things from the messengers. For example, when the messengers told them that Allah gives life to the dead, they said: ﴿Bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 25], although the messengers did not tell them that resurrection would occur in this world, so that they could say: ﴿Bring our fathers.﴾ Rather they told them: when is the resurrection? After death. This differs from what these opponents demanded of the messengers. Their saying ﴿Bring our fathers﴾ is in reality begging the question; that is, demanding proof for something the messengers, peace be upon them, did not say, since they did not say that they would be raised now.
In any case, this claim that they possess benefit or harm is a claim requiring clear proof.
As for the claim of death and life, it is even more evidently false; indeed it might be claimed, because the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord said to him: ﴿I give life and cause death﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258], so it might be claimed.
And in the debate of Ibrahim, peace be upon him — that is, we may benefit from it here — is evidence that if the falsifier makes a claim, we move him to what is clearer, because the aim is not the argument itself; the aim is to establish the proof against the falsity of the matter. If it is refuted even by one proof, that suffices. There is no need that we refute it using the proof that the opponent specifies; we may refute it by another proof. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, if he had wished to argue with this man and dispute with him, would have said: you do not give life and cause death, you only do the cause of life and death. But he, peace be upon him, went to a clearer and more manifest proof that cannot be contested, to cut off dispute and argument, because a person who argues should be met with a proof he cannot repel. So he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258]. Is that a compelling argument or not? It is a compelling argument, with which he cannot claim anything. That is why Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So the one who disbelieved was confounded, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258].
The main point now: ﴿they create nothing﴾ is agreed upon; could its negation be claimed or not? It cannot. Even among the worshippers: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman 25], and ﴿if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 87]. Even among the worshippers, they cannot claim this negated attribute.
﴿While they themselves are created﴾: they also cannot claim that they are not created, because they are made; they fashioned them with their own hands. Ibrahim says to them: ﴿And Allah created you and what you make﴾ [As-Saffat 96].
﴿They do not control for themselves any harm or benefit﴾: we said that what can be claimed is the opposite of this negation, and our answer to it is in two ways:
Either we refute this very claim, saying: this is impossible, and if you wish, then call upon them.
Or it is said: we move away from this negation during debate — look — we do not move away from this negation out of lack of belief in Allah; we must believe that they do not possess that. But in the course of disputation, to what do we move? To a greater, clearer, and more manifest matter.
For example, if heavy, flooding rains came down or earthquakes occurred, we could say to them: call upon these idols and see whether (...) the sky, and whether the earth stops quaking. And the like. But whatever they claim or do not claim, in debate we move to a clearer matter they cannot deny: ﴿They do not control death or life or resurrection﴾.
When Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned what pertains to monotheism, He moved on to what pertains to prophethood, because (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah). So He said, exalted is He..
* Student: (...)?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 3–9 (part 2 of 5):

* The Shaykh: The difference between them is that nushur (resurrection, scattering) is general, whereas hayah (life) is specific, the life of one particular individual; such as saying to them, "Bring this dead person to life." Nushur is general, and for this reason we said that it derives from al-nashr, in the sense of dispersal and spreading out, so it is more comprehensive.
﴿And they possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection﴾. (﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is not but a lie [ifk] he has fabricated, and other people have helped him at it"﴾; i.e., what the Qur'an is, "not but a lie [ifk]," a falsehood, "he has fabricated," Muhammad, "and other people have helped him at it" [al-Furqan 4], and they are from the People of the Book.)
This is the second of the foundational principles in tawhid, which is affirming the prophethood (al-risalah). Affirming the message is undoubtedly one of the two halves of tawhid: ("I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah"). It is not possible to worship Allah, glorified and exalted, except by what the messengers have brought, because worship is the path for a person to his Lord.
Can we reach Allah by a path that He has not made a path? What is the answer?
* Students: It is not possible.
* The Shaykh: No. This path which Allah has made a path to Himself came through the messengers. Therefore worship must have a message, and Allah cannot be worshipped merely by reason; because worship is a path that leads to Allah, and this path cannot be known except by a determination from Allah. And Allah, glorified and exalted, made it through whom? Through the messengers.
Those who denied the messengers also disparaged the messengers and what they brought; ﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is not but a lie he has fabricated"﴾. Here He explicitly mentioned the noun directly. In the first verse He said ﴿and they have taken﴾ [al-Furqan 3] so as to include all the polytheists, Arabs and others; and here He said ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, meaning the Arabs who rejected the prophethood of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
(﴿This﴾, i.e., what the Qur'an is). The author is precise in his tafsir; he explained for us now, may Allah have mercy on him, he explained for us ﴿in﴾ and he explained for us the demonstrative pronoun.
﴿In﴾ in the sense of (ma), so it is negating; ﴿this﴾, he says: (the Qur'an), so the thing pointed to is the Qur'an.
﴿This is not but﴾, i.e., this is not the Qur'an, ﴿but a lie [ifk]﴾. Look, may Allah protect us, they brought restriction (hasr); meaning it cannot be anything but a lie, it cannot contain truth; so they brought restriction through negation and affirmation: ("this is nothing but a lie"), meaning: it cannot be truthful.
(A lie, a falsehood) meaning he invented it; i.e., the Prophet ﷺ.
﴿And other people have helped him at it﴾. He says: (from the People of the Book). And from this also is the man of whom they said: ﴿Only a human is teaching him﴾ [al-Nahl 103].
They say: this is not from Allah, rather it is from Muhammad ﷺ, he fabricated it with the help of others.
Allah, mighty and majestic, says refuting their words: (﴿They have committed injustice and falsehood﴾ [al-Furqan 4], disbelief and lying).
﴿They have committed injustice﴾: the author explained injustice (zulm) as disbelief, because disbelief is injustice; ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. Then also it is an injustice toward the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, because it is an assault upon him and a description of him as a liar; and if a person described someone among the people as a liar, we would say that he is unjust toward him and transgresses against him.
﴿And falsehood [zur]﴾: zur originally means everything that deviates from the straight path; every deviation is zur. ﴿And you see the sun, when it rises, inclining [tazawaru] away from their cave﴾ [al-Kahf 17]; it inclines, so every inclination is zur. And in the hadith: "Whoever does not abandon false speech [qawl al-zur] and acting upon it..." and what is meant is every deviant speech, "and acting upon it"[[The full hadith: "Whoever does not abandon false speech and acting upon it, Allah has no need for him to abandon his food and drink." Recorded by al-Bukhari (1903) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
Zur, then, is lying. So they are among the greatest liars, indeed the greatest liars in what they said. Is there any truth in their saying: ﴿This is not but a lie he has fabricated, and other people have helped him at it﴾? No, rather it is a lie, injustice and aggression against the Messenger ﷺ.
Then we say to them: if Muhammad ﷺ is the one who fabricated it and other people helped him at it, then bring a surah like it; ﴿Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [al-Tur 34]; ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants﴾ [al-Isra' 88].
Moreover, how long did Muhammad ﷺ live among them before the revelation? Forty years. He never once said that he was receiving revelation. Whoever wants to lie lies in the prime of his youth in order to gain followers from the outset. Since this did not happen until after forty years had passed, this shows that their claim is also refuted by reality; for this revelation came while the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, was at the age of forty, and it is not possible that lying would renew itself for him at this age.
Furthermore, we say: among what shows that it is delusion is that these people who say, "he fabricated it," themselves bear witness to the Messenger ﷺ's truthfulness; they used to call him al-Amin (the Trustworthy)[[al-Hakim (1701) recorded from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, may Allah be pleased with him: "And they used to call him in the Jahiliyyah al-Amin."]], and they did not doubt his truthfulness, nor did they doubt his uprightness, ﷺ. Where were they before?
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "Tales of the former peoples, which he has had written down [iktatabaha]"﴾ [al-Furqan 5].
(﴿And they say﴾ also: ﴿tales of the former peoples﴾, their falsehoods; plural of (usturah), with a damma; ﴿which he has had written down [iktatabaha]﴾, he had it copied from that people) what?
* A student: (from another [lighayrihi]).
* The Shaykh: (from another [bighayrihi]).
* The student: With a lam.
* The Shaykh: (lighayrihi)?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: I have it with a ba' (bighayrihi), ﴿so it is dictated to him﴾, it is read to him so that he may memorize it, ﴿morning and evening﴾ [al-Furqan 5], at dawn and at dusk.
﴿And they say: tales of the former peoples﴾. ﴿Asatir﴾ is the plural of usturah, and it refers to widely circulated narratives that have no basis; among the common people they call them (...), this is the usturah. They said: the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought the tales of the former peoples; meaning: their stories and narratives that have no basis.
Is this statement they made from belief, or according to reality? That is: is it from a false belief? Did they say it with their tongues, or did they say it according to reality? Did they claim it as a claim, or is this what they believe and what has become clear to them?
It could be this and it could be that. Allah, glorified and exalted, says in Surah al-Mutaffifin: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. And what can make you know what Sijjin is? It is a written record. Woe, that Day, to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. And none denies it except every sinful transgressor. When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the former peoples." Nay, but rather, what they have been earning has become like rust upon their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 7–14]. This indicates that their saying ﴿tales of the former peoples﴾ is not a mere claim but a belief, and that this is what they believe. If it was a claim while they believed it to be revelation and truth, then it is a false claim like other claims; and if this is what they believe, and it is what appeared to them from the Qur'an, then this is also not strange; because a person, may Allah protect us, when his heart is veiled, sees truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth. So it is possible that these people, because of their injustice, disbelief and aggression, the reality of the Qur'an did not become clear to them, and they thought it to be tales. And this, in truth, is a good meaning for the last point: that they say it not merely as a claim to deny the Messenger ﷺ, but according to reality as they believe; and that is because they have no sound, correct orientation toward accepting the truth, so truth was shown to them as falsehood.
Now, if we recite the Qur'an to a person who is averse, does he taste its sweetness? Does he feel that it is the speech of Allah? Does he feel that it is the most truthful of reports and the most just of rulings? No, never; you find him turned away from it, and it is nothing in his eyes in reality. Why? Because he, may Allah protect us, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight away, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am 110].
So their saying ﴿tales of the former peoples﴾ may be from belief, and that this is according to reality, because their condition requires it; and whenever a person turns away from the Qur'an, it becomes more hidden from him and further from knowing it, and whenever he turns toward it, his certainty and knowledge increase through it. Have you understood now?
For this reason I call you and myself to contemplate the Qur'an constantly and to reflect upon it, lest a person be unlettered (ummiyy). Allah the Exalted named those who do not know the meaning ("unlettered"); whoever does not know the meaning, even if he knows the wording, Allah calls him unlettered; as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who know not the Scripture except wishful thinking [amani]﴾ [al-Baqarah 78]. What is the meaning of ﴿amani﴾?
* The students: Recitation.
* The Shaykh: Recitation. So He named those who know the Scripture only as recitation "unlettered," because whoever reads and does not understand is like whoever does not read; there is no difference between them, except that this one has an understanding of the wording and that one does not have it (...). And what does a person benefit from the wording when he does not know its meaning?! Because the wording is like clothing for the body. If a person has garments, would he be a man? One has twenty garments and says: "By Allah, I want to take it from these people (...) upon them." What do you have? He says: "I have twenty garments." Do these garments benefit him? Twenty garments do not make twenty men.
So the point is, we say: the reality is that if a man does not turn to the Qur'an, contemplating it and eager to know its meaning, he benefits nothing from the Qur'an. And as you know the condition of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them; they would not go beyond ten verses until they learned them and what they contain of knowledge and action[[al-Tabari in his tafsir (1/80) recorded from Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: "Those who used to teach us told us that they used to seek to learn from the Prophet ﷺ; when they learned ten verses they would not move on until they acted upon what was in them. So we learned the Qur'an and the action together."]], so they learned the Qur'an, the knowledge and the action all together.
What harms us is that we are keen on reciting the Qur'an verbally, and this is good, but also meaningfully. It is possible that a person recites what is easy verbally, then when he has memorized what Allah has bestowed upon him, he contemplates it while walking, contemplates it on his bed, and through contemplating the Qur'an Allah opens to the person meanings he did not know and which did not occur to him; ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar 17]. Try it and you will find; because the Qur'an is an explanation of everything, and this is Allah's own statement about it. What prevents us from this explanation of everything is our not turning to this Qur'an, not contemplating it and not reflecting upon it; otherwise, if we contemplated it, we would find it an explanation of everything.
﴿And they say: tales of the former peoples, which he has had written down [iktatabaha]﴾, i.e., he had it copied from another. And also, the Messenger ﷺ, they know that he was unlettered, neither reading nor writing; but he ordered someone else to write it for him. For this reason the author says: (he had it copied from that people, from another); he had it copied through another, because they did not say "he wrote it," they said ﴿iktatabaha﴾; meaning he ordered another to write it for him, because they know that the Messenger ﷺ was unlettered, neither reading nor writing.
﴿So it is dictated to him morning and evening﴾ [al-Furqan 5]. ﴿It is dictated to him﴾ means: it is read to him, not dictated to him for him to write it, because he does not write; rather it is read to him ﴿in the morning﴾, at the beginning of the day, ﴿and in the evening﴾, at the end of the day. Then he brings it to the people and says: this is the speech of Allah, and this is revelation delivered to him; and in that, according to their claim, he is not truthful.
Allah the Exalted said in response to their saying..
* A student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: (...)?
* The Shaykh: It may be (...); both this and that are possible, and it is possible that some of them, like their elders, undoubtedly know the truth, but their common people may not know; this matter may be hidden from them and they say: ﴿tales of the former peoples﴾.
* A student: O Shaykh, the saying of Allah the Exalted: (...), is it derived from this that (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, it is not derived from this; it is derived from this generality and from every time. Whenever generality is intended, morning and evening are mentioned; ﴿And for them is their provision therein morning and evening﴾ [Maryam 62], although their provision does not cease in Paradise; ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 33]; but these two times are mentioned for continuity.
As for the reality and experience, we have tested that memorization at the beginning of the day is faster, and memorization at the end of the day, according to what I have tested, if you memorize at the end of the day it is not quick, but when you rise from sleep you find that you have memorized; so each of the two has its merit for memorization.
Allah refuted them by His saying: (﴿Say: He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth has sent it down﴾, the unseen, ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving﴾ to the believers, ﴿Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 6] toward them).
﴿Say: He has sent it down﴾ is a command to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to say to them in response to their saying: ﴿He has sent it down, the One who knows the secret﴾. We have mentioned previously that the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an; but when a ruling or a report comes and the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to say it, what indicates it? Attention to it and concern with it, as if it were a specific charge concerning this matter.
In this present context there is also an addition to that: it is support for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him; because when Allah is the One who instructs him the proof, that is more eloquent in supporting and strengthening him, is it not so? That is, as if Allah instructs him the argument so that he may argue on his behalf, but through his tongue.
﴿Say: He has sent it down﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth; indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾. It may appear to a person at first glance that this answer is not convincing, because this answer is the very same thing the Messenger was saying; for the Messenger kept saying that this revelation was sent down by Allah, from the outset. So is it possible... Are you understanding the speech now?
That is, at first glance it may appear to a person that this answer is unconvincing. How so? Because the Messenger was still saying that what was sent down is from Allah, so how can this answer be silencing for them and refuting their claim?
* A student: Because Allah, glorified and exalted (...).
* The Shaykh: And what is it?
* The student: ﴿He has sent it down, the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Furqan 6] (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 3–9 (part 3 of 5):

* The Shaykh: Zayn, this is one aspect. Another aspect lies in the words ﴿He who knows the secret﴾; for this reason Allah said: ﴿Say: It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Furqan 6]. Among the reports of this Qur'an are secrets that neither Muhammad ﷺ nor anyone else could know. For this reason Allah, glorified and exalted is He, turned away from saying "Say: It was sent down by Allah" to saying ﴿He who knows the secret﴾. That is, there are in the Qur'an secrets that are known: it gives a report and it comes to pass. Can the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, know that? No, he does not know it; only Allah knows it, and He is the One who sent it down. So from His words ﴿He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾ we derive a decisive proof that this Qur'an is not the speech of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, nor "tales of the ancients", because it contains reports about future matters which come to pass as it reported. I do not think any human being could manage that. This is a very clear aspect.

Another aspect that can be drawn: if this Qur'an were from Muhammad ﷺ and he attributes it to Allah, then Allah could not allow him to do this, because Allah, exalted is He, knows the secret. And this act that Muhammad ﷺ committed, on the assumption that it is not true, is it a secret or open? Open. So if Allah knows the secret, He knows the open all the more so. And if He knows the open, while Muhammad ﷺ says: this is the speech of Allah, then Allah, exalted is He, cannot leave him unpunished: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah 44–46]. ﴿Some sayings﴾: they are not all of them. ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta.﴾

So this is an argument from two aspects:
What is the first aspect? That the Qur'an contains secrets and reports of the unseen that no human being can bring.
The second matter: that if the Qur'an were from Muhammad ﷺ and he (...) to Allah and strives by it as well, striving by it and against it, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, would hasten to do what to him? To punish him; because Allah says: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾. This is the secret of the shift from "Say: It was sent down by Allah" to ﴿Say: It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾.

As for His words ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾: the author (...) the author altered the wording of the verse. The verse is ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾, and he says here: (﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾ toward the believers, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them). So what is your view of this alteration by the author? In reality this is a restriction for which there is no basis; Allah, exalted is He, is described by this attribute ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾ to everyone who deserves forgiveness. The believer who has the basis of faith but commits sins..

Differing from the Ottoman script is permissible. They said: because the script has rules subject to each nation and each era, and if the Qur'an had been written down at the time of its revelation in another manner, it would have been written in another manner.

So (...) the first view says: differing from the Ottoman script is not permissible, and a person who writes the Qur'an for himself or for others, for teaching or recitation, or in any circumstance, must write it in the Ottoman script, based on the principle that this is a matter of tawqif (revealed prescription). Just as we do not change the wording, so we do not change the writing.

Second: it is permissible for the Qur'an to be written according to the rules by which writing is done in any era, and there is no obligation to adhere to the Ottoman script.

They said: because writing has rules that vary with eras and nations, and the Qur'an was not sent down in writing but was sent down to be recited by utterance, not by writing, so that we could say writing is tawqifi. And because if the rules of orthography, at the time of the Qur'an's revelation, had been otherwise, would it have been written accordingly or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Suppose the orthography at the time of the revelation, or at the time of its compilation in the era of 'Uthman, radiya Allahu 'anhu, had been other than these rules; would it have been written by them or in something else? It would have been written by them. This shows that writing follows the era in which it is written.

The third view: a distinction. If it is written for a scholar, then in the Ottoman script; if it is written for an ignorant person, then in the modern script of his time. They said: because if an ignorant person is written for in the Ottoman script, he will err in pronunciation. For example, we want to write (al-salah) (the prayer) in the Ottoman script, where there is a waw in it.
* Student: al-Salawat.
* The Shaykh: The ignorant person reads it, for example, as al-salawat, or al-salawt. Likewise al-zakah, likewise al-riba, and similar words. These people distinguish between writing for a scholar and writing for an ignorant person.

The correct view is the second: it is permissible to write the Qur'an according to the modern rules in which it is written, because its writing is not tawqifi, since it was not sent down in writing. So we say: it is obligatory to adhere to what it was sent down upon; rather, it was written in an era when the rules of orthography were in this form, so it remained in this form.
* Student: Perhaps, O Shaykh (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, that does not occur; its origin is that it is recited, and recitation preserves it from distortion.

Good. Based on this disagreement: is writing the Qur'an in Braille permissible or not?
* Student: It is permissible.
* The Shaykh: No, it is not permissible, all the more so; because these dots are furthest from being letters. On this basis it is absolutely not permissible to write it, though people now act contrary to this; there are now complete copies written in this manner.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, verbally; it is not a translation.
* Student: Is it written in Braille in the Ottoman script?
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: What does that mean?
* The Shaykh: Now, for example: ﴿And when Allah said﴾ [al-Ma'idah 116]; ﴿said﴾ is not written in Braille except according to the rules of Braille, according to its form (...).
* Student: Yes, indeed, it is not written (...), O Shaykh; most of it is abbreviations.
* The Shaykh: No, even if we assume it remains as it is, if there are abbreviations, then they must be examined, even if we say it is permissible.
* Student: No, most of them are abbreviations; we learned in (...) most of them are abbreviations; they abbreviate words into dots (...) the letter.
* The Shaykh: One dot?
* Student: That is, perhaps a complete word, for example (kayf) (how), especially well-known words.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they represent it by a symbol?
* Student: Yes, a symbol; perhaps he symbolized it by one letter.
* The Shaykh: Meaning they drop some letters in writing?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: This is further from permissibility; this is further away, so even if we say it is permissible, this must be considered.
* Student: O Shaykh, regarding writing the Qur'an for us, that is (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, recitations in the Ottoman script come correctly, but before vocalization and i'rab (grammatical inflection) existed. Pointing (i'jam) now prevents it: ﴿fa-tabayyanu﴾ [al-Hujurat 6], for example, after it was pointed and dotted, you cannot read it as ﴿fa-tathabbatu﴾.
* Student: No, like His words, exalted is He: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah 4]?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: It is read ﴿Malik yawm al-din﴾?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: In it, meaning in the Ottoman script, the alif is removed, so it is read in both ways.
* The Shaykh: Now?
* Student: But if it were written in the familiar writing, it would admit only one reading, which is (...).
* The Shaykh: Now ﴿Malik﴾: if I read it in the Ottoman script without vocalization, straightaway we read it ﴿Malik﴾, and we cannot read it ﴿Maalik﴾, right?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And with vocalization you read it ﴿Maalik﴾, because the alif is represented by a short stroke.
* Student: For the noun.
* The Shaykh: By a short stroke?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: So in any case this and that will become clear; meaning after vocalization, in reality, the reading is not made clear; meaning one word does not comprise the reading.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, not at all; this is not forbidden.
* Student: Regarding Braille writing, was the Noble Qur'an not sent down intended for pronouncing it, meaning for people to learn?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: So what prevents the writing from being in this (...)?
* The Shaykh: We say this is based on the disagreement; but if we say it is permissible, then the Braille method is permissible, yes. But what makes the matter problematic for us is what the brother said, that it contains abbreviation.
* Student: If one understands the meaning?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: If, for example, he understands that this dot is, for instance, (kayf) or (limadha).
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed.
* Student: So the Qur'an would be complete, meaning in pronunciation?
* The Shaykh: There is no problem with it.
* Student: No problem?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed; according to the view of permissibility the matter is broad. According to the view that writing the Qur'an other than in the Ottoman script is permissible, the matter is broad. People still, for teaching children, write it in the modern script, and I see no problem with the permissibility of the modern script without need, even if a person has no need for it, because, as we indicated at the beginning. At the beginning we mentioned three aspects of permissibility: that the Qur'an was sent down...?
* Student: To be recited.
* The Shaykh: Uttered, not written; and then tawqif is excluded.
Second: that it was written in this form only because the official orthographic rule at that time was in this form, not because, for example, the Messenger said: write it in this manner, or that Jibril descended with it in this manner... and so on.
* Student: There is a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ commanding that it be written in this manner.
* The Shaykh: In this manner?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Where is it?
* Student: In a hadith (...) ﷺ: "Extend the alif," I do not remember the wording of the hadith: "and vowel the lam..."
* The Shaykh: I do not know it.
* Student: No (...), there is a hadith, O Shaykh, explained by al-Zarqani.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: It mentions the manner in which the Prophet ﷺ instructed them to write the Qur'an, by saying to them, meaning: "Extend the alif," or "vowel the lam."
* The Shaykh: Well, if he said "extend the alif," this is for them, because in ﴿Malik yawm al-din﴾, if we extend the alif we write the alif. Although I do not believe this would be proper from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, not at all, that he would say: write (al-salah) with a waw, write (al-zakah) with a waw, write (al-riba) with a waw.
* Student: No, he mentioned in it the five rules of orthography (...), meaning omission, joining, and...
* The Shaykh: In any case, whoever changes the wording must be addressed, if the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did not command a specific verbal command; this is known: whoever changes the wording.
* Student: (...) according to the seven ahruf, so that you consider them the seven ahruf.
* The Shaykh: Not at all; we do not consider them the seven ahruf. The seven ahruf concern utterance, not writing.

The third aspect: we are certain that if the official orthographic rules at that time had been of another form, it would undoubtedly have been written by them; it could not have been written other than by the official rules of that time.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but in the era of 'Uthman, radiya Allahu 'anhu, they wrote according to the official rules, as it appears to me, in Madinah at that time, even if it were permissible otherwise; since 'Uthman ordered the burning of all copies that differed from this in wording, even ordering them burnt in wording, so that the people might be united.

On this basis we say: this view is the stronger, that it is permissible to write the Qur'an according to the modern rules, and that it is not permissible to write it in the Ottoman script for the ignorant. This is also what we see: a person who is ignorant, whom we are not teaching verbally, meaning we do not teach him recitation orally, it is not permissible to write to him in the Ottoman script, and the reason is that if he reads it according to the Ottoman script, while he has not been taught it by recitation, he will distort the Qur'an.
* Student: O Shaykh, regarding the adherents of the second view, who hold that (...) interpreted regarding (...)?
* The Shaykh: Regarding?
* Student: For the ignorant, meaning it is obligatory to write the Qur'an in the manner in which he reads (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Good, from it we infer also that (...)?
* The Shaykh: There is no doubt about it; this applies if we say it is permissible, whether in detail or absolutely; so this Braille method is permissible out of need.

﴿And they said: What is this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets?﴾ [al-Furqan 7]. We said: (ma) is interrogative, and (li hadha) is a prepositional phrase serving as the predicate of the subject, and ﴿eats food﴾ the clause, what is its place in i'rab? Let us bring a verse resembling it so that it becomes clear to you: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ [al-Muddaththir 49]. How do you parse ﴿turning away﴾?
* Student: (...) a circumstantial clause (hal).
* The Shaykh: A circumstantial clause. So ﴿eats food﴾ is a circumstantial clause: the clause is in the accusative of state, meaning: what is wrong with him eating food? As if they say: if he were a messenger, he would not eat food. This is one.

Second: ﴿and walks in the markets﴾: walking in the markets among the people, not elevating himself, not hiding in his house, nor walking with his soldiers right and left, in front and behind. Why does he walk in the markets?

﴿Why has not an angel been sent down to him, to be a warner with him?﴾, meaning, as if they say: and why was there not an angel with him? Because (lawla) means: why not, and it is for urging.

His words ﴿angel﴾: one of the angels; it is derived from al-ulukah, which linguistically means message, and Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ [Fatir 1].

﴿to be a warner with him﴾: with whom? With the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿a warner﴾, meaning one who warns, so that by this he would know that he is truthful.

The fourth aspect: (﴿Or a treasure be bestowed upon him﴾ [al-Furqan 8] from heaven, so that he would spend it and need not walk in the markets to seek livelihood).

﴿a treasure be bestowed upon him﴾, meaning: sent down from heaven. ﴿A treasure﴾ from heaven. We say "from heaven" because His words ﴿upon him﴾ indicate termination and limit; otherwise it would be permissible: ﴿or a treasure be bestowed upon him﴾, meaning: he finds a treasure in the earth. But ﴿ila﴾ conveys termination and limit, so the meaning is: ﴿bestowed upon him﴾ descending from heaven, ﴿upon him﴾ from heaven, ﴿a treasure﴾ for what purpose? So that he would have great wealth, and would not need to walk in the markets, and poverty would not afflict him as it did the Prophet ﷺ.

How many is this? ﴿eats food﴾, ﴿and walks in the markets﴾, ﴿why has not an angel been sent down to him﴾, ﴿or a treasure be bestowed upon him﴾.

(﴿A garden be his﴾, an orchard, ﴿from which he may eat﴾, meaning: from its fruits, so he is content with it. In another reading ﴿nakulu﴾ with a nun, meaning: we, so that he would have an advantage over us by it.)

(In another reading) is it a seven reading or a shadhdh reading?
* Student: Seven.
* The Shaykh: Seven; because the rule of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, is that when he says "and in a reading" it is seven, and when he says "and it was read" it is shadhdh.

So there are two readings: ﴿yakulu minha﴾ and ﴿nakulu minha﴾, ﴿yakulu﴾ and ﴿nakulu﴾.

Good, these are five matters they raised as objections.

(﴿And the wrongdoers said﴾, meaning the disbelievers to the believers, ﴿You follow only a man bewitched﴾, deluded, overcome in his intellect.)

﴿And the wrongdoers said﴾: first, is there here an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, or not? Because at the beginning everything was pronouns: ﴿And they said: What is this Messenger﴾, and here: ﴿And the wrongdoers said﴾. The explicit noun in place of the pronoun has benefits, and I think we have mentioned them before.
* Student: First (...).
* The Shaykh: Recording this description against them, meaning clarifying their state, that they are with this description, meaning that they are wrongdoers. This is one.

Good, the second?
* Student: Attention to (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verses 3–9 (part 4 of 5):

* The Shaykh: Attention. How so? There is nothing in it.
The second benefit: this statement is considered an injustice, so the ruling is general, meaning that everyone who says it is a wrongdoer.
The third benefit: alerting the listener. When speech follows one pattern, a person becomes absorbed and may drift off. When something comes that departs from the first pattern, attention is aroused. This benefit concerns wording, while the first two concern meaning.
* A student: The cause (...)?
* The Shaykh: This is taken from the second matter, the second benefit.
As we said, the first benefit is that this describes these people with this outward characteristic. If it is disbelief, it is disbelief; if it is injustice, it is injustice; if it is wickedness, it is wickedness; if it is faith, it is faith, and so on to the end.
The second benefit: this ruling, statement or action is an injustice, whoever commits it. This is what (...) pointed to, because it is the reason (ta'lil).
The third benefit: alerting the listener, because a change in speech, or in the pattern of speech, calls for attention.
Regarding ﴿إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ﴾, the author says: (﴿إِنْ﴾ means "mā"). The word "mā" here explains ﴿إِنْ﴾, meaning that ﴿إِنْ﴾ is negative. When it is negative, the matter involves restriction (ḥaṣr): "You follow nothing but ﴿رَجُلًا﴾ (a man)." This is more emphatic than their saying "Indeed, you follow a man who is bewitched." It is as if they said: the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, has no state whatsoever except that he is bewitched, meaning deceived and overpowered in his mind, that is, his intellect is disordered by sorcery.
Among the wonders is that at times they say he is ﴿ساحر﴾ (a sorcerer) [al-Dhariyat 52], and at other times they say he is ﴿مسحور﴾ (bewitched) [al-Isra' 47], and there is a difference between the two. But with this falsifier, whatever false claims he can make, he will make, even if (...).
Let us now look at these six things with which they disparaged the Prophet ﷺ.
First: ﴿مَا لِهَذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ﴾ (What is wrong with this Messenger that he eats food?). How shall we answer them? What shall we reply to them with?
* A student: That he is a human being.
* The Shaykh: That he is a human being. He needs food, and this is not a disqualification, as long as the evidences or proofs have testified to his truthfulness. His eating food does not prevent his truthfulness, because he is a human being.
﴿وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ﴾ (and walks in the markets)...
* A student: Also.
* The Shaykh: No, this is not part of human nature. Cattle walk in the markets, and camels walk in the markets.
* A student: Humility.
* Another student: (...) seeking provision, that is.
* The Shaykh: Yes, humility, correct. We answer them that this supports his being a Messenger, not that it contradicts it, because it shows his humility and his love to be among his nation, benefiting them and benefiting from them.
So this is clearer as evidence for the message than as a barrier to the message, is it not?
Now, ﴿لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ﴾ (why was not an angel sent down to him?). It is as if they are saying: why was an angel not sent down to him?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. It is said: first, an angel was indeed sent down to him, but not in the way they demanded, walking with him and giving warning. Jibril was sent down to the Prophet ﷺ with the revelation, and this is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said. As for his having an angel accompanying him, this does not detract from the message if it is not accompanying him, because if it were accompanying him and came in a form other than the angelic form, the matter would return to what it was. The argument or doubt they raise would still exist. And if he were made an angel in the form of an angel, the matter would be decided against them if they did not believe, because when specific signs are requested and those who requested them do not believe, they are destroyed.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, they are not specific. That is why we qualified it: specific signs when they are requested. But if they say, "Show us a sign" without specifying it, then perhaps they will not be destroyed by it.
Okay, ﴿يُلْقَى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ﴾ (a treasure be thrown to him). They say: why has he not become wealthy? His being poor shows that he is not a Messenger. How shall we answer them?
* A student: Because the Messenger ﷺ called to this; he called to sufficiency and seeking provision.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but they say: you are a Messenger, so why was a treasure not sent down to you, through which you could become independent of seeking provision?
* The student: This indicates (...).
* A student: Because all the prophets were poor, as it is established: ﴿وَكَانُوا يَأْكُلُونَ مِنْ كَسْبِ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ (and they used to eat from the earnings of their own hands).[[Al-Bukhari (2072) narrated from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No one has ever eaten food better than what he eats from the work of his own hands, and the Prophet of God, Dawud, peace be upon him, used to eat from the work of his own hands."]]
* The Shaykh: Okay, and anything else?
* A student: And because the Messenger ﷺ was given a choice between (...).
* The Shaykh: This does not contradict it. He was given the choice between mountains accompanying him as gold, or between being an angel-prophet or a servant-prophet, and he chose this.[[Al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra (4312) narrated that Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, used to relate that God, blessed and exalted, sent to His Prophet ﷺ an angel from among the angels, along with Jibril. The angel said: "God gives you the choice between being a servant-prophet and being a king-prophet." The Messenger of God ﷺ turned to Jibril as one seeking counsel, and Jibril gestured with his hand: be humble. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Rather, I will be a servant-prophet." He said: After that word, he never ate food reclining.]] But this is not convincing in itself.
* A student: Because what he brought is a great matter of calling (...), and of faith in God, glorified and exalted. So it is not, meaning (...), wealth and other things, rather he was to alert them to...
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, okay.
* A student: Because a person may have, for example, wealth and not be a Messenger. How many people of status have it, and that is not evidence of (...).
* The Shaykh: So the meaning is that the message does not depend on it?
* The student: On wealth.
* The Shaykh: On wealth. The message does not depend on wealth, and wealth is not evidence of the message, because there are many rich people who are not messengers.
* A student: Furthermore, if he had wealth, he would have been followed for the sake of his wealth.
* The Shaykh: This is a positive point. What you said is a positive point, but we want the rebuttal, the repelling of their claim. Then we say, as the brother indicated, that his lack of wealth may be more supportive of his being a Messenger, because if wealth had been sent down to him and people followed him because of it, the matter would become that they followed him for his wealth rather than for his message.
So we say: this, that a treasure was not sent down to him, is not a barrier to the message. Why? Because the establishment of the message does not depend on a treasure; it is established without it. And because if he had a treasure, it would have been said: people followed him for his treasure and his wealth. This is a refutation of their claim.
﴿أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا﴾ (or he be given a garden from which he eats). We say about it what we said about the treasure: this is not a requirement of the message, and if he had ﴿لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا﴾ (a garden from which he eats), or ﴿نَأْكُلُ﴾ (we eat) according to the second reading (...), it would have been said: they followed him for the sake of eating from this garden.
Sixth: ﴿وَقَالَ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا﴾ (And the wrongdoers said, "You follow nothing but a man bewitched"). How shall we answer them?
* A student: With the Quranic verses.
* The Shaykh: No, but the Quranic verses are not believed by them, they do not believe in the Quran.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And anything other than this?
* A student: We answer them (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, we answer them that the bewitched cannot bring such speech. He brings speech that the intelligent cannot match, and then they say he is bewitched. Is that possible or not?
* A student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Is it possible that a person bewitched and deranged in mind by sorcery brings speech that eloquent people cannot match, and challenges the intelligent to bring its like, and they cannot, or is it not possible? It is not possible. This is very clear, and that is why God, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ فَضَلُّوا فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا﴾ (Look how they have coined for you comparisons, so they have strayed and cannot find a way) [al-Furqan 9].
* A student: Likewise I would say that (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, the sorcerer (...), but it affected the bewitched person, so he cannot bring such speech.
* The student: If a sorcerer's sorcery is nullified, then the bewitched should be more deserving of having the sorcery nullified.
* The Shaykh: No, in principle he does not bring disciplined speech. We do not say that he brings speech that may or may not be refuted. He cannot bring anything except unbalanced speech, so how about miraculous speech?!
God the Exalted said: ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ (Look how they have coined for you comparisons). The interrogative in His saying ﴿كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ﴾ (how they have coined for you) is for astonishment and denial.
His saying ﴿الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ (the comparisons) means likenesses or descriptions, because the word "mathal" comes to mean likeness and comes to mean description. God the Exalted said: ﴿مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ فِيهَا أَنْهَارٌ﴾ (The description of the Garden promised to the righteous: in it are rivers) [Muhammad 15]; the meaning of ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ here is the description of the Garden. ﴿مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ﴾ (Their likeness is like that of one who kindled a fire) [al-Baqarah 17], meaning: their resemblance is like the resemblance of... So "amthal" means either likenesses or descriptions. That is, how did they make these descriptions with which they disparage your message? Look at them in astonishment, and astonishment in most cases implies denial.
(﴿كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ by describing you as bewitched, and as one in need of what he spends, and as one who needs an angel to stand with him in the matter, ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾ (so they have strayed) thereby from guidance, ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا﴾ (so they cannot find a way), meaning a path to it.)
God's saying ﴿كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ﴾ is addressed to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. That He addresses the Messenger ﷺ with this denunciation of them does not hide the support and strengthening it contains for the Messenger ﷺ, and God's care for him ﷺ, and this is a known matter.
As for His saying ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾ (so they have strayed), the fa' here is conjunctive but indicates causation, meaning: because of what they coined for you of comparisons, they went astray. In this is evidence that when a person raises doubts about himself, or about the one who came with the truth, he becomes a cause of his own straying. If a person does not accept the truth and leaves aside the doubts that come to his mind regarding that truth, he becomes a cause of his own straying. This is why He said ﴿فَضَلُّوا﴾; the fa' is conjunctive and indicates causation.
Ibn al-Qayyim mentioned in Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah that he spoke with his shaykh Ibn Taymiyyah about issues (...). He says: I began to raise objections to him, and he said to me: Do not make your heart like a sponge that accepts every doubt and soaks it up, but make it like a hard glass that reveals what is behind it and is not affected. This is true. When a person opens to himself the door of doubts and questionings, he goes astray. Look at the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ regarding a man when people ask: "Who created this? Who created that? Who created that?" until they say: "Who created God?" The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded a person who reaches this point to seek refuge in God and to desist, and he guided him to recite ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (1) اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ (2) لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (3) وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (4)﴾ (Say: He is God, the One. God, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him) [al-Ikhlas 1–4]. In another hadith: ﴿هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ﴾ (He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden) [al-Hadid 3].
So these thoughts that come to the heart, if a person indulges in them, will be a cause of his straying, as this verse and many other verses indicate, such as: ﴿وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَنَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ﴾ (And We turn their hearts and their eyes, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly) [al-An'am 110]. So a person must be receptive to the truth, seeking it and accepting it, and must not place doubts upon himself, because doubts have no limit, and Satan loves for the son of Adam to let these doubts come upon his heart so that he may go astray.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, ("the bewitched") is clear. And that he ﴿يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ﴾ (eats food and walks in the markets), and ﴿يُلْقَى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ (a treasure is thrown to him, or he has a garden), are all included in His saying: (and one in need of what he spends, and of an angel who stands with him).
The summary now, O people: these disbelievers set up gods alongside God, and this is a disparagement of monotheism. Then they claimed that the Quran is the fables of the ancients, and this is a direct disparagement of the Quran, and it includes disparagement of God as well as disparagement of the Messenger ﷺ. Then God mentioned their direct disparagement of the Messenger ﷺ, through these six aspects, and it became clear, praise be to God, that these aspects they put forward as disparagement of the Prophet ﷺ are not disparagement at all; rather, some of them even support that he is a Messenger.
Some scholars cited this verse as evidence that the Prophet ﷺ was not bewitched, and they denied the well-known, indeed mass-transmitted (mutawatir), hadiths that the Prophet ﷺ was bewitched and that God sent down the two Mu'awwidhatayn to nullify that sorcery.[[Abd ibn Humayd (271) narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So he fell ill, and Jibril came to him and descended upon him with the two Mu'awwidhatayn... the hadith.]] Is there any basis for their citing this verse or not?
* A student: It has a basis.
* The Shaykh: How so?
* The student: Because it (...) the wrongdoers.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but they... Now we do not doubt that the Messenger ﷺ was bewitched, and that the two Mu'awwidhatayn were sent down upon him and his sorcery was nullified by them. This is beyond doubt, because the hadiths about it are mass-transmitted. They say: all these hadiths are lies, they are not authentic, because saying that he was bewitched is the saying of the disbelievers.
* A student: It has no basis, because (...).
* The Shaykh: No, it is not of this description, it is not this refutation. It is correct, it has no basis, but it is not of this...
* A student: Their saying "a bewitched man" indicates a permanent, inherent description.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: That is, this is his constant state, that he is bewitched. But the sorcery that the Jew bewitched him with was something that arose, like an illness, meaning it can be removed by remedies.
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is correct. This is the answer to them. We say: these wrongdoers who said ﴿إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا﴾ (You follow nothing but a man bewitched) intended by this that sorcery is an inherent description of him, and that all this speech he makes is bewitched speech (...). As for the sorcery that befell the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, it was an incidental sorcery, and even then it did not affect the message at all. 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, said: what happened was that he would imagine that he had done something when he had not done it.[[Al-Bukhari (6063) and Muslim, with the wording of Muslim (2189/43), narrated from 'A'ishah, who said: A Jew from the Jews of Bani Zurayq, called Labid ibn al-A'sam, bewitched the Messenger of God ﷺ. She said: So that the Messenger of God ﷺ would imagine that he was doing something when he was not doing it. Then one day, or one night, he called upon God, and called, and called, and then said: "O 'A'ishah, do you realize that God has answered what I asked Him about? Two men came to me; one sat at my head and the other at my feet. The one at my head said to the one at my feet, or the one at my feet to the one at my head: What is the matter with the man? He said: He is bewitched. He said: Who bewitched him? He said: Labid ibn al-A'sam. He said: With what? He said: With a comb and hair combings, and the pollen sheath of a male date palm. He said: Where is it? He said: In the well of Dhi Arwan." She said: So the Messenger of God ﷺ went to it with some of his companions, then said: "O 'A'ishah, by God, its water is like the infusion of henna, and its palm trees are like the heads of devils." She said: I said: O Messenger of God, why not burn it? He said: "No, as for me, God has granted me well-being, and I disliked to stir up evil among the people, so I ordered it to be buried."]] This is what happened, and it was for a short period, and it did not affect it. That is, he said nothing regarding the message that could have changed the message during this period.

Therefore, the conclusion is that using this verse to invalidate sound, mutawatir hadiths is undoubtedly a great audacity. Had the hadiths been weak, or had they been, for example, among the hadiths at the lowest levels of authenticity, we would say that this has some basis. But as for sound, well-known, mutawatir hadiths, invalidating them by such a matter is not possible. Therefore, the correct position, indeed the certain and definite conviction, is that this happened to the Messenger (ﷺ), but Allah the Exalted sent down to him two surahs, and then he was guided to the place of the magic. Where was his magic? In the well of Arees. It was in a comb and hair in the sheath of a male date-palm spathe, meaning the kafur (the spathe). Do you know kafur? The kafur of the stallion (male palm) is large and wide. This magic was placed for the Messenger (ﷺ) in a comb with which the head is combed, and the mushah is the hair that scatters during combing, and this was put in the well to which the Messenger (ﷺ) used to come. So the Prophet (ﷺ) went and ordered that this magic be taken out, and the magic was taken out and undone, and Allah the Exalted granted him recovery.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they have strayed, and they cannot find a way﴾. ﴿Sabeelan﴾ means "a way." To what? To guidance, and we seek refuge in Allah. In this there is a warning, as we pointed out at the beginning, a warning against a person following the doubts that come to him, and that a person must keep far away from all of this.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 3–9 (part 1 of 5):

(...) The verse now. First, the revelation of the Qur'an was mentioned (...).
* Student: (...) ﴿So they have committed injustice and falsehood (4). And they say, "Myths of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." (5) Say, "It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful." (6) And they say, "What is with this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him to be a warner along with him? (7) Or a treasure be thrown to him, or he be given a garden from which to eat?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by magic." (8) See how they have coined for you comparisons, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾ [Al-Furqan 4–9].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods that create nothing, while they themselves are created﴾ [Al-Furqan 3].
(﴿And they have taken﴾ means: the disbelievers. ﴿besides Him﴾ means: besides Allah.) As for the first pronoun, ﴿they have taken﴾, no explicit antecedent has been mentioned for it, but its referent is known from the context; that is, ﴿they have taken besides Him﴾ — who are they?
* Student: The disbelievers.
* The Shaykh: The disbelievers who took them. It has no antecedent in wording, but its referent is known from the situation.
As for ﴿besides Him﴾, its referent is clear from what preceded, because Allah spoke of Himself in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and they have taken besides Him﴾.
The connection of this verse to what precedes it is that when Allah praised Himself with what He praised Himself with, it was appropriate to mention those idols that were taken besides Him — meaning besides Allah — as gods, so that their state would be made clear, because things are made clear by the attributes they possess.
﴿And they have taken besides Him gods﴾: the word ﴿gods﴾ is the plural of (ilah, god). These gods were gods only by their taking, but in reality they are not gods, because they do not deserve worship. Is that not so?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division. They are not but names you have named them, you and your fathers; Allah has sent down no authority for them﴾ [An-Najm 19–23]. And Yusuf said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer? What you worship besides Him are but names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [Yusuf 39, 40]. So they are gods in name and in their belief, but in reality they are not gods; meaning they do not deserve to be gods. Is it clear, O brothers?
So if someone says: how did Allah here establish that they are gods, ﴿they have taken besides Him gods﴾, when all the prophets, peace be upon them, said to their peoples: ﴿Worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾ [Hud 61], and Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [Al-Baqarah 163]. How do we reconcile this negation with this affirmation?
We say: we reconcile this negation and this affirmation in that the negation is with regard to reality and fact, for there is no god except Allah, and there is no doubt about that; and the affirmation is according to what? According to the actions of these people, in that they made these into gods, that is, objects of worship; and there is no doubt that they are worshipped, but they do not deserve to be worshipped. So, with regard to what is deserved, there is negation, and with regard to what actually happens, there is affirmation. Is the matter clear or not?
With regard to what is deserved, there is negation; that is, no one deserves, and no one is truly a god, except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. As for belief and action, some people believe and act so as to take another god alongside Allah, and the reality of these gods is that they are nothing. It is true that they are worshipped, called upon, bowed to, prostrated to, and vowed to, but in reality they do not deserve this, so they are not gods.
Then Allah explained these taken gods: ﴿they create nothing﴾, and their not creating is a proof of their powerlessness, and their powerlessness is a proof that they are not gods, because a god must necessarily be capable, since capability is part of perfection; and this incapacity which these gods are characterized by prevents them from being gods.
Second: ﴿while they themselves are created﴾. Who is ﴿while they themselves are created﴾? The gods. So they are originated after they were not, and the Lord must be primordial, nothing preceding Him; for the Lord deserving worship must be a creator, and if He is created, He is originated, and if He is originated, then whoever came before Him is not of His creation. Thus, in His saying ﴿they create nothing﴾ there is an explanation of their unfitness for divinity in terms of what? The absence of ability.
﴿while they themselves are created﴾ also makes it unfit for them to be gods, in two respects:
First: origination, for they are originated, and a god cannot be originated.
Second: whoever came before them and preceded them is not of their creation, supposing they could create, and this is a proof of their unfitness for divinity.
﴿They create nothing, while they themselves are created, and they do not control for themselves any harm or benefit, and they do not control death or life or resurrection﴾ [Al-Furqan 3]. The author says: (﴿they do not control for themselves any harm﴾, meaning: its repelling). We say: its repelling and its bringing as well. What prevents it?! If they wished to harm themselves, they would not harm themselves, and if they wished to repel harm from themselves, they would not repel it. So keeping the verse general is better: ﴿they do not control for themselves any harm﴾, meaning: neither bringing harm nor repelling it. Even harm that might be easy, if they wished it for themselves they could not do it. That is, if these idols wished to destroy themselves, could they do it or not?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: If they wished to make themselves sick, if they were the kind that can become sick, would they have that power or not? They do not. And if someone wished to attack them, could they repel him or not?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: They cannot. That is why Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it﴾, and this indicates its importance; Allah's command to us to listen to this parable indicates its importance.
The parable: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gather together for it﴾. The fly, which is among the weakest and feeblest of creatures — if they gathered together to create it, they could not.
Another matter: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them something, they could not rescue it from it﴾, despite its weakness, ﴿weak are the seeker and the sought﴾ [Al-Hajj 73].
So these do not control for themselves harm, neither repelling it nor bringing it, nor do they control benefit either. The author says: (meaning: attracting it). That is, they cannot draw benefit to themselves. Is that right? I have here: (meaning: attracting it)?
* Student: Yes, (attracting it).
* The Shaykh: Yes, they cannot draw benefit to themselves, nor can they repel it from themselves, like the first. That is, we should take it in its general sense, although the situation may imply that a person wants to repel harm and seek benefit, or that anyone wants to repel harm and seek benefit; but keeping the verse general is better. That is: they can do nothing for themselves, and if they cannot do that for themselves, then all the more they cannot do it for their worshippers.
(﴿And they do not control death or life﴾, meaning: causing death for anyone or giving life to anyone; ﴿nor resurrection﴾, meaning: raising of the dead.)
﴿They do not control death or life﴾, meaning: they cannot cause death for anyone. (...) We know that the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord and said: ﴿I give life and cause death﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258] was a liar or truthful? A liar.
﴿They do not control death or life﴾, meaning: they cannot bring death to anyone or bring life to anyone, however much they gather for that.
If someone says: Is it not possible that they could kill someone?
The answer: this is the cause of death, not death itself. A person can do the cause of death, but cannot bring about death itself, and there is a difference between the two. That is why sometimes the cause of death exists and the person does not die, and sometimes a person dies without a cause; that is, without a known cause.
So these do not control death or life for anyone; they cannot give life to any of the dead, because that belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
As for the revival of the dead by Isa, it is not of this category; it is not the matter negated by Allah, because the one who truly gives life to the dead is Allah, and for this reason Allah restricted His giving life to the dead by His saying: ﴿by My permission﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 110]. He does not act independently in this; rather his word was a cause of the life that Allah creates. Is it clear?
﴿Nor life, nor resurrection﴾: resurrection is the raising of the dead and their dispersal. Their scattering means they are dispersed; they come out of their graves and spread through the earth, dispersing in it. So they control none of this at all.
So when their inherent and accidental powerlessness becomes clear, it becomes clear that they are not fit to be gods; there is in them inherent and accidental incapacity.
Now, what is the station or state of ﴿they do not control death or life or resurrection﴾ in relation to His saying: ﴿they create nothing﴾?
Its coordination with His saying ﴿they create nothing﴾ is by way of coordinating the specific with the general, or detail after summary.
You now see the noble verse ascending from the lower to the higher: ﴿harm or benefit﴾, then ﴿death﴾, ﴿life﴾, and ﴿resurrection﴾. This is known, because life is greater than death; that is, the existence of the cause of life, or the power to give life, is greater than death. Likewise harm and benefit: which of them is greater? Benefit; because harm... a person seeks from harm the repelling of a thing, and repelling a thing is easier than bringing it, because bringing is positive and repelling is negative, and generally the negative is easier than the positive. So Allah, glorified and exalted, moved, in explaining the powerlessness of these gods and that they are not fit, from the lower to the higher. This is with regard to detail; as for summary, He said: ﴿they create nothing﴾.
* Among the benefits of this: it indicates that a person should present to his opponent what he must acknowledge, so that the proof is established against him.
Could those who made them gods claim that they create? No.
Could they claim that they are uncreated? No, because they know they exist and did not exist before.
Could they claim that they benefit or harm? We say: they can claim that, and indeed they do claim that; they say the saints benefit and harm, and that whoever does not slaughter for this saint or make a vow to him will be harmed by him. This is a claim.
What are they required to produce if they make such claims? They are required to produce evidence. Yes, the evidence would be that someone says to them, for example: call upon this saint regarding a specific matter and see whether he brings you that or not, just as they demand specific things from the messengers. For example, when the messengers told them that Allah gives life to the dead, they said: ﴿Bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 25], although the messengers did not tell them that resurrection would occur in this world, so that they could say: ﴿Bring our fathers.﴾ Rather they told them: when is the resurrection? After death. This differs from what these opponents demanded of the messengers. Their saying ﴿Bring our fathers﴾ is in reality begging the question; that is, demanding proof for something the messengers, peace be upon them, did not say, since they did not say that they would be raised now.
In any case, this claim that they possess benefit or harm is a claim requiring clear proof.
As for the claim of death and life, it is even more evidently false; indeed it might be claimed, because the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord said to him: ﴿I give life and cause death﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258], so it might be claimed.
And in the debate of Ibrahim, peace be upon him — that is, we may benefit from it here — is evidence that if the falsifier makes a claim, we move him to what is clearer, because the aim is not the argument itself; the aim is to establish the proof against the falsity of the matter. If it is refuted even by one proof, that suffices. There is no need that we refute it using the proof that the opponent specifies; we may refute it by another proof. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, if he had wished to argue with this man and dispute with him, would have said: you do not give life and cause death, you only do the cause of life and death. But he, peace be upon him, went to a clearer and more manifest proof that cannot be contested, to cut off dispute and argument, because a person who argues should be met with a proof he cannot repel. So he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258]. Is that a compelling argument or not? It is a compelling argument, with which he cannot claim anything. That is why Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So the one who disbelieved was confounded, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258].
The main point now: ﴿they create nothing﴾ is agreed upon; could its negation be claimed or not? It cannot. Even among the worshippers: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman 25], and ﴿if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 87]. Even among the worshippers, they cannot claim this negated attribute.
﴿While they themselves are created﴾: they also cannot claim that they are not created, because they are made; they fashioned them with their own hands. Ibrahim says to them: ﴿And Allah created you and what you make﴾ [As-Saffat 96].
﴿They do not control for themselves any harm or benefit﴾: we said that what can be claimed is the opposite of this negation, and our answer to it is in two ways:
Either we refute this very claim, saying: this is impossible, and if you wish, then call upon them.
Or it is said: we move away from this negation during debate — look — we do not move away from this negation out of lack of belief in Allah; we must believe that they do not possess that. But in the course of disputation, to what do we move? To a greater, clearer, and more manifest matter.
For example, if heavy, flooding rains came down or earthquakes occurred, we could say to them: call upon these idols and see whether (...) the sky, and whether the earth stops quaking. And the like. But whatever they claim or do not claim, in debate we move to a clearer matter they cannot deny: ﴿They do not control death or life or resurrection﴾.
When Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned what pertains to monotheism, He moved on to what pertains to prophethood, because (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah). So He said, exalted is He..
* Student: (...)?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 3–9 (part 2 of 5):

* The Shaykh: The difference between them is that nushur (resurrection, scattering) is general, whereas hayah (life) is specific, the life of one particular individual; such as saying to them, "Bring this dead person to life." Nushur is general, and for this reason we said that it derives from al-nashr, in the sense of dispersal and spreading out, so it is more comprehensive.
﴿And they possess no power over death, nor life, nor resurrection﴾. (﴿And those who disbelieved said, "This is not but a lie [ifk] he has fabricated, and other people have helped him at it"﴾; i.e., what the Qur'an is, "not but a lie [ifk]," a falsehood, "he has fabricated," Muhammad, "and other people have helped him at it" [al-Furqan 4], and they are from the People of the Book.)
This is the second of the foundational principles in tawhid, which is affirming the prophethood (al-risalah). Affirming the message is undoubtedly one of the two halves of tawhid: ("I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah").
