Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 32–34 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: (﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ — i.e., "Why not?" — ﴿sent down to him all at once﴾ [al-Furqan 32], like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms.)

﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾: this is among the doubts that the deniers raised against the Messenger (ﷺ). They said: the earlier scriptures were sent down upon the prophets all at once, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and likewise others; they were sent down in one piece, not in parts. So these people said: if Muhammad (ﷺ) were truthful, and he were a prophet among the prophets, his case would be like the case of the earlier prophets, with the Quran sent down to him all at once. They used (lawla), which indicates reproach (tahdid), meaning: it was fitting, or it was necessary, that the Quran be sent down to him all at once, according to their claim, just as it was sent down to the earlier prophets.

Here, ﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾: there is no doubt that they are the Quraysh, because it speaks of a matter that actually occurred; it cannot be that it refers to all the disbelievers, meaning it cannot refer to the disbelievers of the earlier nations. However, it is possible that this statement was inherited from the Quraysh, and whoever says it after them says it as a means of deception and misguidance of people.

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32].

The word ﴿nuzzila﴾ and the word ﴿jumlatan﴾ may give the impression of a contradiction, because it is well known that when it is in the intensive form, ﴿nuzzila﴾, it is for something sent down gradually, and when it is (anzala), it is for something sent down all at once. Here they said: ﴿lawla nuzzila ʿalayhi al-Quran jumlatan﴾ ("why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once"), and according to what we have pointed to, they should have said: "Why was the Quran not sent down (anzala) to him?"

It is said: (anzala) and (nazzala) are interchangeable, just as you say: khabbarani and akhbarani; khabbarani and akhbarani have the same meaning. The idea that (nazzala) is for what is sent down gradually and (anzala) is for what is sent down all at once is not part of the inherent meaning of the word itself, but is something determined by context, indications and circumstances. On this basis there is no difference between them, and the meaning of ﴿nuzzila﴾ here is what? (anzala), but it has taken its place.

It is also possible that ﴿nuzzila ʿalayhi al-Quran jumlatan﴾ was said by them as a report of what was being sent down, and then they proposed that ﴿jumlatan﴾ be applied to ﴿nuzzila﴾ according to the actual reality, because the reality is that the Quran was being sent down upon the Messenger (ﷺ) in installments, being sent down in parts. It is as if they said: "Why was the sending down that is now occurring, piece by piece, not all at once?" So the verb ﴿nuzzila﴾ here remains upon the rule, which is for what is sent down gradually, and by this they intend to say: it is as if they are saying: this sending down, which is the attribute of the revelation sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), why was it not all at once?

So before us now are two answers:

The first answer: (nazzala) and (anzala) are interchangeable, and context and indications determine the meaning.

Second: they are not interchangeable, and each has its own meaning, but they said ﴿nuzzila﴾ with regard to the actual state of affairs, since the revelation was coming down upon the Prophet (ﷺ) gradually. It is as if they said: why was this sending down not all at once?

This doubt may at first appear to be a doubt: why was the revelation sent down to him not like the revelation sent down to those before him? This may appear to be a doubt at first, but in reality it is not a doubt; rather it is a proof. Therefore Allah answered it by saying: (Allah the Exalted said: We sent it down ﴿thus﴾, i.e., in installments, ﴿so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾, i.e., strengthen your heart, ﴿and We have recited it in distinct recitation﴾ [al-Furqan 32], i.e., We brought it piece after piece, with deliberation and gentleness, to facilitate its understanding and its memorization.)

﴿Thus﴾ means: you should pause during recitation at His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32], pausing because the speech of the disbelievers ends there; then you begin, saying: ﴿Thus, so that We may strengthen﴾, because this last part is the speech of Allah, so it must be separated from the speech of the disbelievers, since it is an answer to the doubt.

His saying ﴿thus﴾ is an object of an omitted verb, an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), meaning: We sent it down in the manner of that sending down.

The lam in His saying ﴿li-nuthabbita﴾ ("so that We may strengthen") is for causation (ta'lil), and it is connected to the omitted verb, meaning: We sent it down for the purpose of strengthening.

Tathbit means strengthening and establishment, meaning it is not merely strengthening; for you say: thabata al-shay', meaning: I made it firm, it does not waver or move. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra 74]. So tathbit means strengthening, and what else? And establishment, meaning that He makes it settled and fixed. So the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is strengthened by this sending down, and becomes firm and steady, not shaken.

His saying ﴿li-nuthabbita bihi fu'adak﴾ ("so that We may strengthen your heart by it"): the manner of the strengthening here is in two respects:

First: when it was sent down to him after a period of interruption, his heart became settled and he knew that his messengership continued. Consider the state of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) during the interruption of revelation: what did he do? He would go out to the mountains until he nearly threw himself down from them, because he had lost what he had first sensed. This is strengthening: it strengthens the heart of the Messenger that he is a messenger and that his message has not ceased. This is one aspect.

Another aspect: it strengthens the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) whenever a doubt was raised against him, the Quran descended answering it, and this is without doubt strengthening, is it not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: So the strengthening here is in two respects: his being strengthened that he is a messenger, and another strengthening to repel the doubts raised against him. The first matter we illustrated with an example: what is it? The interruption of revelation.

The second matter we illustrate with this verse: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾; the answer came: ﴿Thus, so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾. And ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes"﴾ up to its end [al-Isra 90–91], and ﴿And they say, "Why were not signs sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut 50–51]. This and much else is part of strengthening the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), because when a person is supplied with what defends him against his opponent, that is among the strongest forms of strengthening.

Here Allah explained the wisdom: it is the strengthening of the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him). In another verse He said: ﴿And a Quran which We have separated, that you may recite it to the people over a long period, and We have sent it down in stages﴾ [al-Isra 106]. So it states another wisdom, which is that the Prophet (ﷺ) recites it to the people over a period, to make it easier to memorize and more receptive to understanding. Have you understood? So what is the wisdom in Allah, glorified and exalted, choosing in this place to say ﴿li-nuthabbita bihi fu'adak﴾ [al-Furqan 32], while there He said ﴿li-taqra'ahu ʿala al-nas ʿala mukth﴾?

The wisdom in this is evident, because here it is an answer to a doubt raised against him, so it was fitting to state the wisdom concerning what pertains to the Prophet (ﷺ); for you know that humans are human, and can be affected by the doubts raised against them, as Allah said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra 74]. Is that understood?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have recited it in distinct recitation﴾ [al-Furqan 32]. The author says: (We brought it piece after piece), and according to this, this is the meaning of sending down: tartil (distinct recitation) means tanzil (sending down). But in my view tartil is more specific; the meaning is: We made it arranged (murattal), meaning: some of it follows some other, and each verse is separate from the next. It is as if these verses are stages for a traveler; when a traveler has stages in his journey, his journey becomes easy for him, and these stages dispel the fatigue of his travel, whereas if he is always on one road it becomes burdensome. That the soul finds rest in the Quran because of these verses and this arrangement is well known; and the division of the Quran into parts is also for this reason, that is, so that a person may finish the Quran stage by stage, which makes it easier for him and strengthens him in his recitation. Likewise, dividing it into surahs, each surah independent of the other, is also among the causes of invigorating the reader and sustaining him in his recitation.

So the arrangement of the Quran into verses and surahs is something that benefits the reader and gives him energy and strength for the Quran, in memorization and in understanding.

Also among the benefits of tartil is the practical aspect: that action comes to people gradually. Consider what would happen if the Noble Quran had been sent down to people all at once with all its rulings. Would people be able to absorb these rulings and carry them out or not? That is impossible; it is very difficult, and it is not the way of upbringing or cultivation. Rather, by the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted, as is His way in everything, both in the matters of destiny and in the matters of the Shariah, He brings them into being gradually, even physical matters grow gradually. How long does the fetus remain in its mother's womb? It remains for a period: in the case of the children of Adam, nine months, and for other animals according to their kind. The point is that there must be gradual development.

Does night and day come all at once?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: Gradually. Likewise the laws also come to people gradually, especially to this Ummah. Although the earlier nations were sent down all at once, and this was among the burdens and shackles upon them, that their law was sent down all at once and they were obligated to it at once. But this Ummah, by the mercy of Allah toward it, the Quran was distinctly recited so that He would bring them up in Islam and in the Shariah of Allah gradually.

* Student: Alright, what is the point of the argument here? What do they want (...) the Prophet (ﷺ) if Muhammad says that the Quran was not sent down all at once, what is the defect?

* Shaykh: No, the defect is that he is not a messenger, because if he were a messenger he would be like others, the Quran would be sent down to him all at once, just as it was sent down to those who preceded him all at once.

* Student: That is it?

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, that is it. It is in reality a doubt, not a proof; it is a doubt they wish to use for deception. Otherwise, this is by no means something that prevents the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in that he brings the revelation gradually. But they say this, in addition to what preceded in Surah al-Nahl, where they said: ﴿Only a human teaches him﴾ [al-Nahl 103]. So in their view, if you add this to what came before, it is as if they are saying: he is taught the Quran by instruction, and otherwise it would have been sent down to him all at once like the other prophets.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: Is it an acknowledgment that the Quran is sent down from Allah, glorified and exalted?

* Shaykh: No, they did not acknowledge it.

* Student: They say: ﴿Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan 32]?

* Shaykh: Yes, according to their claim.

* Student: According to their claim.

* Shaykh: Yes, since they say: it is sent down from Allah. Fine, (...) it was sent down to you from Allah all at once, if you are truthful.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Which of them?

* Student: That sometimes they claim he is taught by a human, and sometimes they claim it is sent down to him from heaven (...)?

* Shaykh: Not at all (...), this is Abdullah's question.

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: It is not an acknowledgment from them of the sending down, but they say: this one who says the Quran was sent down to him from Allah (...) was sent down to him all at once. Yes indeed, they do not acknowledge this.

* Student: They acknowledge for example (...).

* Shaykh: No, there is no contradiction; that this is the speech of a sorcerer who bewitches people.

Allah said: (﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ — to undermine your matter — ﴿except that We bring you the truth﴾ that repels it ﴿and better explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33] — clarification.)

This is from the strengthening of the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him).

﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ [al-Furqan 33]: the meaning of "example" (mathal) here is attribute, as Allah said: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Mathal, as you know, is applied to resemblance: ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 17]; it is applied to a great and wondrous attribute: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers﴾ [Muhammad 15]; and it is applied to the proverb known among writers, which is the saying that circulates and is intended to liken a present situation to something past or something similar.

The meaning of "example" here is attribute: that is, they do not bring you any attribute of speech, intending by it to nullify your call, except that We bring you the truth. So, do they bring falsehood or truth? Falsehood; because He set their speech against the truth. This is also evidence that every doubt by which the deniers of the Messenger (ﷺ) argue is falsehood, but this falsehood is falsehood in itself; it may become evident to some people that it is false, and it may be hidden from some people that it is false. This is among the trials, the trial of doubt. That is, not everything that is false is known to everyone, is it not? For this reason you, though you are one person, sometimes find the matter clear to you in some situations and confusing to you in other situations, according to whether your heart is clear and at peace or otherwise. Hence judging while angry was forbidden, and (...) while angry, and in situations of disturbing heat, painful cold and the like; because a person in these circumstances is hindered by these matters from knowing the truth or willing the truth, for in anger the truth becomes confused for you, or perhaps you do not want the truth; you want to carry out your anger against the one you are angry with, for example.

So the summary, O people, is: every doubt that the disbelievers raise in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and after it is falsehood, and no one came with falsehood in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) except that Allah brought the truth.

His saying ﴿and better explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33]: the author says regarding ﴿tafsir﴾: (bayan, clarification). ﴿And better explanation﴾, i.e., clarification.

How is it ﴿and better explanation﴾?! Their speech now, since it is falsehood, does it contain any clarification?

The answer: Yes, because they bring speech that is fine in its eloquence, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there is magic in eloquence" [narrated by al-Bukhari (5767) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. But their eloquence, their rhetoric, and their verbal sorcery, Allah, exalted is He, brings something better than it.

And here, is "better" (ahsan) in its ordinary sense, or is it in the sense of matching the opponent?

* Student: In the sense of matching the opponent.

* Student: In its ordinary sense.

* Shaykh: In its ordinary sense; because they have clarification and explanation of matters and the presentation of doubts, and they are at the utmost of eloquence. For this reason Allah did not challenge anyone in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) with the like of what He challenged them with through the Quran.

So "better" here is in its ordinary sense: they bring very fine and clear speech, but We bring you what is better, clearer and more evident. In this there is from Allah's defense of His Messenger (ﷺ) what there is.

﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces into Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34]. The commentator says: (They are ﴿those who will be gathered﴾ [al-Furqan 34]), making ﴿alladhina﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: ("And better explanation" [al-Furqan 33] — clarification)?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: No, (they are ﴿alladhina﴾ [al-Furqan 34]).

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes?

* Student: (...) (the clarification: they are ﴿alladhina﴾).

* Shaykh: Yes, no, in my view it is: (they are ﴿alladhina yuhsharun﴾).

* Student: Should I erase the lam?

* Shaykh: Yes, erase the lam.

Alright. (﴿Those who will be gathered onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34]) means these people who denied you and opposed what you brought. (﴿Those who will be gathered onto their faces﴾), that is, they will be driven (﴿to Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34]). If the author had said that ﴿yuhsharun﴾ means "they will be assembled," since *al-hashr* means gathering, that is, they will be raised, may Allah protect us, on the Day of Resurrection ﴿onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34], that would also be fine.

But since it is followed by ﴿to Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34], it seems to have taken on the meaning of driving, so it means "they will be driven." There is nothing wrong, however, in saying "they will be gathered and driven," because when a verb is given the meaning of another verb, this does not remove its own indicated meaning. Rather, another meaning is added to it. For example, ﴿from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan 6]: we said that ﴿yashrabu﴾ ("drink") is given the meaning of *yarwa* ("quench one's thirst"), so they drink from it and are quenched. That does not mean the meaning of drinking is removed, since there is no quenching except after drinking. Is that clear? Likewise, there is no driving to Hell except after the gathering, which is the assembling.

As for his saying (﴿those who﴾ [al-Furqan 34]): according to the author's view, *alladhina* ("those who") is the predicate of an omitted subject, and ﴿they are worse in position﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*jumla haliyya*), or it is a subject and predicate beginning a new sentence. It is also possible that ﴿alladhina﴾ is the subject, and the clause ﴿they are worse in position﴾ is the predicate, so it would be the type of subject described by a clause.

As for his saying: ﴿they will be gathered onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34], how can they walk on their faces?

We say, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The One who made him walk on his feet in this world is able to make him walk on his face in the Hereafter" [Reported by al-Bukhari (4760), Muslim (2806/54) and Ahmad, and the wording is his (13392), from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him]. Is that not so? It is not far-fetched. And if the arrogant are gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of ants, trampled by people's feet [On the authority of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Allah will resurrect people on the Day of Resurrection in the form of ants, and people will trample them with their feet. It will be said: 'What are these in the form of ants?' It will be said: 'These are the arrogant ones of the world.'" Mentioned by al-Haythami in *al-Majma'* (10/334), who said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar."], then Allah is powerful over all things. A man who in this world may be one of the largest of people in body, and yet is arrogant, will on the Day of Resurrection be gathered in the likeness of ants, and Allah the Exalted is powerful over all things. This is an example of what was mentioned earlier, that the conditions of the Hereafter cannot be measured by the conditions of this world.

Alright. If it is asked: what is the wisdom in gathering them on their faces as a punishment?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, how?
* Student: Because their likeness is usually (...), so it was fitting that they be gathered on their faces.
* Shaykh: Alright, second.
* Student: It is a humiliation for them (...).
* Shaykh: It is a humiliation for them, because the face is the most honored of the limbs, so when it is made the place of treading, this is humiliation. Alright, but what is the wisdom behind this? There is no doubt that there is humiliation and punishment in it?
* Student: Because they were arrogant toward the truth (...), a person's face (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, like the words of Sulayman. Alright, and others?
* Student: Because they reversed the realities.
* Shaykh: Yes, they reversed them.
* Student: They reversed them.
* Shaykh: Alright, all of these, I mean, are possible reasons. I have yet another possibility.
* Student: Because (...).
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is what ʿAbdullah said: since they used to speak with their tongues while those (tongues) were in their faces, the punishment fell upon them.

Alright. Also, a person turns toward a thing with his face and turns away from it with his face. Since the face is the place of turning toward and turning away, and they have turned away, the punishment came upon them. All these meanings are appropriate, and Allah knows best what He intends, and all of these may be intended.

* Student: Although the face is (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not the highest in any case. No, there are places more sensitive than the face.

In any case, these meanings you mentioned may all be among the reasons they are gathered on their faces.

(﴿They are worse in position, the place being Hell, and most astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan 34], that is, they went further astray from the right path than others, and that is their disbelief.)

﴿Worse in position﴾, meaning in rank, and that is Hell. Worse than whom? Than everyone, because the one being compared to was not mentioned, and not mentioning the one being compared to implies generality. That is, ﴿worse in position﴾ than all places and than everyone.

﴿Most astray in way﴾, meaning further from what is right. Than whom?

* Student: Than everyone.
* Shaykh: Than everyone.

So these are ﴿those who will be gathered onto their faces to Hell﴾, may Allah protect us, and they are the worst of people in rank and the most astray of people in path.

As for his saying ﴿to Hell﴾: this Jahannam is one of the names of the Fire. Its origin is from *al-juhma* (dark, gloomy depth), and the *nun* in it is extra. On this basis its pattern is *fa'annal*, since the *nun* is extra.

It was named this because it is deep in its bottom and black in color, black in color and deep in its bottom. This is *al-juhma* and darkness. We seek refuge in Allah from it.

﴿They are worse in position and most astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan 34].

Alright, the following lessons may be drawn from this noble verse:

* First: the eagerness of the disbelievers to nullify what the Messenger ﷺ brought and to raise doubts against it, from His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32]. Indeed, this is not a proof but a doubt.
* Also in it is evidence of Allah's care for His Messenger ﷺ.
* Student: His refuting these people.
* Shaykh: By what? His refuting these people.
* And in it is evidence for affirming wisdom in Allah's actions?
* Student: ﴿So that We may strengthen﴾ [al-Furqan 32].
* Shaykh: ﴿So that We may strengthen﴾, because the *lam* is for causation (*ta'lil*), and causation is wisdom. So there is a refutation in it against a group of the innovating sects. Which group is this?
* Student: The Ash'aris.
* Shaykh: No, I do not know about the Ash'aris, but what I do know about...
* Student: They denied (...).
* Student: The Jahmiyyah.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. But the origin of this view is with the Jahmiyyah Mujbira (the Determinist Jahmiyyah). They hold that the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, are not caused by purpose, and that He, glorified and exalted, creates and legislates, creating creatures or creation and legislating laws, merely by will and not for any wisdom. They cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23]. But how could they derive that from this verse?!

So these verses show the wisdom behind sending down the Qur'an in stages, and that Allah's actions are purposeful and accompanied by wisdom.

Alright, is this wisdom in the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted, whether legislative or non-legislative, known or unknown?

Some of it is known and some is unknown to us, but it is known to Allah.

In this is evidence that among the wisdoms in sending down the Qur'an is strengthening the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, whether that strengthening is in establishing the message. What else?

* Student: (...) in refuting doubts.
* Shaykh: Yes, or strengthening in refuting the doubts presented to him.
* In the verse there is evidence that for every falsehood there is a response to that falsehood in the Qur'an. Or, if you wish, say something more general: we find the clarification of its falsehood in the revelation sent down to Muhammad ﷺ. From where do we take this?
﴿And they do not bring you any example but that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33]. No doubt that has been raised up to our day that is not refuted, and in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ is what refutes it. But as you know, not everyone perceives that. Is that not right? Yes, not everyone perceives it. A sword in the hand of a person who does not use it is worth nothing and benefits him no more than a stick or less, but in the hand of someone who wields it, it is a sharp sword with which he strikes and kills. Likewise, the revelation sent down to the Messenger ﷺ is not known to everyone, and not everyone can establish the proof from it, but ﴿the bounty of Allah He gives to whom He wills﴾.

For this reason, "'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrust you with anything? He said: No, by the One who split the seed and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah gives a person regarding the Qur'an, and what is in this sheet: the blood-money (for the killed), the freeing of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever" [Reported by al-Bukhari (3047) from Abu Juhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do you have anything of revelation besides what is in the Book of Allah?" He said: "No, by the One who split the seed and created the soul, I know of nothing except an understanding that Allah gives a man concerning the Qur'an, and what is in this sheet." I said: "And what is in the sheet?" He said: "The blood-money, the freeing of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever."].

The conclusion is that Allah, glorified and exalted, gives His bounty to whom He wills regarding the understanding of the Qur'an. How many a verse passes by a person from which he derives several issues, while another cannot (...). Yes. Indeed, Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, hosted Imam Ahmad one night. He brought him supper, and Imam Ahmad ate the whole supper, all of what was brought, then slept, lay down on his bed, and did not get up for the night prayer. Then he got up at dawn and did not ask for wudu'! One of Imam Ahmad's daughters said to her father: "This is al-Shafi'i, about whom you used to say such-and-such. We have not seen him do anything, and we have also not seen him limit himself to a third of his food!" He said: "I will bring you the news." He first asked al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him: "Why did you eat all the food?" He answered: "I do not see anyone in this city whose food is more lawful than Imam Ahmad's, so I wanted my belly to be filled with this lawful food." That is one answer. So he had a purpose. And is satiety at times permissible or not?

* Student: Permissible.
* Shaykh: Permissible. "Abu Hurayrah drank milk, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Drink,' and he said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I cannot find a passage for it'" [Reported by al-Bukhari (6452) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "I cannot find a path for it."]. But we, we talk to ourselves about this hadith at every meal. Every meal we say what Abu Hurayrah said! That is a passing thought, and passing thoughts are many.

And he asked him: "Why did you not stand in the night prayer?" He said: "I was reflecting on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Abu 'Umayr, what did the little bird do?' [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6129) and Muslim (2150/30), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.] And I derived a thousand benefits from the hadith." As for my praying without wudu' for the dawn prayer, I did not sleep; I was reflecting on this hadith.

The conclusion is that people differ in understanding the Book and the Sunnah and in deriving rulings from them. For this reason you find some people who recite a verse to you and set out its benefits, perhaps five or ten benefits, according to what is in the verse, while another derives fifty instead of five, and the bounty of Allah He gives to whom He wills. (...)

Yes indeed, but I do not think he took it from the wording of the hadith alone; Allah knows best. Whenever he saw a benefit, he brought another hadith that indicates it and then derived from it. (...)

﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan 32].

* Student: (...) says: Why was the Qur'an sent down to him all at once?
* Shaykh: How is the doubt raised?
* Student: Because the earlier nations were...
* Shaykh: The messengers.
* Student: The earlier messengers used to have their books sent down to them without (...).
* Shaykh: Well done. ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾

Alright, this expression ﴿was sent down﴾ (*nuzzila*), although it is well known that *nuzzila* is used when something is sent down gradually, here He said it was sent down all at once. How can ﴿nuzzila﴾ and ﴿all at once﴾ be reconciled?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It comes with the meaning of *anzala* ("to send down").
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: That is, *nazzala* and *anzala* have the same meaning. Like, a similar example among verbs is that the doubled form can have the meaning of the hamzated form. Who has an example?
* Student: (*ihmarra*) and (*ihtamara*).
* Shaykh: No, subhan Allah, you brought half the answer. Who has an example?
* Student: (*akhbara*).
* Shaykh: (*akhbara*) and (*khabbara*).

Alright, fine, this is one way. What is the second way?

* Student: The second way is that (...), that is, this sending down, if it were sent down, would be all at once.
* Shaykh: You mean in terms of consideration?
* Student: In terms of consideration (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, in terms of the actual reality? In terms of reality, and "all at once" in terms of what was demanded.

Alright. Did Allah answer this doubt?

* Student: Yes.
* Shaykh: Yes, with what?
* Student: With His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that We may strengthen﴾ [al-Furqan 32].
* Shaykh: Allah answered that He sent it down this way so as to strengthen the heart of the Prophet ﷺ. Good.

Strengthening the heart through what?

* Student: Through what is sent down to him (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, but how? Or what is its manner?
* Student: In one of two ways.
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Either (...) that is returned upon him (...) .
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: And the second matter (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, strengthening the heart comes in two ways. First?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The second (...).
* Shaykh: Reassuring the Messenger ﷺ that the message will continue, just as when the revelation paused he was extremely grieved and went out to the mountains awaiting this revelation.

In this verse Allah clarified that the wisdom in sending it down in stages is strengthening, and in another verse He mentioned another benefit. We say: Allah mentioned that the benefit of sending it down in stages is strengthening. In another verse He mentioned another benefit?

* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes (...).
* Student: Because this is in response to their question about the reason it was sent down.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Or opposing the Qur'an on the grounds that it was sent down in stages.
* Shaykh: In response to raising a doubt about the Prophet ﷺ that might affect him. Yes, so this clarification of wisdom came for strengthening.
* Student: That the meaning is ﴿We have separated it﴾ [al-Isra' 106] (...); this is the cause.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed.

In these noble verses we noted that there is a refutation in them of a group of the people of innovation who deny one of the greatest attributes of Allah. What is it that they deny of Allah's attributes?

* Student: The face.
* Shaykh: They deny what?
* Student: Affirming wisdom for Allah, the Exalted (...).
* Shaykh: They deny wisdom, and in the verse there is a refutation of them. By what?
* Student: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾ [al-Furqan 32].
* Shaykh: No, I want you to show me the word in which the refutation lies. Not the whole verse.
* Student: ﴿Thus﴾.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: The *lam* in ﴿li-nuthabbita﴾.
* Shaykh: The *lam* is for causation: ﴿so that We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾, and causation means wisdom.

Alright, Allah, glorified and exalted, clarified that for those who deny the Messenger ﷺ, whatever doubt they raise, however clearly it is put, Allah answers it with something stronger and greater.

* Student: (...) that from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they do not bring you any example but that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33].
* Shaykh: What is meant by ﴿example﴾ (*mathal*)?
* Student: ﴿Example﴾, that is, in the form of the doubts (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, with a kind of speech by which they intend to nullify what you brought. ﴿But We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾ Yes indeed.

From what preceded, what indicates the affirmation of resurrection?

* Student: ﴿Those who will be gathered onto their faces﴾.
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿those who will be gathered onto their faces to Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 32–34 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: (﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ — i.e., "Why not?" — ﴿sent down to him all at once﴾ [al-Furqan 32], like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms.)

﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾: this is among the doubts that the deniers raised against the Messenger (ﷺ). They said: the earlier scriptures were sent down upon the prophets all at once, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and likewise others; they were sent down in one piece, not in parts. So these people said: if Muhammad (ﷺ) were truthful, and he were a prophet among the prophets, his case would be like the case of the earlier prophets, with the Quran sent down to him all at once. They used (lawla), which indicates reproach (tahdid), meaning: it was fitting, or it was necessary, that the Quran be sent down to him all at once, according to their claim, just as it was sent down to the earlier prophets.

Here, ﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾: there is no doubt that they are the Quraysh, because it speaks of a matter that actually occurred; it cannot be that it refers to all the disbelievers, meaning it cannot refer to the disbelievers of the earlier nations. However, it is possible that this statement was inherited from the Quraysh, and whoever says it after them says it as a means of deception and misguidance of people.

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32].

The word ﴿nuzzila﴾ and the word ﴿jumlatan﴾ may give the impression of a contradiction, because it is well known that when it is in the intensive form, ﴿nuzzila﴾, it is for something sent down gradually, and when it is (anzala), it is for something sent down all at once. Here they said: ﴿lawla nuzzila ʿalayhi al-Quran jumlatan﴾ ("why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once"), and according to what we have pointed to, they should have said: "Why was the Quran not sent down (anzala) to him?"

It is said: (anzala) and (nazzala) are interchangeable, just as you say: khabbarani and akhbarani; khabbarani and akhbarani have the same meaning. The idea that (nazzala) is for what is sent down gradually and (anzala) is for what is sent down all at once is not part of the inherent meaning of the word itself, but is something determined by context, indications and circumstances. On this basis there is no difference between them, and the meaning of ﴿nuzzila﴾ here is what? (anzala), but it has taken its place.

It is also possible that ﴿nuzzila ʿalayhi al-Quran jumlatan﴾ was said by them as a report of what was being sent down, and then they proposed that ﴿jumlatan﴾ be applied to ﴿nuzzila﴾ according to the actual reality, because the reality is that the Quran was being sent down upon the Messenger (ﷺ) in installments, being sent down in parts. It is as if they said: "Why was the sending down that is now occurring, piece by piece, not all at once?" So the verb ﴿nuzzila﴾ here remains upon the rule, which is for what is sent down gradually, and by this they intend to say: it is as if they are saying: this sending down, which is the attribute of the revelation sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), why was it not all at once?

So before us now are two answers:

The first answer: (nazzala) and (anzala) are interchangeable, and context and indications determine the meaning.

Second: they are not interchangeable, and each has its own meaning, but they said ﴿nuzzila﴾ with regard to the actual state of affairs, since the revelation was coming down upon the Prophet (ﷺ) gradually. It is as if they said: why was this sending down not all at once?

This doubt may at first appear to be a doubt: why was the revelation sent down to him not like the revelation sent down to those before him? This may appear to be a doubt at first, but in reality it is not a doubt; rather it is a proof. Therefore Allah answered it by saying: (Allah the Exalted said: We sent it down ﴿thus﴾, i.e., in installments, ﴿so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾, i.e., strengthen your heart, ﴿and We have recited it in distinct recitation﴾ [al-Furqan 32], i.e., We brought it piece after piece, with deliberation and gentleness, to facilitate its understanding and its memorization.)

﴿Thus﴾ means: you should pause during recitation at His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32], pausing because the speech of the disbelievers ends there; then you begin, saying: ﴿Thus, so that We may strengthen﴾, because this last part is the speech of Allah, so it must be separated from the speech of the disbelievers, since it is an answer to the doubt.

His saying ﴿thus﴾ is an object of an omitted verb, an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), meaning: We sent it down in the manner of that sending down.

The lam in His saying ﴿li-nuthabbita﴾ ("so that We may strengthen") is for causation (ta'lil), and it is connected to the omitted verb, meaning: We sent it down for the purpose of strengthening.

Tathbit means strengthening and establishment, meaning it is not merely strengthening; for you say: thabata al-shay', meaning: I made it firm, it does not waver or move. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra 74]. So tathbit means strengthening, and what else? And establishment, meaning that He makes it settled and fixed. So the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is strengthened by this sending down, and becomes firm and steady, not shaken.

His saying ﴿li-nuthabbita bihi fu'adak﴾ ("so that We may strengthen your heart by it"): the manner of the strengthening here is in two respects:

First: when it was sent down to him after a period of interruption, his heart became settled and he knew that his messengership continued. Consider the state of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) during the interruption of revelation: what did he do? He would go out to the mountains until he nearly threw himself down from them, because he had lost what he had first sensed. This is strengthening: it strengthens the heart of the Messenger that he is a messenger and that his message has not ceased. This is one aspect.

Another aspect: it strengthens the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) whenever a doubt was raised against him, the Quran descended answering it, and this is without doubt strengthening, is it not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: So the strengthening here is in two respects: his being strengthened that he is a messenger, and another strengthening to repel the doubts raised against him. The first matter we illustrated with an example: what is it? The interruption of revelation.

The second matter we illustrate with this verse: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?"﴾; the answer came: ﴿Thus, so that We may strengthen your heart by it﴾. And ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes"﴾ up to its end [al-Isra 90–91], and ﴿And they say, "Why were not signs sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut 50–51]. This and much else is part of strengthening the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), because when a person is supplied with what defends him against his opponent, that is among the strongest forms of strengthening.

Here Allah explained the wisdom: it is the strengthening of the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him). In another verse He said: ﴿And a Quran which We have separated, that you may recite it to the people over a long period, and We have sent it down in stages﴾ [al-Isra 106]. So it states another wisdom, which is that the Prophet (ﷺ) recites it to the people over a period, to make it easier to memorize and more receptive to understanding. Have you understood? So what is the wisdom in Allah, glorified and exalted, choosing in this place to say ﴿li-nuthabbita bihi fu'adak﴾ [al-Furqan 32], while there He said ﴿li-taqra'ahu ʿala al-nas ʿala mukth﴾?

The wisdom in this is evident, because here it is an answer to a doubt raised against him, so it was fitting to state the wisdom concerning what pertains to the Prophet (ﷺ); for you know that humans are human, and can be affected by the doubts raised against them, as Allah said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra 74]. Is that understood?

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have recited it in distinct recitation﴾ [al-Furqan 32]. The author says: (We brought it piece after piece), and according to this, this is the meaning of sending down: tartil (distinct recitation) means tanzil (sending down). But in my view tartil is more specific; the meaning is: We made it arranged (murattal), meaning: some of it follows some other, and each verse is separate from the next. It is as if these verses are stages for a traveler; when a traveler has stages in his journey, his journey becomes easy for him, and these stages dispel the fatigue of his travel, whereas if he is always on one road it becomes burdensome. That the soul finds rest in the Quran because of these verses and this arrangement is well known; and the division of the Quran into parts is also for this reason, that is, so that a person may finish the Quran stage by stage, which makes it easier for him and strengthens him in his recitation. Likewise, dividing it into surahs, each surah independent of the other, is also among the causes of invigorating the reader and sustaining him in his recitation.

So the arrangement of the Quran into verses and surahs is something that benefits the reader and gives him energy and strength for the Quran, in memorization and in understanding.

Also among the benefits of tartil is the practical aspect: that action comes to people gradually. Consider what would happen if the Noble Quran had been sent down to people all at once with all its rulings. Would people be able to absorb these rulings and carry them out or not? That is impossible; it is very difficult, and it is not the way of upbringing or cultivation. Rather, by the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted, as is His way in everything, both in the matters of destiny and in the matters of the Shariah, He brings them into being gradually, even physical matters grow gradually. How long does the fetus remain in its mother's womb? It remains for a period: in the case of the children of Adam, nine months, and for other animals according to their kind. The point is that there must be gradual development.

Does night and day come all at once?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: Gradually. Likewise the laws also come to people gradually, especially to this Ummah. Although the earlier nations were sent down all at once, and this was among the burdens and shackles upon them, that their law was sent down all at once and they were obligated to it at once. But this Ummah, by the mercy of Allah toward it, the Quran was distinctly recited so that He would bring them up in Islam and in the Shariah of Allah gradually.

* Student: Alright, what is the point of the argument here? What do they want (...) the Prophet (ﷺ) if Muhammad says that the Quran was not sent down all at once, what is the defect?

* Shaykh: No, the defect is that he is not a messenger, because if he were a messenger he would be like others, the Quran would be sent down to him all at once, just as it was sent down to those who preceded him all at once.

* Student: That is it?

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, that is it. It is in reality a doubt, not a proof; it is a doubt they wish to use for deception. Otherwise, this is by no means something that prevents the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in that he brings the revelation gradually. But they say this, in addition to what preceded in Surah al-Nahl, where they said: ﴿Only a human teaches him﴾ [al-Nahl 103]. So in their view, if you add this to what came before, it is as if they are saying: he is taught the Quran by instruction, and otherwise it would have been sent down to him all at once like the other prophets.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: What?

* Student: Is it an acknowledgment that the Quran is sent down from Allah, glorified and exalted?

* Shaykh: No, they did not acknowledge it.

* Student: They say: ﴿Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan 32]?

* Shaykh: Yes, according to their claim.

* Student: According to their claim.

* Shaykh: Yes, since they say: it is sent down from Allah. Fine, (...) it was sent down to you from Allah all at once, if you are truthful.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Which of them?

* Student: That sometimes they claim he is taught by a human, and sometimes they claim it is sent down to him from heaven (...)?

* Shaykh: Not at all (...), this is Abdullah's question.

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: It is not an acknowledgment from them of the sending down, but they say: this one who says the Quran was sent down to him from Allah (...) was sent down to him all at once. Yes indeed, they do not acknowledge this.

* Student: They acknowledge for example (...).

* Shaykh: No, there is no contradiction; that this is the speech of a sorcerer who bewitches people.

Allah said: (﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ — to undermine your matter — ﴿except that We bring you the truth﴾ that repels it ﴿and better explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33] — clarification.)

This is from the strengthening of the heart of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him).

﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ [al-Furqan 33]: the meaning of "example" (mathal) here is attribute, as Allah said: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Mathal, as you know, is applied to resemblance: ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 17]; it is applied to a great and wondrous attribute: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers﴾ [Muhammad 15]; and it is applied to the proverb known among writers, which is the saying that circulates and is intended to liken a present situation to something past or something similar.

The meaning of "example" here is attribute: that is, they do not bring you any attribute of speech, intending by it to nullify your call, except that We bring you the truth. So, do they bring falsehood or truth? Falsehood; because He set their speech against the truth. This is also evidence that every doubt by which the deniers of the Messenger (ﷺ) argue is falsehood, but this falsehood is falsehood in itself; it may become evident to some people that it is false, and it may be hidden from some people that it is false. This is among the trials, the trial of doubt. That is, not everything that is false is known to everyone, is it not? For this reason you, though you are one person, sometimes find the matter clear to you in some situations and confusing to you in other situations, according to whether your heart is clear and at peace or otherwise. Hence judging while angry was forbidden, and (...) while angry, and in situations of disturbing heat, painful cold and the like; because a person in these circumstances is hindered by these matters from knowing the truth or willing the truth, for in anger the truth becomes confused for you, or perhaps you do not want the truth; you want to carry out your anger against the one you are angry with, for example.

So the summary, O people, is: every doubt that the disbelievers raise in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and after it is falsehood, and no one came with falsehood in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) except that Allah brought the truth.

His saying ﴿and better explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33]: the author says regarding ﴿tafsir﴾: (bayan, clarification). ﴿And better explanation﴾, i.e., clarification.

How is it ﴿and better explanation﴾?! Their speech now, since it is falsehood, does it contain any clarification?

The answer: Yes, because they bring speech that is fine in its eloquence, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there is magic in eloquence" [narrated by al-Bukhari (5767) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. But their eloquence, their rhetoric, and their verbal sorcery, Allah, exalted is He, brings something better than it.

And here, is "better" (ahsan) in its ordinary sense, or is it in the sense of matching the opponent?

* Student: In the sense of matching the opponent.

* Student: In its ordinary sense.

* Shaykh: In its ordinary sense; because they have clarification and explanation of matters and the presentation of doubts, and they are at the utmost of eloquence. For this reason Allah did not challenge anyone in the time of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) with the like of what He challenged them with through the Quran.

So "better" here is in its ordinary sense: they bring very fine and clear speech, but We bring you what is better, clearer and more evident. In this there is from Allah's defense of His Messenger (ﷺ) what there is.

﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces into Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34]. The commentator says: (They are ﴿those who will be gathered﴾ [al-Furqan 34]), making ﴿alladhina﴾ the predicate of an omitted subject.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: ("And better explanation" [al-Furqan 33] — clarification)?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: No, (they are ﴿alladhina﴾ [al-Furqan 34]).

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes?

* Student: (...) (the clarification: they are ﴿alladhina﴾).

* Shaykh: Yes, no, in my view it is: (they are ﴿alladhina yuhsharun﴾).

* Student: Should I erase the lam?

* Shaykh: Yes, erase the lam.

Alright. (﴿Those who will be gathered onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34]) means these people who denied you and opposed what you brought. (﴿Those who will be gathered onto their faces﴾), that is, they will be driven (﴿to Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34]). If the author had said that ﴿yuhsharun﴾ means "they will be assembled," since *al-hashr* means gathering, that is, they will be raised, may Allah protect us, on the Day of Resurrection ﴿onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34], that would also be fine.

But since it is followed by ﴿to Hell﴾ [al-Furqan 34], it seems to have taken on the meaning of driving, so it means "they will be driven." There is nothing wrong, however, in saying "they will be gathered and driven," because when a verb is given the meaning of another verb, this does not remove its own indicated meaning. Rather, another meaning is added to it. For example, ﴿from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [al-Insan 6]: we said that ﴿yashrabu﴾ ("drink") is given the meaning of *yarwa* ("quench one's thirst"), so they drink from it and are quenched. That does not mean the meaning of drinking is removed, since there is no quenching except after drinking. Is that clear? Likewise, there is no driving to Hell except after the gathering, which is the assembling.

As for his saying (﴿those who﴾ [al-Furqan 34]): according to the author's view, *alladhina* ("those who") is the predicate of an omitted subject, and ﴿they are worse in position﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*jumla haliyya*), or it is a subject and predicate beginning a new sentence. It is also possible that ﴿alladhina﴾ is the subject, and the clause ﴿they are worse in position﴾ is the predicate, so it would be the type of subject described by a clause.

As for his saying: ﴿they will be gathered onto their faces﴾ [al-Furqan 34], how can they walk on their faces?

We say, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The One who made him walk on his feet in this world is able to make him walk on his face in the Hereafter" [Reported by al-Bukhari (4760), Muslim (2806/54) and Ahmad, and the wording is his (13392), from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him]. Is that not so? It is not far-fetched. And if the arrogant are gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the likeness of ants, trampled by people's feet [On the authority of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Allah will resurrect people on the Day of Resurrection in the form of ants, and people will trample them with their feet. It will be said: 'What are these in the form of ants?' It will be said: 'These are the arrogant ones of the world.'" Mentioned by al-Haythami in *al-Majma'* (10/334), who said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar."], then Allah is powerful over all things. A man who in this world may be one of the largest of people in body, and yet is arrogant, will on the Day of Resurrection be gathered in the likeness of ants, and Allah the Exalted is powerful over all things. This is an example of what was mentioned earlier, that the conditions of the Hereafter cannot be measured by the conditions of this world.

Alright. If it is asked: what is the wisdom in gathering them on their faces as a punishment?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, how?
* Student: Because their likeness is usually (...), so it was fitting that they be gathered on their faces.
* Shaykh: Alright, second.
* Student: It is a humiliation for them (...).
* Shaykh: It is a humiliation for them, because the face is the most honored of the limbs, so when it is made the place of treading, this is humiliation. Alright, but what is the wisdom behind this? There is no doubt that there is humiliation and punishment in it?
* Student: Because they were arrogant toward the truth (...), a person's face (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, like the words of Sulayman. Alright, and others?
* Student: Because they reversed the realities.
* Shaykh: Yes, they reversed them.
* Student: They reversed them.
* Shaykh: Alright, all of these, I mean, are possible reasons. I have yet another possibility.
* Student: Because (...).
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is what ʿAbdullah said: since they used to speak with their tongues while those (tongues) were in their faces, the punishment fell upon them.

Alright. Also, a person turns toward a thing with his face and turns away from it with his face. Since the face is the place of turning toward and turning away, and they have turned away, the punishment came upon them. All these meanings are appropriate, and Allah knows best what He intends, and all of these may be intended.

* Student: Although the face is (...).
* Shaykh: No, it is not the highest in any case. No, there are places more sensitive than the face.

In any case, these meanings you mentioned may all be among the reasons they are gathered on their faces.

(﴿They are worse in position, the place being Hell, and most astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan 34], that is, they went further astray from the right path than others, and that is their disbelief.)

﴿Worse in position﴾, meaning in rank, and that is Hell. Worse than whom? Than everyone, because the one being compared to was not mentioned, and not mentioning the one being compared to implies generality. That is, ﴿worse in position﴾ than all places and than everyone.

﴿Most astray in way﴾, meaning further from what is right. Than whom?

* Student: Than everyone.
* Shaykh: Than everyone.

So these are ﴿those who will be gathered onto their faces to Hell﴾, may Allah protect us, and they are the worst of people in rank and the most astray of people in path.

As for his saying ﴿to Hell﴾: this Jahannam is one of the names of the Fire. Its origin is from *al-juhma* (dark, gloomy depth), and the *nun* in it is extra. On this basis its pattern is *fa'annal*, since the *nun* is extra.

It was named this because it is deep in its bottom and black in color, black in color and deep in its bottom. This is *al-juhma* and darkness. We seek refuge in Allah from it.

﴿They are worse in position and most astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan 34].

Alright, the following lessons may be drawn from this noble verse:

* First: the eagerness of the disbelievers to nullify what the Messenger ﷺ brought and to raise doubts against it, from His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan 32]. Indeed, this is not a proof but a doubt.
* Also in it is evidence of Allah's care for His Messenger ﷺ.
* Student: His refuting these people.
* Shaykh: By what? His refuting these people.
* And in it is evidence for affirming wisdom in Allah's actions?
* Student: ﴿So that We may strengthen﴾ [al-Furqan 32].
* Shaykh: ﴿So that We may strengthen﴾, because the *lam* is for causation (*ta'lil*), and causation is wisdom. So there is a refutation in it against a group of the innovating sects. Which group is this?
* Student: The Ash'aris.
* Shaykh: No, I do not know about the Ash'aris, but what I do know about...
* Student: They denied (...).
* Student: The Jahmiyyah.
* Shaykh: Yes indeed. But the origin of this view is with the Jahmiyyah Mujbira (the Determinist Jahmiyyah). They hold that the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, are not caused by purpose, and that He, glorified and exalted, creates and legislates, creating creatures or creation and legislating laws, merely by will and not for any wisdom. They cite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23]. But how could they derive that from this verse?!

So these verses show the wisdom behind sending down the Qur'an in stages, and that Allah's actions are purposeful and accompanied by wisdom.

Alright, is this wisdom in the actions of Allah, glorified and exalted, whether legislative or non-legislative, known or unknown?

Some of it is known and some is unknown to us, but it is known to Allah.

In this is evidence that among the wisdoms in sending down the Qur'an is strengthening the heart of the Messenger ﷺ, whether that strengthening is in establishing the message. What else?

* Student: (...) in refuting doubts.
* Shaykh: Yes, or strengthening in refuting the doubts presented to him.
* In the verse there is evidence that for every falsehood there is a response to that falsehood in the Qur'an. Or, if you wish, say something more general: we find the clarification of its falsehood in the revelation sent down to Muhammad ﷺ. From where do we take this?
﴿And they do not bring you any example but that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ [al-Furqan 33]. No doubt that has been raised up to our day that is not refuted, and in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ is what refutes it. But as you know, not everyone perceives that. Is that not right? Yes, not everyone perceives it. A sword in the hand of a person who does not use it is worth nothing and benefits him no more than a stick or less, but in the hand of someone who wields it, it is a sharp sword with which he strikes and kills. Likewise, the revelation sent down to the Messenger ﷺ is not known to everyone, and not everyone can establish the proof from it, but ﴿the bounty of Allah He gives to whom He wills﴾.

For this reason, "'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrust you with anything? He said: No, by the One who split the seed and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah gives a person regarding the Qur'an, and what is in this sheet: the blood-money (for the killed), the freeing of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever" [Reported by al-Bukhari (3047) from Abu Juhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do you have anything of revelation besides what is in the Book of Allah?" He said: "No, by the One who split the seed and created the soul, I know of nothing except an understanding that Allah gives a man concerning the Qur'an, and what is in this sheet." I said: "And what is in the sheet?" He said: "The blood-money, the freeing of captives, and that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbeliever."].

The conclusion is that Allah, glorified and exalted, gives His bounty to whom He wills regarding the understanding of the Qur'an. How many a verse passes by a person from which he derives several issues, while another cannot (...). Yes. Indeed, Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, hosted Imam Ahmad one night. He brought him supper, and Imam Ahmad ate the whole supper, all of what was brought, then slept, lay down on his bed, and did not get up for the night prayer. Then he got up at dawn and did not ask for wudu'! One of Imam Ahmad's daughters said to her father: "This is al-Shafi'i, about whom you used to say such-and-such. We have not seen him do anything, and we have also not seen him limit himself to a third of his food!" He said: "I will bring you the news." He first asked al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him: "Why did you eat all the food?" He answered: "I do not see anyone in this city whose food is more lawful than Imam Ahmad's, so I wanted my belly to be filled with this lawful food." That is one answer. So he had a purpose. And is satiety at times permissible or not?

* Student: Permissible.
* Shaykh: Permissible. "Abu Hurayrah drank milk, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Drink,' and he said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I cannot find a passage for it'" [Reported by al-Bukhari (6452) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "I cannot find a path for it."]. But we, we talk to ourselves about this hadith at every meal. Every meal we say what Abu Hurayrah said! That is a passing thought, and passing thoughts are many.

And he asked him: "Why did you not stand in the night prayer?" He said: "I was reflecting on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Abu 'Umayr, what did the little bird do?' [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6129) and Muslim (2150/30), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.] And I derived a thousand benefits from the hadith." As for my praying without wudu' for the dawn prayer, I did not sleep; I was reflecting on this hadith.

The conclusion is that people differ in understanding the Book and the Sunnah and in deriving rulings from them. For this reason you find some people who recite a verse to you and set out its benefits, perhaps five or ten benefits, according to what is in the verse, while another derives fifty instead of five, and the bounty of Allah He gives to whom He wills. (...)

Yes indeed, but I do not think he took it from the wording of the hadith alone; Allah knows best. Whenever he saw a benefit, he brought another hadith that indicates it and then derived from it. (...)

﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ [al-Furqan 32].

* Student: (...) says: Why was the Qur'an sent down to him all at once?
* Shaykh: How is the doubt raised?
* Student: Because the earlier nations were...
* Shaykh: The messengers.
* Student: The earlier messengers used to have their books sent down to them without (...).
* Shaykh: Well done. ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾

Alright, this expression ﴿was sent down﴾ (*nuzzila*), although it is well known that *nuzzila* is used when something is sent down gradually, here He said it was sent down all at once. How can ﴿nuzzila﴾ and ﴿all at once﴾ be reconciled?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It comes with the meaning of *anzala* ("to send down").
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: That is, *nazzala* and *anzala* have the same meaning. Like, a similar example among verbs is that the doubled form can have the meaning of the hamzated form. Who has an example?
* Student: (*ihmarra*) and (*ihtamara*).
* Shaykh: No, subhan Allah, you brought half the answer. Who has an example?
* Student: (*akhbara*).
* Shaykh: (*akhbara*) and (*khabbara*).

Alright, fine, this is one way. What is the second way?

* Student: The second way is that (...), that is, this sending down, if it were sent down, would be all at once.
* Shaykh: You mean in terms of consideration?

In these noble verses we noted that there is a refutation in them of a group of the people of innovation who deny one of the greatest attributes of Allah. What is it that they deny of Allah's attributes?

Alright, Allah, glorified and exalted, clarified that for those who deny the Messenger ﷺ, whatever doubt they raise, however clearly it is put, Allah answers it with something stronger and greater.

From what preceded, what indicates the affirmation of resurrection?
