* The Shaykh: How? Indeed, its presence beside a verb makes it for exhortation, and its presence beside a nominal sentence makes it conditional. Yes.
(﴿Had it not been that we were patient in adhering to them﴾. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in way﴾, openly in the Hereafter, ﴿who is more astray in way?﴾ Are they, or the believers?) If he had said: "or the Messenger" — since (...) the Messenger ﷺ — it would have been better.
﴿And they will know when they see the punishment﴾. The author says: "openly in the Hereafter." This is not necessarily in the Hereafter; one restricts to the Hereafter what is necessary. We say: when do they see the punishment? In the Hereafter, and at death they witness it. And if they claim that they repented at death, repentance does not benefit them: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"﴾ [an-Nisa 18].
﴿And they will know﴾ ﴿who is more astray in way﴾: they, or the Messenger ﷺ.
In the phrase ﴿And they will know﴾ there is a threat that is evident; i.e., they will know in that state whether they are the more astray or the Messenger ﷺ is. And what is the reality?
* Students: They are the more astray.
* The Shaykh: They will know, when they see the punishment, that they are the more astray.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire? Would you be responsible for him?﴾ [al-Furqan 43]. ﴿Have you seen﴾: the address is to the Messenger ﷺ, because the context indicates it; and I do not think it is correct here to make it address everyone who can be addressed, because His saying ﴿Would you be responsible for him?﴾ suits whom? The Messenger ﷺ, as in His saying: ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 22].
And here ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾, he says: "meaning, inform me." How does "seen" mean "inform me"? Seeing is information?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: But I want its implication; that is: have you seen, then inform me. This meaning is the reason scholars interpret ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ as "inform me," because the intended question about seeing here is not merely whether you have seen or not, but its implication, which is informing; that is, if you have seen, then inform me.
Here (ra'aytu) they say it takes two objects, and the second object must be an interrogative clause. Let us see what we have in the verse: ﴿Have you seen one who took as his god his own desire﴾: the first object?
* Student: ﴿مَنِ﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَهَهُ﴾. And the second object is the clause ﴿Would you be responsible for him?﴾. This is what the author mentioned.
Are there examples of this in the Qur'an?
* Student: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids﴾ [al-Alaq 9].
* The Shaykh: No, that is not in the sense of "inform me."
* Student: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock﴾ [al-Kahf 63].
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿for indeed I forgot the fish﴾.
* Student: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza﴾ [an-Najm 19].
* The Shaykh: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [an-Najm 19, 20].
* Student: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away, and gave a little and was stingy﴾ [an-Najm 33, 34].
* The Shaykh: Yes, there are many. But sometimes the second object is mentioned, and often the second object is omitted, because the context indicates it.
﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ The answer cannot be: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female?﴾ [an-Najm 21]; that is not possible. But the meaning is: do they avail you anything? Do they benefit you? Do they deserve to be worshipped? And similar things. There is more to discuss, Allah willing, to come.
* Student: According to the grammarians' view (...), so here the matter becomes (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he says: "You have known this, so inform me of it."
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Allahu Akbar, Glory be to Allah the Mighty! The Qur'an, glory be to Allah the Mighty, is not like the rest of speech; you find questions, commands, challenges in the context, and this is from its inimitability in reality, meaning you do not find speech... because all these variations in speech necessitate stirring a person and drawing him in, but, as we have said before, this applies to one who reads it with the heart. As for one who reads it only with the eyes without insight, he does not benefit from it.
* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they were, before it was sent down to them, before that, certainly in despair﴾ [ar-Rum 49]. The repetition of ﴿من قبل﴾ twice (...), ﴿وَإِنْ كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ﴾?
* The Shaykh: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done — do not think them safe from punishment﴾ [Al 'Imran 188]. This repetition is for a benefit and purpose. Here, ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ involves a difference: is it the first, or is ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ other than the first? ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ means: ﴿before it was sent down upon them﴾, i.e., ﴿before this descent﴾, so it is repetition for emphasis. If ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ means: before this matter that happened to them, not before it was sent down, then their state, there is no repetition.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: So what does it mean? Does it mean that (...)?
* The Shaykh: (...) faith at death, except for a person whose inner state is corrupt. As for the person whose deeds are righteous and built upon sound belief, it is not possible, but he is at risk, because it is feared that his deeds are built upon a corrupt inner state.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, when a person witnesses it, repentance no longer benefits him.
* Student: Then, is it not valid to say: (...)?
* The Shaykh: If He misguided him? What do you think?
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: We say: it is not possible for Him to misguide him, because Allah says: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim 27]. Misguidance at death occurs only on the basis that the person was not upright in his worship, as came in the sound hadith: "Indeed, a man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise in what appears to people, while he is among the people of the Fire"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4207), and Muslim (112/179), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him.]].
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, it must be that the inner state is corrupt, because we know that if a person builds his deed on sound belief, whether sincerely or not sincerely, Allah will not forsake the believer ever, the true believer. This is what we always called to: to be careful about the work of the heart. As for the works of the limbs, they are like the walls of a garden; that is, the outward deeds of the limbs are in the position of the walls for the orchard, protecting it and surrounding it, while the essential work is the work of the heart. We have said: one should always be careful to purify the heart and correct the heart; this is the most important thing. These outward deeds are in reality means of improvement and growth, like watering the orchard. The Messenger ﷺ likened the greatest outward worship, which is prayer, to a river that purifies a person from his filth[[Muslim (667/286) narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you see if there were a river at the door of one of you, in which he bathed five times every day, would any of his filth remain?" They said: "No filth would remain." He said: "That is like the five prayers; Allah erases sins by them."]]. These are thus nourishments for the heart, substances from which the heart benefits; the essential thing is the heart.
Therefore we must always examine our hearts: sometimes there is an inner state of envy in the heart, for example. This inner state of envy is not minor, because it was inherited from whom? From the Jews. Would you be pleased to resemble the Jews? No one would be pleased, yet you find it present in the hearts of many believers. The matter of showing off in worship or in appearance. (...)
After he clarified examples from the nations that Allah, blessed and exalted, destroyed because of their denial of the messengers, and clarified that among these nations were those upon whom they had passed, namely the town of the people of Lot, which was rained upon with the rain of evil.
Then Allah the Exalted moved on to what is even worse and more severe in rebuke: that they ﴿do not expect resurrection﴾; i.e., they do not hope for resurrection, so they neither aspire to it nor fear it.
Then Allah the Exalted moved on to the state of these people with the Messenger ﷺ, whom we must honor, magnify and revere, namely that these deniers took him in mockery, and that the saying "took him in mockery" is more severe and emphatic than saying "they mocked him"; i.e., they made him like a figure that is mocked. But if he had said "they mocked him," it would be an act, and an act in general indicates a single occurrence, unlike the first, which made him like a figure to be mocked.
Then he clarified that, along with taking him in mockery, they ridicule him in speech, saying: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?﴾ belittling him. Then, despite their belittling of him, they boast that they were patient with their gods, and that the Prophet's ﷺ call had a strong effect, were it not that they were patient with it, with their gods, they would have been influenced by it: ﴿He had nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been patient in adhering to them.﴾
Then Allah the Exalted threatened them that when they see the punishment they will know who is more astray: they, or the Prophet ﷺ.
Then Allah the Exalted mentioned an interrogation mixed with wonder regarding one who took his own desire as his god, saying: ﴿Have you seen one who takes as his god his own desire? Would you be responsible for him?﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 35–44 (part 7 of 9):

We have already mentioned, regarding ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾, that it means "inform me" (akhbirni), and that this is not its literal meaning, but rather a meaning necessarily implied by the sight that means knowledge ('ilm). When the questioner says "Ara'ayta" he does not want to ask the addressee whether he saw something; rather he wants to ask about the necessary consequence of this seeing, which is informing. For this reason they say that it means "akhbirni", by way of mentioning the thing necessarily implied (itlaq al-mulzumll-lazim) [i.e., the cause-term used for its implied result].

As for its grammatical analysis (i'rab), did we mention it yesterday?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The first is the wish (al-tamanni).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...), ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. This construction ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ occurs frequently in the Qur'an, and it governs two objects: the first of them is a noun, and the second is either an interrogative clause or an oath clause. As for the first object—pay attention to its analysis, because it is difficult—we said that it is a noun, either mentioned or omitted. So now the first object is a noun, either mentioned or omitted. That is one point. The second object is a clause, either interrogative or oath. Is this understood?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good. The taa' in ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ is the subject (fa'il). It may be followed by a pronoun merely to indicate the addressee, and it has no place in grammatical analysis; we say it is a letter of address (harf khitab) with no place in analysis. The kaf, which is a letter of address, is attached to it and has no place in analysis.

Let us give examples of this: ﴿قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ [al-Isra' 62]. Where is the first object here? ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾?
* Students: (...).
The Shaykh: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكَ هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ [al-Isra' 62]?
* Student: ﴿هَذَا الَّذِي﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿هَذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ﴾ is the first object, and the second object is the oath clause: ﴿لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ﴾, ﴿لَئِنْ أَخَّرْتَنِ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَأَحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾. Understood?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And the kaf in ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكَ﴾ is a letter of address with no place in analysis. So the first object is present, and the second object, an oath clause, is present.

﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ وَخَتَمَ عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ مَنْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾ [al-An'am 46]. Where is the first object?
* Student: Omitted.
* The Shaykh: Omitted, because it cannot be a clause as the first object. So it is omitted, its estimated form being: ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ your state, meaning: inform me about your state ﴿إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ﴾ and so on. The clause ﴿مَنْ إِلَهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾ is the second object.

﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ اللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أَوْ جَهْرَةً هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ [al-An'am 47]. Here there is the kaf of address, ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ﴾, the taa' is for the singular, and the addressee is plural or singular?
* Student: Plural.
* The Shaykh: What indicates that they are plural?
* Student: The mim.
* The Shaykh: The kaf and the mim in ﴿أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ﴾. Its first object is omitted, and its second object is ﴿هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾. So the summary of its analysis is: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ [al-Furqan 43] means "inform me," this meaning is implied, and it is not the literal meaning of ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾, because ra'a here means 'alima. As for its analysis, the taa' in ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ is the subject, and it may be singular always, or plural such as ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-An'am 46], or dual: "ara'aytuma in kana kadha wa kadha?"

It may sometimes be followed by a kaf to indicate the addressee while the taa' remains singular. This is regarding ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾. As for its object or the thing it governs, it governs two objects: the first is a noun, either omitted or mentioned, and the second is an interrogative or oath clause.

Let us look at what we have now in the noble verse: (﴿أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾ [al-Furqan 43] i.e., its object of desire (mahwiyyuhu)).

The author explained "hawa" as meaning "mahwi" (object of desire), that is, he explained the verbal noun in the sense of the passive participle. That is, he took a stone or a tree as the god, making the tree the god, and the tree or stone is the hawa or the mahwi? 
* Student: Mahwi.
* The Shaykh: Mahwi. For this reason he explained hawa as mahwi, because he wants the god here to be the one worshipped.

But the correct view is that the verse stands on its apparent meaning, and that the god is the hawa itself. That means he has made the followed thing his hawa. A person following another, whether his own desire or someone else's, following another is from taking him as a god. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Tawbah 31]. "'Adi ibn Hatim said: O Messenger of Allah, we do not worship them? He said: 'Do they not make lawful what Allah has forbidden and you make it lawful, and forbid what Allah has made lawful and you forbid it?' He said: Yes. He said: 'That is their worship.'"[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (218), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Kubra (20350), with their two chains from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with a gold cross on my neck, and he said: "O 'Adi, throw this idol from your neck," so I threw it, and I reached him while he was reciting Surat Bara'a, and he recited this verse: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ until he finished it. I said: We do not worship them. He said: "Do they not forbid what Allah has made lawful and you make it lawful, and make lawful what Allah has forbidden and you make it lawful?" I said: Yes. He said: "That is their worship."]]

So we say: the verse stands on its apparent meaning, namely that the god is the hawa itself, and hawa leads a person to worship trees and stones, and leads him to make adultery lawful, and usury lawful, and other things. Therefore the better course, and what is the better course? To keep the verse on its apparent meaning, and not to turn it toward the worshipped thing, contrary to the author.

As for his statement: "the second object is put first because it is more important": how is the second object, and where is the second object?

The original is: "man ittakhadha hawahu ilahahu" (whoever took his desire as his god). So the hawa is what is taken, not the god; the one who takes a god is the hawa, not the god taking a hawa. The god has not taken a hawa; rather the hawa is taken as a god. Therefore the author said the object was put first because it is more important; that is, because it is the locus of wonder. The wonder is that this thing should be a god. That is the locus of wonder, not merely the hawa, which is not a locus of wonder; the focus of astonishment is that it should be taken as a god.

On this basis: the first object is ﴿إِلَهَهُ﴾ [al-Furqan 43], and the second is ﴿هَوَاهُ﴾ [al-Furqan 43].

He said: (And the clause ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾ [al-Furqan 43] is the first object of ra'ayta.)

His statement: "the clause ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾". Is his statement correct or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Is his statement correct or not?
* Student: ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾ is the first object?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he says: the clause ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾ is the first object.
* Student: If we say it is singular, the statement is not correct.
* The Shaykh: And if you say it is not singular?
* Student: Then his statement is correct, but not (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but is the relative pronoun and its complement expressed as a clause? Because ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾, whether you say it is singular, and it is singular in any case as you said, there are no two opinions about it except according to the method of Ibn Jinni (...).

Is ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾ expressed as a clause together with its complement?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, but is it described as a clause? If you say, for example: "Qadima alladhi safara" (the one who traveled arrived), would you say "alladhi safara" is a clause? No, because the relative noun is singular, but its complement is a clause. This is shown by the fact that the relative noun occurs as a subject, and a subject cannot be a clause. You say: "Ja'a alladhi safara" (the one who traveled came); "alladhi" is the subject and cannot be a clause.

Accordingly, his statement "the clause ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾" contains looseness of expression, and the correct statement is: ﴿مَنِ﴾ in his words ﴿مَنِ اتَّخَذَ﴾ is the first object of (ra'ayta).

The second: ﴿أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ [al-Furqan 43]. The interrogative here is for negation; meaning: you will not be a guardian over him, i.e., "a protector who guards him from following his desire." That is, you are not a guardian over him, and if you are not a guardian over him, you are not responsible for him. If this is said to the Prophet ﷺ, then others are more deserving of it. We are not guardians over those who disobey Allah nor over those who transgress His command. Rather, what is incumbent upon us is what? 
* Student: Conveying (al-balagh).
* The Shaykh: Conveying and calling to Islam, and the reckoning is upon Allah the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسَابُ﴾ [al-Ra'd 40]. From this we know that a person should not grieve over the misguidance of one who has strayed, if he has fulfilled what Allah obligated upon him of conveying and calling. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ [al-Nahl 127], and He the Exalted said: ﴿لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 3], meaning: destroying yourself that they do not believe, and other verses to this effect; and that a person should not grieve, because the misguidance of one who strays is by the act of Allah the Exalted, and His act is for a wisdom. For this reason the scholars said: we look at the people of sin with two views: a legal (shar'i) view and a divine-decree (kawni) view. The legal view: we try to bind them to what Allah has obligated, and punish them for it, discipline them as befits them, and establish the prescribed penalties upon them, and we do not show them mercy in this, based on His saying: ﴿وَلَا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِمَا رَأْفَةٌ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Nur 2]. This is the legal view, a view of strength and firmness.

As for the second view, the divine-decree view: we feel pity for them and show them mercy, since Allah the Exalted tested them with this matter. Some people bear both of these, and some people can bear only one of them. Which is more complete? The one who bears both is more complete. But some people cannot bear the divine decree, and you find them becoming angry and becoming extremely agitated and rushing excessively, and some people look at the divine decree and say: this is by Allah's decree and destiny, and have no zeal at all, and this too is an error.

So it is obligatory for a person to look at matters through two windows: the window of destiny and the window of the law, so that he may be upright, and this is justice.

So whoever of the people goes astray, we are not guardians over him, but what is due to him from us? Calling to Allah and striving to reform him as far as we can. Yes.
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: This grief over a relative is, in truth, from tenderness and mercy, and it must be accompanied by firmness in calling to Allah, conveying His law, and establishing what is obligatory, including the prescribed penalties upon this opponent, because some people feel tender toward their relative, friend, brother and the like, and do not perform the duty regarding disciplining him and striving to reform him, and this is an error.

The author says: "(No)." What is the meaning of "no"?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: An indication that the interrogative here means negation; that is, you will not be a guardian over him.

(﴿أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ hearing of understanding ﴿أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ what you say to them ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا﴾ [al-Furqan 44] they are further astray from the path, because cattle are led by whoever tends them, while they do not obey their Lord who has blessed them.)

﴿أَمْ تَحْسَبُ﴾: the address is either to the Messenger ﷺ or to everyone to whom address may apply.

As for ﴿أَمْ﴾ meaning "bal" together with the interrogative hamza: is it connected (muttasilah) or disconnected (munqati'ah)? Is it disconnected or connected, or do we not know what connected and disconnected mean?

It is disconnected, because it means "bal," and the connected one is the one that occurs between two equal items, such as His saying: ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ﴾ [al-Munafiqun 6]; this is connected. The one that occurs between two equal items is called connected, because it connects the first to the second; and if it is not so, it is disconnected.

So His statement here, ﴿أَمْ﴾, has no counterpart, so it is disconnected, meaning "bal" and the interrogative hamza.

Is it "taḥsib" or "taḥsab"? ﴿تَحْسَبُ﴾ means "tazunn" (thinks): ﴿أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Furqan 44].

That is, they neither hear nor understand. What is meant by hearing? The author here says: "hearing of understanding." He restricted it to hearing of understanding, because they hear with perception; is this so or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: They hear with perceptual hearing, but it does not benefit them, because they do not comprehend. It would have been better had the author left the verse on its general sense without restriction, and the denial of hearing would then stand for the absence of its benefit, since what gives no benefit is like the non-existent. They do not hear, even though they perceive what is said with sensory perception, but because they do not benefit from this hearing, they become like those who do not hear.

His statement: ﴿أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [al-Furqan 44]: he says "what you say to them." There is clear difficulty in this; rather the intended meaning is ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ everything that benefits them; that is, they have no intellect neither for what you say nor for anything else. ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ here is not the intellect that is quick-wittedness, the perception of matters; for they do understand in this sense, is this so or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: But the intended meaning of intellect is that which restrains its possessor from behaving in an unbecoming way; that is intellect. Intellect is what prevents its possessor from acting unbecomingly; this is true intellect, not the intellect by which a person grasps intelligible things, for the intellect in the sense of grasping intelligibles is the basis of legal responsibility (manat al-taklif), not the basis of praise or blame. Have you understood now?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: So intellect is of two kinds: first, the basis of legal responsibility, by which a person perceives and is distinguished from animals; second, the intellect which is the basis of praise, which restrains its possessor from what is unbecoming. Which of these is negated of the disbelievers?
* Student: The second.
* The Shaykh: The second is negated of the disbelievers, the intellect in the sense of what restrains its possessor from what is unbecoming; this is what is negated of the disbelievers. As for the first, the grasping of intelligibles, this is established for them; that is why they were held responsible and addressed by the law, and were it not so, they would not have been obligated nor would adherence to the law have been binding upon them.

Is this intellect, which Allah the Exalted negated of the disbelievers, one that requires negating quick-wittedness from them?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: No. They are clever, understanding what benefits them and understanding what harms them, but they have no intellect in the sense that this intellect does not restrain them from what is unbecoming. Therefore it is correct to say that they do not understand. Abu Jahl, for example, is he intelligent or not intelligent?
* Student: Intelligent.
* Another student: In the meaning, Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: If you say "intelligent," it is not correct; if you say "not intelligent," in absolute terms it is also not correct.
* Student: In terms of the basis of legal responsibility...
* The Shaykh: Yes. We say: the intellect which is the basis of legal responsibility, he is intelligent, without doubt, and among the most clever of people; and the intellect which is the object of praise, by which a person refrains from what is unbecoming, he is not intelligent. For this reason he remained in his disbelief despite the clarity of the proofs and evidences for the truth of what the Messenger ﷺ brought.

And here, is the intended meaning of intellect the one that Allah negated?

**Student:** It is the one who prevents (a person) from what is unbecoming.

**Shaykh:** Yes. What is meant by it is the intellect, which prevents its possessor from what is unbecoming.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They are only like livestock﴾ [Al-Furqan 44]. This is a restriction (ḥaṣr, exclusive limitation). That is, they are nothing but like livestock, i.e., similar to livestock. "Livestock" (al-anʿām) refers to beasts. It is known that if you say to any person, "You are a beast," does he become angry or not?

**Student:** He becomes angry.

**Another student:** He does not become angry.

**Shaykh:** No. If you say, "You are a beast"?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Yes, he becomes angry without doubt. Allah says ﴿They are only like livestock﴾; He did not say "they are only livestock." The phrase ﴿like livestock﴾ uses the particle of comparison (kāf al-tashbīh), and comparison requires that the thing compared be less than the thing it is compared to. For this reason He says ﴿Rather, they are more astray in the way﴾ [Al-Furqan 44]. This is a shift to the explicit: ﴿Rather, they are more astray in the way﴾, meaning (they are further off the path) than the livestock. How is that?

Because livestock are guided to what benefits them, whereas these people were not guided to what benefits them. When the herdsman calls livestock to the pasture, do they come or not?

**Student:** They come.

**Shaykh:** They come. If he calls them to the milking place, they come. If he calls them to the shelter, they come. Likewise, they flee from what harms them, do they not? But these people are the opposite. The messengers, peace be upon them, call them to what benefits them and warn them against what harms them, yet they are not guided to the right way and do not submit. So they become more astray in the way than the livestock. For this reason Allah the Exalted says, in many verses (Allah has made it clear in several verses, and there are many of them), that the disbelievers are the worst of creation, the worst of what Allah has created: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. They are the worst of creation﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 6]. And ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve﴾ [Al-Anfal 55]. Does it mean worse than dogs?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** Yes, worse than dogs and pigs. Whatever lowliness you can name among the creatures Allah the Most High has created, they are worse than that. Yet we find some Muslims today who honor them, even prefer them over the believers. This is a great trial, by which the enemies of Allah have grown arrogant over the Muslims, for this reason: they see themselves as objects of veneration and reverence among many Muslims, so they became proud of themselves. Even more grievous and calamitous, they have become objects of imitation (taqlīd) for some people, meaning they imitate them.

You know that when a person imitates, he will take pride and see himself as a leader. In reality this is a mishandling of matters and a weakness of character. Rather, it is obligatory that we place these disbelievers in the rank Allah, blessed and exalted, has placed them, and that we not make them examples. If they open for us doors of inventions, industries and other things, yes, we benefit from their knowledge, but not in a way that we display them as outstanding, advanced, and exalted. Yes, we say: they are like the sheep that is guided to good fodder and eats it. They were guided to this craft, and Allah made their work a trial for them and for others. But for us to give them precedence and make them objects of honor and esteem, this is an error.

﴿Rather, they are more astray in the way﴾ [Al-Furqan 44]. The author explained it: "Because the livestock submit to whoever looks after them, while they do not obey their Lord, the One who bestowed blessings upon them."

Last night we were reading the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while they are humbled﴾ [At-Tawbah 29]. So if these People of the Book say, "We adopt the religion of truth, because we follow a messenger," Allah has restricted it: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture﴾. They say: "We believe in Allah and the Last Day, we consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful, and we adopt the religion of truth, because we are upon the religion of the messengers."

**Student:** How is it the religion of truth, when the religion of truth is Islam?

**Shaykh:** What is the evidence?

**Student:** Because whoever affirms the message of Moses and Jesus must necessarily follow Islam, since Jesus came bringing good news of the message of Muhammad ﷺ. So it follows that their following of the messengers...

**Shaykh:** Jesus and Moses.

**Student:** And Moses likewise. It follows from it...

**Shaykh:** ﴿the unlettered Prophet whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [Al-A'raf 157]. Yes.

**Student:** So it follows that they must agree; that is, they must follow the Messenger ﷺ.

**Shaykh:** This is by way of implication (lāzim), but there are things more explicit than this. Yes?

**Student:** We say that it has passed us that whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers.

**Shaykh:** (...)

**Student:** And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Ali 'Imran 85].

**Shaykh:** Praise be to Allah. The context of the verses clarifies what the religion of truth is. The context of the verses: ﴿The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded? They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him. They wish to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [At-Tawbah 30–33].

So we say: the religion of truth is what the Messenger, peace be upon him, brought. Therefore, a Jew or a People of the Book who remains upon a religion, even if his religion was true at the time when it was the established one, is now not true; it is not a religion of truth, because the religion of truth is what Muhammad ﷺ brought. So at the end of the verses there is what indicates that these people, even if they claim that they follow a law and a religion, their religion is not a religion of truth after the Messenger ﷺ came with it: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾.

This is similar to what these people argue with from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 6]. He says ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture﴾, and they say: "We have not disbelieved, we believe." So they make ﴿among﴾ (min) partitive (lil-tabʿīḍ), not explanatory of the genus (li-bayān al-jins). We say: ﴿min﴾ is explanatory of the genus; ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists is an explanation of ﴿those﴾ (alladhīna), an explanation of the relative pronoun in ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture﴾.

The conclusion is that in the Qur'an there are verses, as we mentioned yesterday, that are ambiguous (mutashābihāt), which are followed by whom? ﴿those in whose hearts is deviation﴾ [Ali 'Imran 7]. But the believers refer them back to the clear verses (muḥkam), so they are all clear.

Yes?

**Student:** (...) in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before﴾ [At-Tawbah 30]. So then (...) for the earlier disbelievers?

**Shaykh:** Yes, in their saying: ﴿Ezra is the son of Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah 30]. Yes indeed. But if (...) we say: ﴿Ezra is the son of Allah﴾.

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 68]. Is (...) explicit, Shaykh?

**Shaykh:** It is not explicit.

**Student:** It is not explicit?

**Shaykh:** No.

**Student:** Is there in it (...)?

**Shaykh:** (...)

**Student:** ﴿O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel﴾.

**Shaykh:** Yes. They say: "We have established the Torah and the Gospel."

**Student:** ﴿and what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾, and coordination (ʿaṭf) requires difference.

**Shaykh:** It does not contradict it. We say: what has been revealed to us from our Lord, other than the Torah and the Gospel, because the messengers came with matters other than the Torah and the Gospel.

**Student:** ﴿And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾.

**Shaykh:** ﴿many of them﴾. We say: they are not the many.

**Student:** O Shaykh (...)?

**Shaykh:** Yes, it is not explicit, but there are explicit verses, praise be to Allah, very clear. And this is what made me obligated. I read and said: I read in an article by a woman (...), and apparently she is the one attributed to a female, but it is a feminine noun, not a female. She says: "Why do you make this great uproar about importing nannies? And what is the reason? It is a religion you acknowledge." She says, addressing the Muslim: "A religion you acknowledge. How do you object to one who practices it? And how do you object to the Christian woman who comes to your house to perform the rites of her religion? This is not objectionable, because we, over there in their lands, practice our religion. Even that they, she says, even they provide us with the meal at the fast, so they help us with our religion, and now we deny their religion? And we say: why do we bring nannies and create this uproar?" Although there was no uproar, unfortunately (...). Yes.

This, in reality, is among what makes the matter of the Christians and Jews seem trivial to them: that there exist in some verses ambiguous matters, which people like those whom Allah has caused to deviate in their hearts follow, may Allah protect us. Otherwise, if they had reason, they would understand the danger of the Christians in these very countries, because these very countries are targeted by the enemies of the Muslims, since, to our knowledge, no other land of Islam applies Islam as these countries apply it. So they are targeted from two directions:

From the direction of their adherence to Islam, to an extraordinary degree beyond others, that is one. And from another direction, that they are the place of descent of revelation and the source of the message. If the message is eliminated in its cradle and its source, then the peripheries are all the more so. Although the peripheries have now been consumed, so only this core remains, they have concentrated their efforts on these countries.

But, unfortunately, many of us do not comprehend the danger of this matter, and they are heedless, and their only concern is this world. For this reason they want to obtain it by any means. It is obligatory upon us to be cautious of these enemies, and to know that however much advice they give, as they say, and sincerity in work, this is nothing but a net with which they hunt those who do not understand.

Indeed, in reality, however much they claim advice (if that is true), Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even if he should please you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 221], and ﴿a believing maidservant is better than a polytheistic woman, even if she should please you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 221]. The verse says ﴿believing﴾ (mu'min) and ﴿believing﴾ (mu'minah) as well, notice this; not "Muslim man and Muslim woman," because among the Muslims there are those in whom there is no good. But the speech is about the believer. For this reason, a person should, regarding the nannies of his children and his servants, ensure that they are believers, and be cautious of these enemies.

**Student:** (...)?

**Shaykh:** By Allah, when considering its harms. As for the original ruling, it is permissible to employ a disbeliever. But in view of its harms, and that these countries are free of them, we incline to the view that prohibiting them is more appropriate. Because you know that a dirty garment is not bothered by becoming soiled, but a clean garment is destroyed by any filth. So our country, since it is free of them, is purer. And as you know, in the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, awoke one night in alarm, his face reddened, saying: "There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today an opening has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this," [and he made a circle with his fingers]. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness (khabath) increases."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3346) and Muslim (2880/1).]] And who are the wicked (khabath)? The disbelievers: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾ [At-Tawbah 28]. So the disbelievers are the wicked. Although the hadith may intend something more general than that, yet "an opening has been made today in the barrier of Gog and Magog" indicates what we have pointed to, namely the multiplicity of non-Muslims among the Muslims. Rather, by wickedness may be meant all acts of disobedience; all acts of disobedience are wickedness, and acts of obedience are purity. But perhaps the hadith includes this and that, and the opening of the barrier of Gog and Magog supports the first meaning. Yes.

**Student:** Is there not any (...)?

**Shaykh:** And what is it?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Which of them?

**Student:** (...) ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteousness—no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 69]?

**Shaykh:** Yes. We say: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. Those who deny the Messenger are not believers.

**Student:** There is no mention in it of denial of the Messenger ﷺ.

**Shaykh:** No, it is well known.

**Student:** Meaning within the same verse?

**Shaykh:** Yes, but it is well known...

**Student:** (...) according to the way of the messengers?

**Shaykh:** Yes indeed. Essentially, whenever a prophet came and they denied him, they became disbelievers in their prophet. Yes.

**Student:** Is it not (...)?

**Shaykh:** Is it coordinated with (...)?

**Student:** Yes, ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans﴾.

**Shaykh:** Like this, ﴿and the Sabeans﴾ is in the nominative (marfūʿa).

**Student:** It is nominative only in Surat al-Ma'idah.

**Shaykh:** Yes.

**Student:** In the other verses, in the other surahs, no...

**Shaykh:** It is nominative, and it is coordinated with something in the accusative (manṣūb).

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and those who establish prayer and those who give zakah and those who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [An-Nisa' 162]. This is the reverse of the verses you mentioned: an accusative (manṣūb) among nominatives, whereas this is a nominative among accusatives.

**Student:** (...)?

**Shaykh:** And what do you say about the i'rab (grammatical analysis)?

**Student:** Nominative (...).

**Another student:** The subject is omitted (...).

**Shaykh:** Yes. ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾, we are finished. That is, the teacher analyzed it: ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾ as an accusative of praise or commendation, "and I commend those who establish prayer."

If someone says: What is the wisdom in breaking the coordination to this construction? Shall we say?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes, concern for prayer, that is?

**Student:** Yes.

**Shaykh:** And something else: this is a semantic benefit. Is there also a verbal benefit?

**Student:** Alerting, alerting the listener.

**Shaykh:** Yes, alerting. Because a change of style necessitates attention. If we kept them all in one pattern we would just go on, but (...). So there is in this an alerting.

We have the verses the brother mentioned: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ and so on to the end [Al-Ma'idah 69]. Yes?

**Student:** (...)

**Shaykh:** Yes, but the discussion is on whether (...) is disjoined?

**Student:** The predicate (khabar) of (...).

**Shaykh:** No, the predicate? The "waw" is a particle of coordination (ʿaṭf).

**Student:** ﴿and the Sabeans﴾ is the predicate.

**The Shaykh:** (...) ﴿And the Sabians and the Christians﴾. It is permissible for ﴿the Christians﴾ to be in the nominative case as well; it can be nominative.

**The student:** And it is permissible to put it in the accusative.

**The Shaykh:** It can be accusative, but it is not required to be accusative. The *waw* here is then for *istinaf* (resumption, beginning a new sentence). ﴿And the Sabians and the Christians﴾ is likewise. The construction is: ﴿And the Sabians and the Christians [are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day]﴾, yes. This becomes a resumptive sentence between two sentences. Or we say: ﴿And the Sabians and the Christians, whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ is the predicate (*khabar*), and the predicate is omitted from the first sentence.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 35–44 (part 1 of 9):

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book and appointed his brother Harun with him as a minister﴾ [al-Furqan 35].

In this sentence, ﴿And We certainly gave﴾, there are emphatic particles. How many are they?
* Student: The lam, qad, and the waw.
* The Shaykh: No, the waw is a conjunction particle (harf 'atf).
* Student: The lam and qad.
* Student: And the oath?
* The Shaykh: And the oath. Because the lam is a preparatory lam (lam al-mawți'ah) for the oath, and the estimate is: "By Allah, indeed."

Emphasis in the Qur'an arises from one of two matters: either it is in response to the denial of a denier, or it is due to the importance of the subject, or both together. The matter is important, and there is someone who denies it, so Allah the Exalted emphasizes that matter.

Here, the giving of the Book to Musa is a fact that is not denied, but because of the importance of the subject Allah emphasized it, in order to present to the Messenger ﷺ images of the denial of earlier peoples, so that this is more eloquent in consoling him. Earlier, Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And thus We appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾ [al-Furqan 31]. This is a general statement, right or not?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And thus We appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals, and sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper﴾ [al-Furqan 31]. Then he began here to detail that and explain what occurred in a specific manner.

(﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾ [al-Furqan 35] the Torah), and "gave" (ataynā) means: We gave it to him, sent it down to him by Allah the Exalted, written on tablets. This is the meaning of ītā' (giving).

(﴿and appointed his brother Harun with him as a minister﴾ [al-Furqan 35], a helper).
* Student: O Shaykh, (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, tablets on which the Torah was written.
* Student: So, in the form of tablets (...).
* The Shaykh: Musa brought them from Allah; they did not descend from the sky.
* Student: No, he (...).
* The Shaykh: Allah sent them down to Musa, and he brought them to his people (...) in al-A'raf, spread out.

﴿and appointed his brother Harun with him as a minister﴾.
Is ﴿his brother﴾ from both father and mother, or from the mother only?
* Student: From the mother only.
* The Shaykh: How many, from father and mother. As for his saying: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard nor my head﴾ [Taha 94], this is from the way of gentleness and tenderness, because the mother is more compassionate than the father; otherwise he is his brother from father and mother.

(﴿Harun as a minister﴾ [al-Furqan 35], a helper) from al-azr, which is strength (...).
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: What issue?
* Student: The kinship.
* The Shaykh: The kinship?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: That he is his full brother?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that is established.

His saying: ﴿minister﴾ is from al-azr, which is support, meaning that he was a minister, i.e., a helper to him. That was at Musa's request, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Harun, my brother. Strengthen my back through him, and make him a partner in my affair﴾ [Taha 30–32]. It is said that there is no brother more generous and more virtuous than Musa was toward Harun, because he requested that he be a messenger, and prophethood is the highest rank that a human can attain.

(﴿So We said: Go to the people who denied Our signs﴾, i.e., the Copts, Pharaoh and his people, so they went to them with the message and they denied them, ﴿then We destroyed them with destruction﴾ [al-Furqan 36], We annihilated them with annihilation).
﴿Go to the people who denied Our signs﴾. In the word ﴿denied﴾ there is a difficulty, namely that it implies the denial preceded the message: ﴿Go to the people who denied Our signs﴾. How could they be deniers when no messenger had reached them?
The answer: the past tense here has the meaning of the future, meaning: those who will deny Our signs, since the signs had not yet reached them.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Wait a moment, brother.

So the meaning: ﴿who denied Our signs﴾, i.e., they will deny them in the future. Or it may be said: they denied Our signs according to the knowledge of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, meaning: We estimated that they would deny.

A third possibility may be mentioned, though it is a possibility not supported by anything: that a messenger had been sent to them and they denied him. This is supported by the saying of the believing man from the family of Pharaoh: ﴿And Yusuf had already come to you with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought you, until when he died you said: Allah will never send after him a messenger﴾ [Ghafir 34]. So if it is said: Yusuf was very much earlier than Musa, and we do not know whether Pharaoh reached him or not, then it is said: perhaps the traces of his message remained; for this reason he addressed them (...) ﴿And Yusuf had already come to you﴾, and they did not deny it, they did not say: he did not come to us, ﴿but you remained in doubt about what he brought you﴾, meaning: until now.

So the possibilities we have are how many? The possibilities are three: either the past here means the present.
* Student: (...) its usage with the meaning of the present.
* The Shaykh: This is common in the Arabic language, which does not come to mind now, and perhaps will come.

Or it means: they denied in the knowledge of Allah, according to the knowledge and estimate of Allah the Exalted. Or it means: according to the earlier message, which is the message of Yusuf.

﴿Those who denied Our signs﴾ [al-Furqan 36].
And his saying: ﴿Our signs﴾, is the intended meaning of the signs here cosmic or legislative?
* Student: Legislative.
* Another student: Both.
* The Shaykh: It appears that it can include both, because the signs of Allah the Exalted, as you know, are legislative signs and cosmic signs. What relates to creation and decree is cosmic signs, because in its orderliness, precision, and craftsmanship there is what indicates the wisdom of its Maker and His power. What relates to revelation is legislative signs, because the rectification of this revelation for the one to whom it was sent down according to what was legislated is one of the great signs indicating that it is from Allah: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa 82]. Yes?
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, good, fine.

﴿Go to the people who denied Our signs, then We destroyed them with destruction﴾ [al-Furqan 36]: go to them, and We destroyed them. We all know that the verse contains an estimate. What is the estimate? So they went to them, they denied them, and We destroyed them with destruction. This estimate is required because destruction cannot occur merely by the messenger's going to them; there must be denial, for Allah the Exalted will not destroy anyone except for a sin.

His saying: ﴿destruction﴾ is a verbal noun intended for magnification, meaning a great destruction. There is no doubt that the destruction that befell Pharaoh and his people is among the greatest destructions, because Allah says: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and comfort in which they took delight﴾ [al-Dukhan 25–27]. When this great blessing in which the people of Pharaoh were is followed by destruction, what is the effect of the destruction upon them? It is severe, because destruction that strikes the wretched is lighter than when it strikes the comfortable, far lighter; for this reason Allah described this destruction by His saying: ﴿destruction﴾, meaning great and complete.

This destruction does not contradict what our brother pointed to, that Allah the Exalted saved Pharaoh in his body, not in his soul; for his soul perished with those who perished. But He saved his body so that it would be a sign to the Children of Israel, a token that he had perished, because the man had terrified and frightened them, so they would not be fully reassured until they saw his corpse dead; and thereby it is a sign and token that nothing of him remained.

Now, is there in this a confirmation of what consoles the Messenger ﷺ?
The answer: yes, there is, because Pharaoh was among the most arrogant and haughty of people, and yet Allah destroyed him and his people with complete destruction. Likewise, the final outcome will be for the Messenger ﷺ just as the final outcome was for Musa and his people.

This is a story: ﴿and the people of Nuh﴾ [al-Furqan 37].
* Student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, they know it either before the revelation of the Qur'an or after it, because they know that the Qur'an is true in themselves.

Now, he began with mentioning Musa (...) although he is later in time relative to the people of Nuh. What is the wisdom in that?
* Student: Closer in time (...).
* The Shaykh: Because he is closer in time to the people of Nuh.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, closer in time and more intense in arrogance.

﴿And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ and so on [al-Furqan 37].
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And what is it?
* Student: Observance of (...).
* The Shaykh: No, the difficulty is: why did he begin with Musa before Nuh, when Nuh is earlier?

Now, ﴿and the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers﴾ has a difficulty from the standpoint of i'rab, namely that ﴿the people of Nuh﴾ is in the accusative, and ﴿and the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾, though no governing element preceded it that requires the accusative?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "And mention the people of Nuh"? Yes, the commentator mentioned it. But in truth my thought went to something other than the commentator's estimate; otherwise, had I seen it, I would not have asked you.

In reality, the governing element for it exists and is not estimated: it is his saying ﴿We drowned them﴾, so it is an instance of ishtighal (the verb being occupied with the pronoun). But why is it in the accusative when the preferred reading on the surface is the nominative?

We say: because it is conjoined to a verbal sentence, and when it is conjoined to a verbal sentence, the estimate of a verb is preferable to a subject-predicate; so that the two sentences correspond: a verb is conjoined to a verb, meaning: ﴿so We destroyed them with destruction, and We drowned the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, and We drowned the people of Nuh﴾ (...) ﴿so We destroyed them and We drowned the people of Nuh﴾.

The point now, according to the author's view, is that it is accusative by an estimate (﴿and﴾ mention ﴿the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers﴾ [al-Furqan 37]). But we say: we do not need an estimate, and the matter is one of ishtighal, and ishtighal is known to you, I think?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: This ishtighal, like (...), admits of the five rulings, and ishtighal also admits of the five rulings: sometimes the nominative is obligatory, sometimes the accusative is obligatory, sometimes the accusative is preferred, sometimes the nominative is preferred, and sometimes both are equal; the five rulings apply to it. The rulings of grammar are not the divisions (...) in the Sharia.

In such a construction, which is preferred? The accusative is preferred, because it is conjoined to a verbal sentence, and when conjoined to a verbal sentence the accusative is preferred, so that the verb is estimated to make it fit what it is conjoined to.

(﴿and the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers﴾ [al-Furqan 37]: by their denial of Nuh, because of the length of his stay among them, so he was as if he were messengers; or because his denial is a denial of the rest of the messengers, since they all came with monotheism.)

The author has made the noble verse take the form of an answer to a difficulty.
﴿when they denied the messengers﴾. It is known that Nuh, peace be upon him, is the first of the messengers: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa 163]. Likewise, regarding intercession, "I was the first messenger Allah sent to the people of the earth" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (7410) and Muslim, the wording is his (193/322), from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be troubled by that - Ibn 'Ubayd said: they will be inspired to that - and they will say: If we sought intercession from our Lord, so that He might relieve us from this place of ours. So they will come to Adam ﷺ and say: You are Adam, the father of mankind, Allah created you with His hand, breathed into you of His spirit, commanded the angels and they prostrated to you; intercede for us with your Lord, so that He may relieve us from this place of ours. He will say: I am not the one for that... but go to Nuh, the first messenger Allah sent..." the hadith].

If he is the first of the messengers, how is the answer to His saying ﴿they denied the messengers﴾, since no messenger preceded him and no messenger came with him?

The author answered with one of two matters: either that, because of his long stay among his people, he became as though he were many messengers, for he remained among them nine hundred and fifty years, and this period encompasses many messengers; so because of the length of his stay he became as one multiplied. That is the first.

The second answer: (or because his denial is a denial of the rest of the messengers, since they all shared in coming with monotheism). This is then a case of the genus, for whoever denies one messenger is as if he denied all messengers, since—as we have stated—the enemies of the messengers do not oppose them for their persons, but oppose them for what they call to and what they brought. This is a genus, so their denial of one messenger is a denial of all messengers. This is closer, and for this reason whoever denies one messenger is a denier of all messengers. By this we know that the Jews now deny Musa, and that the Christians who claim to follow Isa deny Isa, why? Because they deny the Messenger ﷺ, so they deny even their own prophets. By this we also know that the widespread modern usage of calling the Christians "Christians" (Masihiyyin) is a mistake, and that they should not be called that, because the Messiah is innocent of them, and it is not permissible to attribute them or their religion to him; rather they should be called what Allah called them, namely "Nasara" (Christians/Nazarenes). The Muslims in their books have continued to call them by this name, al-Nasara, until they colonized the Muslim lands and introduced this expression to the Muslims as a softening and an honoring, so that their creed would be dyed with the legal description, which is "Masihiyyah" (Christianity).

We say: we call Allah to witness that the Messiah, peace be upon him, is innocent of them, and that they disbelieve in him just as they disbelieve in Muhammad ﷺ. Indeed, in reality they disbelieve in him, not in terms of generality and genus, but in terms of specification; for Allah the Exalted says about Isa: ﴿O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾ [al-Saff 6]. He addresses whom? The Children of Israel, and gives them good tidings of this messenger. Can one give good tidings of something not connected to him? It is not possible. If he were giving them good news of a messenger who would come to the Arabs and fight and battle them, would that be good news? Never; the good news is "a messenger who will come" to them to rescue them from misguidance. When Muhammad ﷺ came to this nation, did he fight the Christians or not? Yes, he fought them, and Allah obligated fighting them, the Jews, and all the disbelievers. Is it possible that Isa gave the Christians good news of "a messenger who will come after me whose name is Ahmad" in order to fight them? No, it is not possible. By this we know that they denied Isa specifically, not the genus of messengerhood, as we stated at first.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but this good news is present in the original book, and I do not think it was altered; it must remain, because he gives them good news, and one gives good news only of what is connected to him. So it appears that it was not subjected to alteration, because it remains.
* Student: (...) from the meaning, meaning?
* The Shaykh: The meaning, or some matters, they concealed them or the like. For this reason, when the Jews wanted not to apply the legal penalty in the Torah, they did not go to remove it from the Torah; it remains, but they try to conceal it from the people, as is well known.

* Sheikh: Yes. And you know that proper names may be fixed nouns without derivation, yes, perhaps they have no derivation.

* Sheikh: Yes, but as it appears to me, and God knows best, the names of the prophets mostly have meanings, but I do not know anything about them.
* Student: But are they not better than ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd al-Rahman, I mean?
* Sheikh: What?
* Student: The names of the prophets.
* Sheikh: No, the best names (...) no, rather "The most beloved names to God are ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd al-Rahman"[[Recorded by Muslim (2132/2) and Abu Dawud, with his wording (4949), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, may God be pleased with them both.]]. (...)
That He placed for every prophet an enemy among the criminals, as consolation for the Prophet ﷺ and a warning to his people, and that He named specific peoples so that this would be more eloquent, because specification is like a striking example. Who was named?
* Student: Shu'ayb.
* Sheikh: Before that?
* Student: The people of Lut.
* Sheikh: Before that? The first one God began with was the people of Musa, then after that Noah, and after that ʿAd and Thamud. All of this we have already mentioned, and we mentioned that God, glory be to Him, destroyed Pharaoh, who denied the Messenger, peace be upon him, by drowning in what place? He was drowned in the Red Sea, and that the wisdom behind his drowning in water is that he boasted of water when he said to his people: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾ [al-Zukhruf 51], so he boasted of water and God Most High destroyed him with what he boasted of.
As for the people of Noah, they were destroyed by the general flood, which is among the signs of God, when God caused the earth to gush forth with springs and opened the gates of heaven with pouring water.
As for ʿAd, with what were they destroyed? With the wind. The wisdom in that is that they used to boast of strength, saying: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15], so God Most High destroyed them with subtle things that are nothing, to show people that a human, however strong, is weak before the power of God, Mighty and Majestic.
With what were the people of Thamud destroyed?
* Student: With the quake together with the cry.
* Sheikh: With the quake together with the cry. God shook them and Gabriel cried out at them until their hearts were torn within their bodies, and they became like the crushed stubble of the fence-builder. Then, the cry is also not like warning sirens that repeat, so that perhaps someone enters the shelters; rather, it was one single cry only: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single cry, and they became like the dry stubble of one who builds a pen﴾ [al-Qamar 31], meaning like the stubble of a pen, and it is known that the stubble of a pen is crumbled and decayed.
The wisdom of all of this is two things. Are these the wisdom of mentioning these messengers and what befell their peoples?
* Student: (...).
* Sheikh: No, anything else?
* Student: And a warning to the disbelievers.
* Sheikh: And a warning to the disbelievers of Quraysh. Consolation for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and warning to those who deny him that what befell those before them may befall them. Yes, and for this reason Shu'ayb said to his people: ﴿And O my people, let not my dissension bring upon you what befell the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih, and the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud 89].
Then He said: ﴿and the companions of the Rass⁠﴾ [al-Furqan 38]. The Rass: the name of a well; it is said: a well not lined with stone, either for any well or for an unlined well. God, glory be to Him, did not specify who the companions of the Rass were, so the exegetes differed about them greatly. It is said that they are, as the author said, the people of Shu'ayb, but this is not correct. It is said that they are from the people of Thamud, and not the people of Thamud. On this view, their being coordinated with Thamud is coordination of a part with the whole. Yes. And they are not the Thamud, companions of the well, meaning the well of the she-camel, because Thamud is well known, meaning they are distinct: their destruction is known, and their reply to their messenger is known, and the principle in coordination is what? Difference.
It is also said that the companions of the Rass, as Ibn Jarir preferred, are the companions of the Trench mentioned by God Most High in Surat al-Buruj.
But the better course is to suspend judgment on their identification, because God Most High did not identify them, yet we know that these people were known to the Arabs at the time of the Qur'an's revelation, because God, glory be to Him, would not have struck examples for them with a people whose fate they did not know. Rather...
Because God, glory be to Him, would not have struck examples for them with a people whose fate they did not know; and rather they were attributed to the Rass. Now we are speaking of identifying them by individuals or by tribes; we say: the better course is suspension. But why were they called the companions of the Rass? It is said: they buried their prophet in this Rass, meaning in the well, so they were called the companions of the Rass, by way of attributing a thing to a shameful and reprehensible deed.
And it is said: they were around this well, and God caused them to sink with their well; the well collapsed with those around it, and they all perished. This concerns the manner of punishment that befell them, or the manner of the deed they did, to which they clung. On the first view, the attribution points to what? To the ugly act they committed, which became the cause of their destruction; and on the second, it points to the type of punishment with which they were punished.
Alright, ﴿and the companions of the Rass and generations between them, many﴾ [al-Furqan 38]. ﴿And generations⁠﴾ is coordinated with what? Let us read the author's words: (﴿and the companions of the Rass⁠﴾: the name of a well. Their prophet is said to be Shu'ayb, and it is said to be someone else. They were sitting around it, so it collapsed with them and their dwellings).
The author restricted himself to what? To mentioning the manner of their destruction; they were attributed to the well because their destruction was by what was around it.
He said: ﴿and generations between them, many⁠﴾, (﴿and generations⁠﴾: peoples, ﴿between them, many⁠﴾; meaning between ʿAd and the companions of the Rass). Yes.
* Student: (...)?
* Sheikh: Yes, ﴿and ʿAd and Thamud and the companions of the Rass and generations between them﴾, this is what the author held. It is possible that the reference returns to what preceded, the people of Noah; meaning: from the people of Noah to the companions of the Rass were many generations that God Most High destroyed.
The author's statement: (﴿generations⁠﴾: peoples), as if he is saying that the intended meaning of "qarn" is the people and nation who lived in one age, and this is one of the opinions on "qarn": that it means the nation and group who were in one age and on one path, and they cite the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2652) and Muslim (2533/212), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him.]].
It is also said that "qarn" means a period of time, and they differed on its length: some said it is one hundred, which is the well-known view; some said one hundred and twenty; and some said eighty years.

These sayings that measure a generation by time are close to those that measure it by a community, because such a span of time usually sees the earlier people pass away and others come after them. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said near the end of his life: "On the head of a hundred years, none of those who are upon the face of the earth will remain"[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (601) and Muslim (2537/217) from Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the 'Isha' prayer one night near the end of his life. When he had finished the salam, he stood and said: "Do you see this night of yours? At the head of a hundred years from it, none of those who are upon the face of the earth will remain."]]. "On the head of a hundred years" indicates that a generation (qarn) is a hundred years.

But the context here shows that what is meant by "qurun" (generations) is nations. Is the destruction of generations a destruction of periods of time or of the people of those times?
* Student: Of the people of those times.
* The Shaykh: Of the people of the times. So the context of this verse shows that what is meant by the many "qurun" is nations. How many generations did Allah destroy between Noah and the People of ar-Rass! It has been related in the hadith narrated by Abu Dharr, which is hasan and authenticated by al-Hakim, that the number of the Messengers is three hundred and some over ten, the Messengers; as for the Prophets, they are many, one hundred and twenty-four thousand[[Narrated by Ahmad (22288) with his chain from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, how many were the Prophets? He said: "One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand; of them the Messengers were three hundred and fifteen, a large multitude."]]. This is a large number, so if most of the Messengers were denied, it means that the generations that were destroyed were many. The Prophet ﷺ saw visions and saw the Prophets: he saw a Prophet with a small group, a Prophet with a man or two, and a Prophet with no one with him[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5705) and Muslim (220/374) from Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The nations were displayed before me, and I saw a Prophet with a small group, a Prophet with a man or two, and a Prophet with no one with him..." the hadith.]], which indicates that most of the Prophets were denied in earlier times and only a few followed them.

Now Noah, as you know, remained among his people for nine hundred and fifty years. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud 40]. Consider this great period in which he struggled with them, debated them and argued with them, and they said: ﴿O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you promise us﴾ [Hud 32]. "We are not obeying you; whatever you have, bring it," and we seek refuge with Allah. This is what happened over this period.

If we struggle with one person in calling to Allah for a single minute, we consider it a long time, yes! Why did he not respond the first time? We say to him: the Messengers, peace be upon them, whom Allah promised victory: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. They struggle with their peoples, and then only a few of them believe.

The conclusion is that we say: these great and numerous generations were all destroyed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because they denied their messengers. Is He not able to destroy those who deny the Messenger? Yes, He is able, and this is what happened. But Allah made the destruction of the enemies of the Messenger ﷺ at the hands of the Messenger: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people (14) and remove the rage of their hearts﴾ [At-Tawbah 14, 15]. If the Quraysh had been destroyed by a punishment from Allah, would these great benefits have been achieved or not?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: No. For this reason, when your enemy is destroyed at your hands, it is more healing for you, is it not? And greater joy and happiness that Allah destroys him at your hand. As for when he is destroyed by a punishment from Allah, there is no doubt that Allah has spared you his evil, but his being destroyed at your hand is more eloquent and brings greater joy and happiness.

﴿And to each We presented examples, and to each We destroyed with complete destruction﴾ [Al-Furqan 39]. ﴿And to each We presented examples﴾: we will ask, why is ﴿kullan﴾ in the accusative when a noun that begins a sentence is a subject (mubtada')?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: Object.
* The Shaykh: What is the object?
* Student: ﴿Daraba﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, ﴿daraba lahu﴾. He would say "wa-kullin" (in the genitive), because ﴿lahu﴾ is a prepositional phrase (jar wa-majrur).
* Student: Referring to ﴿Nuh﴾.
* The Shaykh: No, meaning ﴿wa-qawma Nuhin﴾ [Al-Furqan 37] ﴿wa-kullan daraba﴾; that is not valid.
* Student: After ﴿wa-'Adan wa-Thamud wa-ashab al-Rass﴾ (...).
* The Shaykh: No.
* Student: Object of a later verb ﴿tabbarna﴾.
* The Shaykh: No; because ﴿tabbarna﴾ already has an object.

This is called the case of ishtighal (the verb occupied with a pronoun), and in ishtighal the verb is occupied with a pronoun referring to the noun before it, and the verb governs a dependent element. Here the verb after it cannot govern it, because the verb after it is transitive with a preposition, so we must estimate a suitable verb. The estimate: "wa-andhara kullan ﴿daraba lahu al-amthal﴾" ("and We warned each one, to whom We presented examples"), so it is the object of a deleted verb, and this is from the case of ishtighal.

The accusative is preferred here because it is conjoined to a verbal sentence, and among the preferences of the accusative in ishtighal is that it is conjoined to a verbal sentence.

(﴿And to each We presented examples﴾ in establishing the proof) ﴿daraba lahu al-amthal﴾ means: We made clear to him the examples, i.e., the incidents that Allah brought upon those before them. Every nation is warned by those before it, and examples are presented to it, and it is said: this is the example of the deniers, such-and-such happened to them. Allah warned every nation with complete warning, so that no proof remains for them, neither the nation of Muhammad ﷺ nor others.

(﴿And to each We presented examples﴾ in establishing the proof against them, so We do not destroy them except after warning) This is from the justice of Allah, the Exalted, because Allah is able to destroy His servants merely for their disobedience, since He has taken from them the covenant and the primordial or sensory pledge (on this there is difference of opinion) that He is their Lord and that they worship Him. Yet He does not destroy anyone except after sending the Messengers: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the Messengers﴾ [An-Nisa' 165]. Thus Allah did not leave the servants to their nature nor to the covenant He took from them, but sent to them messengers as bearers of good news and warners.

After this sending, does anyone retain a proof? No, not even those who argue by predestination can argue with it once the proof has been established against them by the Messengers. For this reason, if predestination were a proof, the sending of Messengers would not have eliminated it, since predestination exists alongside the presence of the Messengers. If predestination were a proof for the disobedient, the sending of Messengers would not be a proof over creation, because they would say: O our Lord, predestination exists even with the sending of the Messengers, so it is a proof for us. But since people have been warned and given signs, no Messenger came except that he was given what humanity could believe in on the basis of its like. All Messengers came not merely saying "I am a messenger, do such-and-such"; even if a person came and said "I am a messenger, do such-and-such" without bringing signs, people have the right to reject his words, saying: "Never, bring evidence that you are a messenger, or we will not accept."

Yet still, no Messenger came except that he brought a sign by which humanity could believe, and then they were warned. Shu'ayb, as we pointed out earlier, said to his people: ﴿Let not my dissension bring upon you what befell the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih﴾ [Hud 89]. Hud said to his people: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah﴾ [Al-A'raf 69], and Salih said to his people: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad﴾ [Al-A'raf 74]. So every Messenger presented examples to his people from those who came before them, and thus the proof is established.
