﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾, meaning: be concerned with asking about Him, and ask one who is aware. This is the *tadmin* (implicit meaning).

(The request that the one asked about be a serious matter that the questioner himself is not already concerned with. It is evident that the creation and the istiwa', after being mentioned, are not like that. As for what has been said, that the meaning is: "If you doubt it, then ﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾," with the address being to the Prophet ﷺ while the intended meaning is someone else, this is far from sound. Rather the meaning is: "If you wish to verify what was mentioned, or to explain in detail what was mentioned, then ﴿فَاسْأَلْ﴾, being concerned with it, ﴿خَبِيرًا﴾ one of great standing, encompassing the outward and inward aspects of matters, and that is Allah (...), who will reveal to you the clear truth of the matter." It was also said: ﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ﴾ means: whoever finds it in the earlier books..." to the end.)

What I understand now is that he wants to attach *bi* to an omitted element functioning as a circumstantial state (*hal*) of the subject of *is'al*: "Ask, being concerned with Him, one who is aware," or "ask, being concerned with Him, one who is aware." These are two possibilities. The first is that *bi* means *'an*, which is clear: "ask about Him one who is aware." The second is that it is attached to an omitted verb, whose estimated form is "being concerned with or caring about Him," a state (*hal*) from the implied pronoun in it: ﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾.

I also think there is a possibility that ﴿فَاسْأَلْ﴾ is answered by ﴿خَبِيرًا﴾, meaning that the request implicitly contains what indicates the answer, just as it was said about ﴿سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ﴾: "a questioner asked" and was answered "with a punishment that will surely befall." In that case the *bi* here is used instead of *'an*, because *'an* only indicates the mere request, whereas *bi* also indicates the answer.

In any case, the meaning is this: The Most Merciful, who created the heavens and the earth and rose over the Throne, ask about Him one who is aware, who will inform you. Then who is meant by this aware one whom Allah, the Exalted, has commanded us to ask?

So the meaning is: ask about Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, one who is aware of Him, and that is Himself. This is derived from the verse.

I say: *The benefits of these noble verses.* First: the affirmation that the heavens and the earth were created, and that they were previously non-existent. In this there is a refutation of the saying of the philosophers who claim that the celestial spheres are eternal (*qadim*), because what is created is not eternal. Note that "eternal" here is not in the linguistic sense but in the sense the philosophers intend by the term: that the eternal (*qadim*) is that which has no beginning and is not created. Did you understand? It does not mean the linguistic sense of *qidam* (antiquity), because in the language *qadim* means anything that is earlier, even if it is newly created, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿حَتَّى عَادَ كَالْعُرْجُونِ الْقَدِيمِ﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:39], "until it returned like an old date-stalk." But in the terminology of the philosophers, when they say *qadim*, they mean *azali* (without beginning), not created. We say: this verse refutes them, because Allah says: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾, "He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days."

* And in it also: evidence for what the author pointed out, that what the agent should observe is perfection and care in matters, so that the thing comes out in complete form, and the product comes out perfect.

* And in it also: evidence of the wisdom of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, in arranging matters according to their causes in the manner we have indicated: that its creation extended over six days, because things develop and are linked to specific causes that are completed within this period.

* And in it is evidence of the perfect power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. These heavens and earth and what is between them are great things that creation can never create, neither in six days nor in six thousand years, nor... it is impossible. Those who made the artificial satellites, when they first launched them, you know what great commotion and great honour resulted for those who made them, even though they are nothing compared to the smallest star in the sky, is that not so? Neither in essence, nor in size, nor in form, nor in power, nor in regularity; they will eventually pass away, their order will be disturbed and they will be destroyed.

The conclusion is that in the creation of the heavens and the earth, even in six days, even in those six days, there is evidence of the perfect power and greatness of Allah, blessed and exalted, because the greatness of the created thing indicates the greatness of the Creator, just as the greatness of an act in other than the Creator indicates the greatness, skill and power of the doer. For this reason, when people see a well-built structure, do they praise the structure or the builder?

**Students:** The builder.

**Shaykh:** Yes. They praise the builder first, and then the structure second. It is mentioned in the story of the debate (*hayda*) attributed to 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Kinani, if it is authentically from him, that one of those who debated him in the presence of the caliph criticized his appearance. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Kinani said to him: "You have not criticized me now; rather, you have criticized the Creator." Then he gave an example: if the wall near the caliph were deformed and leaning, and then the wall was blamed, on whom does the blame truly fall? On the builder, the one who built it. So a person's physical form is not of his own choosing, so he is not blamed for it.

For this reason, the hadiths that link blame to physical form, the blame is not for the form itself; rather it is evidence of what this form may carry of the attributes for which the servant is blamed. Because some hadiths mention blame, and then the scholars explain it with physical attributes; this is blame linked to a quality.

We say: if it is valid that the hadith is explained by these physical attributes, then it is not because of these physical attributes themselves, but because of what they usually contain of the person's actions or moral conduct; for a person is not blamed for what Allah created in him, but he is blamed for what was by his choice. Is it clear?

* And in this: evidence for the istiwa', the istiwa' of Allah over His Throne, from His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾, "then He rose over the Throne." And that istiwa' is one of the attributes of action (*sifat fi'liyyah*), not the essential attributes (*sifat dhatiyyah*), because it is ordered after the creation of the heavens, meaning it is newly occurring. Is the istiwa' before the creation of the heavens and the earth established or not established?

**Student:** Not established.

**Shaykh:** Huh?

**Shaykh:** The Throne was over the water.

**Shaykh:** We do not know; perhaps (...). So we say: concerning the istiwa' over the Throne before creation, we do not speak about it; Allah knows best about it. But the istiwa' over the Throne at the time of creation, does it exist or not? It does not exist, because that would contradict His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى﴾. As for before creation, the obligation is to remain silent about it, because that is not within our capacity, and Allah, the Exalted, did not inform us about it concerning Himself.

* And in it is evidence that the attribute of mercy is established for Allah, from His saying: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ﴾.

* And in it is evidence of the greatness of His attributes, blessed and exalted, from His saying: ﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾.

* And in it is also evidence, in the verse, that the attributes are tawqifiyyah (based on revelation alone, not on independent reasoning), from His saying: ﴿فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾. Meaning: the description of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, can only be according to what we have learned from Him. So we cannot describe Allah, the Exalted, with anything He has not described Himself with. For this reason the scholars said: the names and attributes of Allah are tawqifiyyah, and this is the correct and preferred view. It is not for us to describe Allah, the Exalted, with what He has not described Himself with, because that contradicts complete good manners toward Him. ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ [Al-Hujurat 49:1], "O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger." Just as we are not permitted to introduce anything new into His law, we are not permitted to describe Him with anything He has not described Himself with. And to Allah belongs the highest likeness. If a person is told: "Speak about a man who is absent," can he speak about any of his attributes? Except what is known of human attributes, such as saying: "He is a created human who lives and dies," and so on. But he may not speak about an attribute that is not among the general human attributes. How much more so with Allah, glory be to Him and exalted!

* Shaykh: Because the principle is that the address that comes in the Qur'an in the singular is for all people, unless evidence shows that it is specific to the Messenger. The Qur'an was revealed for everyone, so it addresses all, unless evidence indicates that it is specific to the Messenger, such as: ﴿Did We not expand your breast for you?﴾ [al-Sharh 1]. It is well known that this is specific to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him (ﷺ). Likewise: ﴿O Messenger, convey﴾ [al-Ma'idah 67], which explicitly addresses the Messenger alone. It indicates the greatness of that, and also of what we see between them: the sun, the moon, the stars and other things. The claim that these are within the heavens themselves has no evidence from the Book or the Sunnah. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that they are in an orbit (falak) between the sky and the earth, and reality also bears witness to this. They reached the moon, and if it were within the heaven itself, they would not have reached it, because Allah says: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ [al-Anbiya' 32]. If the sky is protected even from the most noble of messengers and the most noble of angels, except with permission, then those below them are all the more so.

* Student: Meaning they do not contain it?
* Shaykh: No, they do not contain it. What is contained is the direction. This will come to us, God willing, in: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾ [al-Furqan 61]. It is the same matter.

It has also been mentioned before that Allah, the Exalted, rose over His Throne, meaning He is exalted above it with a particular elevation, not like the absolute elevation of created beings. It is a particular elevation, and it is among the attributes of action (al-sifat al-fi'liyyah). Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) believe in this in the manner that befits Allah, glorified and exalted. They do not ask how (la yukayyifuna), and they do not attempt to ask how, because that is impossible.

It has also been mentioned before that the attribution of the istiwa' (rising) to the Most Merciful: ﴿Then He rose over the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 59], indicates that although He, exalted be He, is above all His creation, His mercy encompasses all creation. His elevation is unlike the elevation of others, which when they rise, they become tyrannical and arrogant and deal with harshness and severity.

Likewise, it has been stated before that it is derived from His saying: ﴿then ask about Him one who is informed﴾ [al-Furqan 59], that knowledge of Allah is sought only from Allah, from the One who is informed about Him, who is Allah, glorified and exalted. This verse also testifies to what Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah hold: that the names and attributes of Allah are tawqifiyyah (based on revelation only). It is not permissible for anyone to affirm of them except what Allah and His Messenger have affirmed.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 60:

Then Allah the Exalted said, after mentioning His greatness and His lordship in creating the heavens and the earth and His istiwa' (settling) upon His Throne: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. The author said: (to the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿"Prostrate to the Most Merciful." They say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ [al-Furqan 60]).

This prostration may refer to the specific prostration, which is a person falling down upon his seven limbs, or it may refer to the general prostration, which is absolute submission. This is because prostration (sujud) is used in two senses: the general prostration, which is submission and humility in every form, and the specific prostration upon these well-known limbs.

When they were told this, they said: ﴿And what is the Most Merciful?﴾, thus denying the One to whom prostration is directed. Then they became arrogant about prostrating: ﴿Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?﴾. This interrogative is an interrogative of denial and disbelief: ﴿Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?﴾. The first, ﴿And what is the Most Merciful?﴾, is an interrogative of denial, meaning that they deny the Most Merciful. By their denial of the Most Merciful is meant the denial of this name, not the denial of Allah. That is, they denied the name but not the essence. They believe in Allah: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [al-Zukhruf 87]. However, they denied the Most Merciful. They denied this name of Allah, the Exalted, and said: "We do not know the Most Merciful except the Most Merciful of al-Yamamah"[[Ibn Abi Hatim recorded in his Tafsir (15305) from 'Ata': ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ [al-Furqan 60]: "We do not know the Most Merciful except the Most Merciful of al-Yamamah." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾ [al-Baqarah 163].]]. They knew of no one named "the Most Merciful" except this one described as the Most Merciful of al-Yamamah. Thus they denied this great attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, which is one of His greatest attributes and greatest names, namely the mercy that encompasses all creatures. This denial has no basis, because once something has been established through revelation, there is no justification for denying it on the grounds that they do not know it. A person who believes only in what he knows, is he a believer in the messengers or a follower of his own desire?

* Student: A follower of his desire.

* Shaykh: A follower of his desire. The one who believes only in what he knows. Among this is what some common people do today. When a sunnah that has been killed off is revived, they say: "What is this? This is a new religion; we do not accept it and do not want it!" We say to these people that they resemble those disbelievers in some respects, in that they deny what they do not know and say: "We do not accept it. Where are the scholars regarding this religion? Where is so-and-so? Where is so-and-so?" This is not a proof, because the truth must be accepted, and a person's desire must follow the truth, not the truth following his desire: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71]. When a believer sees or hears something he does not know, it is obligatory upon him to verify it. It is true that a person finds unfamiliar things strange, but it is obligatory upon him in such a case not to deny them. It is obligatory upon him to verify and to know the source of this thing. As for saying, "You have brought a new religion and we do not accept it," this is not so. Rather, the one who revives a sunnah (the Prophetic way) is the one who brings the old religion, and whoever opposes the sunnah is the one who brings the new, innovated religion. As for the sunnah, it is the old religion upon which the Messenger ﷺ and his companions were.

The summary is that you hardly find any act of disobedience without some resemblance to a form of disbelief. You hardly find any act of disobedience that does not have a counterpart of disbelief of the same kind.

﴿Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. This is also denial and arrogance, meaning: how can we prostrate to what you order us? He said: (It is read with the fawqaniyyah and the tahtaniyyah, and the one who orders is Muhammad ﷺ).

Regarding His saying ﴿Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?﴾, is the word "ma" here in the sense of "man" (who), or is "ma" a masdariyyah (verbal particle)? That is, is the meaning "to the one whom you order us to prostrate to," making it a relative pronoun in the sense of "man," or is it a masdariyyah, meaning "to your command"?

* Student: Both.

* Shaykh: Both cannot be intended together.

* Student: I think both are possible.

* Shaykh: Both are possible. The commentator says "and we do not know him," which indicates that "ma" is a relative noun, meaning: "to the one whom you order us to prostrate to, and we do not know him." According to his interpretation, "ma" would be in the sense of "man." In that case, using "ma" instead of "man" for non-inanimate beings, or for beings that do not reason, as they say, goes against the original usage, because the original usage is to refer to rational beings with "man," not with "ma." "Ma" is only used to draw attention to a quality, such as His saying: ﴿So marry those women who are good for you among the women﴾ [al-Nisa' 3]. He did not say "man tāba" (those who are good). So what is this thing?

We say: in ﴿So marry what is good for you among women﴾, He does not mean a particular woman, so as to refer to her with "man." Rather He means the category of those who are married for their goodness. Thus He considers the attribute and not the one described, and for this reason He used "ma": ﴿So marry what is good for you﴾.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: This (...) is for generality, as a matter of emphasis.

Likewise here: ﴿to what you order us﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. If we take "ma" to mean "man," we say: they shifted from the one described to pointing to the attribute, because they deny this attribute, which is "the Most Merciful." It is as if they said: "Shall we prostrate to an unknown, unidentified command, which is what you order us to prostrate to?"

As for "ma" being a masdariyyah, the matter is very clear. It is as if they are saying: "Shall we prostrate to your command, when you are nothing in our eyes?" For they said: ﴿Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them﴾ [al-Furqan 41-42]. So here they combined denial and arrogance: denial of an attribute of Allah and a name of His, then denial of what they were ordered to prostrate to, then arrogance toward the command of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Shall we prostrate to that which you order us?﴾ [al-Furqan 60].

(﴿And it increases them﴾, this speech to them, ﴿in aversion﴾ [al-Furqan 60] from faith), and we seek refuge in Allah!

That is, it did not increase them in acceptance or compliance, but rather increased them in aversion. In this is evidence that the duty of the caller (da'i) is to call to Allah, whether the one called complies or turns away. Some people have asked: "If this person, when I call him, becomes more averse and hateful toward the Shariah and what it commands, is it permissible for me to call him, or is it forbidden for me to call him, because I become the cause of his aversion and arrogance? His aversion and arrogance are greater than his mere disobedience. What is your opinion on this question? Or did you not understand the question?"

* Student: Yes, we did.

* Shaykh: He says: "When I call my brother or my uncle or my father, he becomes more averse and arrogant, so I become the cause of his arrogance, his aversion, and his hatred of the truth. That is greater than mere disobedience or abandoning an obligation. So should I leave him, or should I call him, and then consider myself in difficulty that I was the cause of him falling into this great matter?" So what do we say?

* Student: He calls him.

* Student: (...) an act commanded, as long as (...), then how does he (...)? The outcome is not something to be upset about.

* Shaykh: Meaning, it means he commands him (...)?

* Student: He commands him, and guidance is in the hand of Allah.

* Student: (...) he may respond to this and not respond to that.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. Even if he responds, even if there is aversion toward the person himself, he does not abandon the call.

* Student: I see that if, for example, (...) is greater than his righteousness or his call.

* Shaykh: Yes, but now, with what we have: Allah says regarding the Messenger ﷺ, ﴿and it increases them in aversion﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. When the Messenger ﷺ saw these people increasing in aversion, did he abandon the call?

* Student: Absolutely not, but he abandoned it for these people.

* Shaykh: No, he never abandoned it for these people.

* Student: Alright, if it is for a disobedient person, then his call may be permitted. If disbelief reaches the point of speech of disbelief and words of disbelief, then he is left alone.

* Shaykh: No. What we see is that you must call.

* Student: In general?

* Shaykh: In general. And ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 272]. Because if you remain silent about him, he will become accustomed to disobedience and will not see it as disobedience, and he will not become upright. Then he may also become arrogant, but afterward he may return and take account of himself. A word said for the sake of Allah must have an effect. Every word said for the sake of Allah must have a tremendous effect. We are not far from the repetition of the matter of Musa, peace be upon him, when he spoke to all the people and especially to the magicians. He said to them: ﴿Woe to you! Do not invent against Allah a lie, or He will destroy you with a punishment. Indeed, he fails who invents﴾ [Ta-Ha 61]. This is a great speech, meaning: a deterring speech, a warning and a threat. Yet did it have an effect or not?

* Student: It had an effect.

* Shaykh: It had an effect.

* Student: ﴿So they disputed their affair among themselves﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿So they disputed their affair among themselves﴾ [Ta-Ha 62]. The fa' indicates sequence and consequence. That is, this dispute was provoked by this word, like what they call the bomb that divided them. So do not think that the word you say for Allah will be wasted in vain. It must have an effect, and although this effect may not appear at the present time, it will certainly have an effect.

They said: (﴿And it increases them﴾, this speech to them, ﴿in aversion﴾ [al-Furqan 60] from faith).

* Student: Shaykh.

* Shaykh: Yes (...) to the point that they placed the entrails of a slaughtered camel on his head while he was prostrating [[Al-Bukhari, in his wording (3854), and Muslim (1794/107), from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: While the Prophet ﷺ was prostrating, and around him were some people from Quraysh, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came with the entrails of a camel, and threw it upon the back of the Prophet ﷺ. He did not raise his head, until Fatimah, peace be upon her, came and removed it from his back, and invoked curses upon the one who did it. The hadith.]], and to the point that they threw filth and excrement at his threshold. Yes, this is not right. And if you believe in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the outcome is for the righteous﴾ [Hud 49], this will not harm you. The outcome is for the righteous. I told you before, I said: the success of the call refers to the success of the category, not of the individual. You may not succeed personally and die without attaining your goal, but the discussion concerns the call, that it succeeded and had an effect, and this must happen. We said this before. Is this clear?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Then read the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an, sent down progressively﴾ [al-Insan 23]. What comes after it? He did not say: "So be thankful for the blessing of your Lord for this sending down." He said: ﴿So be patient﴾ [al-Insan 24]. This means that whoever bears this Qur'an, whether it was revealed to him or he memorized it, will surely face what he faces, whether in relation to his own self, which commands evil and opposes this revelation, or in relation to others. As for these matters, they are truly cowardice and from Satan: ﴿It is only the Shaytan who frightens his allies, so do not fear them but fear Me, if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran 175].

We say this and affirm it, even though we ourselves fall short. Yet it is necessary to explain the truth, and the shortcoming is in truth upon ourselves. But we believe that the caller to Allah, and indeed the scholar whom Allah has given knowledge, must spread it and call to it, or else it becomes a proof against him.

* Student: And do they only dislike it outwardly, Shaykh?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Perhaps they only dislike it outwardly, and what is in their souls of envy, or what is in their souls of aversion to opposing their desires, leads them to oppose him outwardly, even if their hearts love him. This may also be the case.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: In any case, the matter is this: if you are struck by harm while remaining upright, this is for the elevation of your ranks. And if you are struck by harm while not being upright, that is, through an error in the path of the call, by not using the wisdom, good admonition and argument in the best manner that Allah has guided to, then this harm will be an expiation for your sins that you committed. So in any case you will necessarily be afflicted with harm, but it is either an elevation of ranks or an expiation of sins.

* Student: (...). Those who do not agree that a person should always be a caller say, for example: "How can we call people while we are unable to reform ourselves?"

* Shaykh: If you do not call people, you have corrupted yourself by your own choice, because from reforming yourself is calling to Allah. So if you do not call to Allah, you have corrupted yourself by your own choice (...). Fear Allah as much as you can. As for abandoning an obligation because you are abandoning another obligation, that is not correct. It is undoubtedly a lack of good manners and a lack of wisdom for a person to call to a matter while he himself is engaged in the opposite of what he commands:

Do not forbid a trait and then commit its like; it is a great shame upon you if you do so.

But this does not mean that you should abandon the obligation. Strive to reform others and to reform their affairs.

﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾ [al-Furqan 61].

(﴿Tabāraka﴾ [al-Furqan 61] means "exalted in greatness"). It has already been noted that one should not limit its meaning to "exalted," for it also indicates the abundance and vastness of its goodness, because these constellations (burūj) that will be mentioned contain benefit, welfare and advantage for people, befitting this description: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations﴾.

The word (tabāraka) is an intensive form derived from "barakah" (blessing), by the addition of the letter tā' (ta). It is said of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the common people among us say it of other than Allah. They say: "Tabāraka 'alaynā" and similar expressions. Some people say that this description is specific to Allah, and that one may not say to a human being "tabārakta." However, what we see is that there is no harm in it, because people intend by "tabārakta" that Allah has placed blessing in you, not that it is an intrinsic blessing. There is no harm in it, and what matters is the meaning; if the wording contains no legally prohibited element, then there is no harm in it.

As for His saying ﴿alladhī ja'ala fī al-samā'i burūjan﴾: is (ja'ala) here in the sense of ṣayyara (to make) or in the sense of waḍa'a (to place)?

It is in the sense of waḍa'a (to place). On this basis it is transitive to one object, which is His saying ﴿burūjan﴾, the plural of burj. The burj originally means a lofty, elevated building, and these burūj that include the stars are in reality like towering, high buildings, because of their height.

As for his saying (twelve): this is an apposition (badal) to ﴿burūjan﴾.

(Twelve: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces), twelve constellations.

The author began with Aries because it is the time of the equinox of spring; when the sun enters the first day of the sign of Aries, night and day become equal in spring at the beginning of the sign of Aries, meaning the night is twelve hours and the day is twelve hours.

Three signs: (Aries, Taurus, Gemini). When Gemini is completed and Cancer begins, the night ends in its shortness and the day in its length (?), meaning that the sun reaches the northern signs after the three (Aries, Taurus, Gemini), and then afterwards the sun turns toward the south.

(Cancer, Leo, Virgo): these are three. When the three have passed, night and day become equal in autumn after the end of the length of the day. Have you understood now?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Good. (Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius): when these three end, the length of the night ends and the shortness of the day ends.

Then the sun returns through (Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces); when Pisces ends, night and day become equal in spring.

People have differed over whether one should begin with Aries, because it is the best time of the year, since it contains the spring equinox, or begin with Libra, because it is the time when the day ends in shortness and the night in length?

* Student: It is the equinox, Shaykh.

* Shaykh: The equinox of autumn.

The well-known, famous and most common view, which the author followed, is that one begins with the sign containing the spring equinox. But some people begin with the other point and claim that this is the method of the Arabs, and Allah knows best. What I see is that most calendars begin with this. It is said that the Arabs begin from the autumn equinox, and the non-Arabs (ʿajam) begin from the spring equinox. That the non-Arabs begin from the spring equinox is clear, because today the non-Arabs, Iran and (...), date the beginning of the year from Aries; they have solar years and begin them with the sign of Aries.

The author says: (They are the stations of the seven wandering planets: Mars, which has Aries and Scorpio; Venus, which has Taurus and Libra; Mercury, which has Gemini and Virgo; the Moon, which has Cancer; the Sun, which has Leo; Jupiter, which has Sagittarius and Pisces; and Saturn, which has Capricorn and Aquarius.)

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. In any case, I do not know the reasoning behind this last division, and I am not aware of it. But these burūj the sun traverses in the year, as we heard shortly, and the moon traverses them in the month; every month the moon crosses these burūj, and it has twenty-eight stations (manāzil) that encompass these twelve burūj. As for the sun, it traverses them in a year.

That these burūj indicate their greatness is shown by Allah's saying ﴿Tabāraka alladhī ja'ala﴾. His saying ﴿fī al-samā'﴾ [al-Furqan 61]: what is meant is height, not the protected ceiling; rather it is height, because these burūj are below it.

(﴿And He placed in it also﴾ ﴿a lamp (sirājan)﴾, which is the sun, ﴿and a luminous moon﴾ [al-Furqan 61]. In another reading, burujan is in the plural, meaning luminous bodies (nayyirāt). He singled out the moon from among them for mention.)

* Student: ﴿Surujan﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿Surujan﴾, yes, ﴿surujan﴾, correct. (﴿Surujan﴾ in the plural, meaning luminous bodies.)

* Student: Mine has ﴿sirājan﴾.

* Shaykh: No, ﴿sirājan﴾ is what is in the Qur'an.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: And what is in the original?

* Student: Likewise.

* Shaykh: No, (﴿And He placed in it﴾) in the original?

* Student: (﴿And He placed in it also﴾ ﴿sirājan﴾).

* Shaykh: Yes. The second one: (﴿surujan﴾ in the plural), plural: surujun.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes.

On this reading (He singled out the moon from among them for mention for a kind of virtue).

﴿And He placed in it a lamp﴾, meaning surujan, ﴿and a luminous moon﴾. He says: it is coordinated (ʿaṭf) upon surujan, and it is among them (for a kind of virtue). But on the singular reading, the sirāj is the sun, and it is called a sirāj while the moon is called munīr, because the sun's light is intrinsic and hot, while the moon's light is acquired from the sun; so it is not in itself a sirāj, but rather it is luminous (munīr) or a light (nūr), though its light is acquired.

On the reading ﴿surujan﴾, the author says: (meaning luminous bodies), and the moon is among them, luminous, but he singled it out for a kind of virtue.

If we say that the moon is among them, meaning the sun is among them too, or not? The sun is the mother of the lamps, in reality.

* Student: Do we have (li-nawʿi faḍīlatihi)?

* Shaykh: What I have is (faḍīla) with the tā', it is suitable; what we have is better.

* Student: (faḍīlatihi)?

* Shaykh: No, I have only (faḍīla).

I say: the author's statement, may Allah have mercy on him, is open to examination. But the coordination of the luminous moon upon the lamps is coordination of two different things (ʿaṭf al-mutaghāyirayn), not coordination of the specific upon the general. The moon is not from the lamps. ﴿And He made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾ [Nuh 16]. The sun is undoubtedly a lamp, but the moon is a light; therefore it is not among them, and there is no need for the answer the author mentioned: (he singled out the moon for a kind of virtue). Rather we say: this is not a matter of specification, but of coordinating what? Two different things.

But on the plural reading, ﴿And He placed in it lamps﴾ indicates that the other stars besides the sun have heat and also illumination, but they do not reach the earth. Why?

* Student: Because of their distance.

* Shaykh: Because of distance; they do not reach the earth because of distance. But this verse indicates that they have heat and illumination.

The lamps and the luminous moon were mentioned together with the burūj because the burūj are stations (manāzil) and these things are those that descend (nāzila) upon them; so He mentioned the stations and what descends upon them together, and both indicate the great signs of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, which no one can match.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 62:

(...) Then he said: (﴿And it is He who made the night and the day succeeding each other﴾, meaning each of them succeeds the other, ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾ [al-Furqan 62], with the shaddah and without it [yadhdhakkar and yadhkur]) "yadhdhakkar" and "yadhkur" (as previously mentioned, whoever missed some good in one of them may do it in the other), ﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾ [al-Furqan 62], meaning, grateful for his Lord's blessing upon him in both).

﴿And it is He who made the night and the day succeeding each other﴾. The pronoun in His words ﴿And it is He who﴾ refers back to ﴿He who placed in the sky constellations﴾ [al-Furqan 61]. That is, among His signs and blessings is that He made the night and the day succeed one another, meaning each of them replaces the other. This succession (khilfah) has an extremely great benefit, indeed two great benefits: first, remembrance and admonition; and second, gratitude for the blessing.

As for remembrance, the author says: (whoever missed some good in one of them may do it in the other). This is indeed a kind of remembrance. But among remembrance is that you recall through it the power of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He brings the night in place of the day and the day in place of the night. Even if all of creation gathered to change this order, bringing night instead of day or the reverse, they would not be able to do so.

Second, among what you remember through this night and day is death and life: ﴿And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day﴾ [al-An'am 60]. In reality, when a person rises from sleep at night, he feels as if he has been created anew. If a person imagined that the whole time were day or the whole time were night, this renewed vitality that comes to him every day would not occur, and he would not feel that he had entered a new life. For this reason Allah the Exalted called it resurrection: ﴿Then He resurrects you therein﴾ [al-An'am 60]. So you remember resurrection after death.

Likewise, among what one remembers and is admonished by is the remembrance of the absolute fact of resurrection and that Allah is able to do it. One remembers that there must be an awakening after the sleep, and that is on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 52]. This must happen, because it is the sunnah of Allah. But the Day of Resurrection is one day with no night in it; it remains always as it is.

Likewise, what the author mentioned of practical remembrance: if a person forgets an act of worship at night, he makes it up during the day, or if during the day he did not repent, he repents at night. "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent, and extends His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent"[[Narrated by Muslim (2759/31), and Ahmad, and the wording is his (19619), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]], and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when sleep or illness overcame him, would make up in the day what he used to pray at night[[Ahmad (26058) narrated that Abu al-Darda' used to tell the people that there is no witr for one who reaches the dawn. A group of believers went to 'A'ishah and informed her, and she said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would reach the morning and then perform witr.]]. This too is practical remembrance.

As for ﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾, is the "or" here for division and classification? That is, is this a counterpart to the first, so that it is mani'at al-jam' (exclusive in the sense of not combined), or is it mani'at al-khuluw (permitting combination)?

* Student: Mani'at al-khuluw (...).

* Shaykh: Is it mani'at al-khuluw or mani'at al-jam'?

* Student: All of it is mani'at al-khuluw.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, mani'at al-khuluw. Mani'at al-jam' means that if the first exists, the second is precluded; if one of them exists. But mani'at al-khuluw means that either this exists, or that, or both.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾. Can both be combined?

* Student: No, they cannot be combined.

* Shaykh: Then it is mani'at al-khuluw.

﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾: that is, whoever wishes to thank his Lord for His blessing upon him in this day and night, he is permitted to do so. There is no doubt that whoever remembers Allah's blessing in this night and day must thank Allah. The night is calm and tranquil, and everything sleeps and is still, so sleep is sweet and pleasurable and complete rest is attained; this is a great blessing. In the day, the reverse holds: a person is full of activity, strength, and desire for earning and work, and so he increases in thanks to Allah the Exalted for this blessing. This place is not sufficient to encompass what a person may conceive of Allah's blessing upon him through this night and day. A person sometimes, upon reflection and contemplation, is granted a clearer understanding of Allah's blessing than what we say or are able to say. Even if a person stays awake one night, the blessing of Allah the Exalted upon people through this night and this day would become clear to him.

﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 63 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63].

(Ar-Rahman, the Most Merciful) It is repeated in very close verses. How many times? Three times now: ﴿Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 59], ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ [al-Furqan 60], and the third here: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63]. Then the whole surah opens with the Qur'an: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾ [al-Furqan 1], which indicates that the revelation of this Qur'an is from the mercy of Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: The correct view is that he does not make it up in its own form, and that he adds to it (shafa'a, i.e., makes it even).
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, because this hadith is established in Muslim.
* Student: Is it called witr?
* Shaykh: No, it is called qada' (making up a missed prayer). But the origin of witr is: "Make the last of your prayers at night witr (odd)" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (472) and Muslim (751/151) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. The night prayer has now ended, so there is no benefit in witr now; but whatever a person used to worship his Lord with, he should love not to miss it.
* Student: And if he left it, when he loved it?
* Shaykh: If he left it, what (...).
* Student: (...)?
* Shaykh: No, he did not leave it deliberately; he left it through forgetfulness. Making it up is easier than doing it. But even so, we say: a person whose habit is to pray witr with three should not pray four, and let him remember, when his soul tells him, "Do not do this act of obedience," that he needs it, does he not? He needs it a great need.
* Student: ﴿And He grants protection, and none can be granted protection against Him, if you know. They will say, "It is for Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun 88, 89].
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The question is addressed to whom, and the answer is ﴿Lillah (It is for Allah)﴾?
* Shaykh: There are two readings here. This reading you recited is the one in the Mushaf, and there is a second, seven-fold reading: ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾. ﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things, and He grants protection and none can be granted protection against Him, if you know." They will say, "Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun 88, 89]. As for the first: ﴿Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?" They will say, "To Allah."﴾ [al-Mu'minun 84, 85]. That is, the first, ﴿They will say, "To Allah,"﴾ is agreed upon by both readings, because the question is ﴿To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it?﴾. The second, ﴿Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 86], has two readings in the answer: ﴿They will say, "To Allah"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 87], and a second seven-fold reading: ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾. The third also: ﴿Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 88], the answer: ﴿They will say, "To Allah"﴾ [al-Mu'minun 89], or ﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾
As for ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾, there is no difficulty in it, or is there?
* Student: Yes.

Good. In the verse, yes?

And in it is also a proof, I think, that it is not permissible for a person to judge the truth by its speaker; rather the truth is known by the truth, not by the speaker. Good. Also here: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. There is a reading here, he says: (with the feminine and the masculine prefix), two seven-fold readings.

But according to the reading ﴿to what you command us﴾, here it is specified, and by "what you command us" they mean whom? The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾ So what is the wisdom in his expressing the first with generality: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful"﴾, leaving the speaker vague because of its generality, while here He said: ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾
* Student: (...).
