Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 63 (part 2 of 2):

* The student: This is the position of the disbelievers, then?
* The Shaykh: No. These disbelievers have now denied two things. They denied prostration, saying: ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾ [al-Furqan 60], as if they were saying: "If the command had come from someone other than you, we would consider it." The second is their denial of the Most Merciful: ﴿And what is the Most Merciful?﴾ [al-Furqan 60]. Does every disbeliever deny the Most Merciful? We do not know.
* The student: A hadith (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The student: It indicates (...).
* The Shaykh: Correct, but is it because of what was mentioned, or because of its strong effect on them? That is, when the threat came first and it was mentioned: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away, and gave a little and then withheld?﴾ [al-Najm 33-34], and before it also the censure of the idols... and so on to the end. Then the attributes of Allah came: ﴿And that it is He who enriches and suffices﴾ [al-Najm 48]. Then the threat came with the mention of the examples of the earlier nations. It is as if this (Qur'an) had seized their minds, so that they forgot what they were upon, until they forgot (...).
It is well known that the Messenger used to recite, and Abu Bakr used to recite, and the children and women among the disbelievers would come to Abu Bakr to listen to his recitation, and they would also hear the recitation of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.
* A student: (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, they would come out, because the Messenger would convey it and the Companions would convey it.
* The student: O Shaykh, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira (...)?
* The Shaykh: I do not know. What I know is: I adjure you by Allah and by kinship.
* The student: Or: I adjure you by Allah and by kinship.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Alright, does that mean that when he acknowledged (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: Would al-Walid ibn al-Mughira have continued on this (...)?
* The Shaykh: No, never (...).
* * *
* Student: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace." [63] And those who spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing. [64] And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever adherent. [65] Indeed, it is evil as an abode and a station. [66] And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, justly moderate."﴾ [al-Furqan 63-67].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [al-Furqan 63].
It has passed earlier that Allah the Exalted praised Himself through His great creations: the constellations (al-buruj) that He placed in the sky, because of what they contain of indication of His power and of His mercy toward His servants. Likewise the moon and the sun, and in them are benefits for the servants, religious and worldly, that are well known. The moon, Allah the Exalted made it a measure of time for the Hajj, for fasting, for the terms of people's sales, purchases, debts, and other things. The sun also has many benefits, such as ripening fruits, the alternation of night and day, the seasons, and others.
Then He explained that He, glorified and exalted, ﴿made the night and the day alternating﴾, each succeeding the other. But this sign benefits only the one who ﴿desires to remember or desires gratitude﴾ [al-Furqan 62]. ﴿Remember﴾ means remembering the signs of Allah, glorified and exalted, and the indication toward what is greater than resurrection and rising on the Day of Judgment: for night and sleep are like death, and day and waking are like resurrection. As for gratitude, since this alternation between night and day includes what it includes of the benefits of the servants, it becomes obligatory upon the servant to thank Allah, glorified and exalted, for His blessing in that.
Then Allah, glorified and exalted, after mentioning what came before about the polytheists who argued with the Messenger ﷺ and denied him, who did not benefit from the signs of Allah and did not believe in Him nor in His Messenger, explained. He concluded this surah by mentioning those who were in opposition to these. Thus the Qur'an, Allah made it mathani (oft-repeated), in which opposing meanings and similar meanings are repeated. Therefore, whenever you find that Allah mentions the Fire, He mentions the Garden; and when He mentions the Garden, He mentions the Fire; and when He mentions the attributes of the people of the Fire, He mentions the attributes of the people of the Garden. And so on, because it is mathani. This is from wisdom: for when a person sees the Fire and the attributes of its people, that may lead him to despair of Allah's mercy, so there follows the mention of the Garden and its people, and he becomes enlivened and hopes for the mercy of Allah, glorified and exalted; and the reverse is the same. It is known to a person that if he is upon one uniform state, boredom and weariness overtake him; but when his states vary and the address varies, he becomes energetic.
* Student: How (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, this is for the reason we mentioned.
* The student: That is, it did not begin with describing the believers (...).
* The Shaykh: That is according to what suits the context. Sometimes it begins with the Garden and sometimes with the Fire, according to what the context requires. Generally, when it mentions the attributes of one group, it mentions the attributes of the other, so that the person is neither complacent nor despairing of the mercy of Allah, and neither secure from His plan.

He said: (﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 63] is a subject (mubtada'), and what follows it are its attributes up to (﴿those will be rewarded﴾), without the interrupting element in it.)

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾: "ibad" is the plural of "abd" (servant). He attributed them to the Most Merciful as an indication that this servitude with which they are characterized is one of the effects of Allah's mercy, and that Allah, the Exalted, showed them mercy until they became His servants.

In the attribution there is also another meaning: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾ are servants who worship Allah in hope of His mercy, not worshipping for show or reputation. So the attribution has two aspects. One of them?

* Student: The first is an attribution of honour, and that they are devoted worshippers of Allah, the Exalted, so they are servants who comply with His command.
* The Shaykh: You were not present; the reality is that you were not present.
* Student: That this worship came about by Allah's grace and mercy.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that their being servants of Allah is from the effect of His mercy. This is one.
* The student: The second is that they worshipped the Most Merciful hoping for His mercy (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, that they worship Allah hoping for His mercy: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾, meaning the servants who worship Allah hoping for His mercy, and by His mercy they also worshipped Him.
So this is the aspect of the attribution from two sides: from the side that their worship of Allah was among the requirements of His mercy, and from another side that by this worship they hope for the mercy of their Lord, not hoping by it for worldly gain or to ward off blame from themselves, but they hope by this for the mercy of Allah: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾.
* Student: There is praise in it (...).
* The Shaykh: No, yes, but our intention was the attribution, the attribution to the Most Merciful. He did not say "servants of Allah" or "servants of the Lord" or the like.

Is this servitude general or specific?
* Student: Specific.
* The Shaykh: Specific, because what is meant by it is the servitude of the Shari'ah (religious law), and the servitude of the Shari'ah is specific to the one who brings the Shari'ah. As for the general, it is the servitude of destiny (qadar), which is submission to the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and this is general: every person is subject to the decree of Allah, glorified and exalted, and none can be beyond it.

As for the author's statement: ("a subject and what follows it are its attributes"), meaning: the predicate is ﴿those will be rewarded the high chamber﴾ [al-Furqan 75], there is scrutiny in it. Rather, the correct view is that "wa-'ibad" is the subject and "alladhina" is its predicate, and what follows is coordinated to it. That is: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ up to the end [al-Furqan 63], and ﴿those will be rewarded the high chamber﴾ becomes a resumed sentence (jumla mustaʼnafa) explaining their recompense and reward. That is because if we proceed as the author said, it would require separating the subject and predicate by long intervening phrases with no need for them, and the statement would remain incomplete until the end of ﴿those will be rewarded the high chamber for what they endured﴾ [al-Furqan 75].

So the correct view is that ﴿wa-'ibad﴾ is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿alladhina yamshuna 'ala al-ardi hawnan﴾.

He said: (﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63], i.e., with tranquility and humility.)

﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ is more eloquent than "the walkers upon the earth in humility," because a verbal sentence indicates occurrence and renewal; that is, those who, in the state of their walking, walk upon the earth in humility.

In the definition of the subject and predicate there is evidence of restriction (hasr), as is well known in the rules: when the subject and predicate are both definite, that is evidence of restriction, meaning that the servants of the Most Merciful are these people.

﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾: the author says "with tranquility and humility," meaning their walk is not the walk of a person (...) who is not composed, but their walk is a walk of composure, humbly, without haste. This does not contradict what is established from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he used to walk with strength and vigour, "as if he were descending from a slope"[[Recorded by Ahmad (947) from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.]]; that was due to his strength, and this is not from the category of haste that (...). So there is a difference between a person who walks like the walk of a foolish, ungracious madman, and a person who walks with strength but a composed walk. The first is blameworthy and the second praiseworthy, because it indicates energy and strength, is more restful for the body, and quicker in reaching the goal, as the Messenger ﷺ used to do.

Then, is this walking the physical walking, or does it include both physical and figurative walking?
* Student: Both physical and figurative.
* The Shaykh: The answer: it includes both together, even the figurative walk, by the evidence of His saying: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [al-Furqan 63], and this is from the humility of the figurative walk: that when the ignorant address them, they do not hasten to respond with their ignorance, but they say "peace."

He says: (﴿And when the ignorant address them﴾ with what they dislike, ﴿they say, "Peace."﴾ [al-Furqan 63], i.e., words by which they are safe from sin), and the intent is not "peace" meaning the greeting "peace be upon you"; that is why the verb governs it in the accusative. Had the intent been the greeting formula, it would have said "salamun." Rather, the intent, as the author said, is "a word, peace," i.e., ("by which they are safe from sin"), and from excessive abuse. For when a man answers the ignorant in kind, the ignorant person has no limit, restrained by neither law nor reason; if he says one word, he is answered with two or ten. But if he is intelligent, faithful, and composed, he says a word by which he is safe from sin and from harm. This speech preserves a person's dignity, for it does not say that they remain silent; rather it says ﴿they say﴾, a saying; there must be speech, but it is speech by which they are safe from the harm of this ignorant person and from his sin, and they defend themselves, so the ignorant person does not consider them cowards, nor do they appear to be what he says if they stay silent; for if they remain silent while able to object, that indicates they accept what they are described with. Response is necessary, but as Allah the Exalted said: with a word by which a person is safe from sin.

﴿They say, "Peace"﴾: what is an example of it?
* Student: (...).
* Student: If he is ignorant, for example.
* The Shaykh: That is, for example, if he says to him: "You are a sinner, you are a thief, you are a liar, you are such-and-such"?
* Student: No.
* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...) he says: "If you are truthful, may Allah forgive me and have mercy on me, and if you are lying, may Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful," or as he said.
* The Shaykh: Yes. The point is that we cannot specify it, because its specification returns to the state or the situation in which the person finds himself.

(﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا﴾ jama' sājid (prostrating), ﴿وَقِيَامًا﴾ [al-Furqan 64] bi-ma'na qā'imīn (standing)) i.e. (they pray during the night).

(They pray during the night.) He derived this from His saying: ﴿يَبِيتُونَ﴾ (they spend the night).

﴿يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا﴾: this is coordinated with what came before.

In His saying ﴿يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا﴾, the fronting of the object or the complement (taqdīm al-ma'mūl aw al-muta'alliq) indicates restriction (ḥaṣr). That is, they do not prostrate for show (riyā', ostentation) or for reputation (sum'ah), but they prostrate to Allah alone ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾.

In their saying ﴿لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾ rather than "for Allah," there is an indication that they intend by this prostration the reward of Allah and His good pleasure, because the Rabb (Lord) is the Owner who disposes of affairs, and it is from His ownership and disposal that He recompenses these people for their deeds.

As for His saying ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾, the meaning of sājid (one who prostrates) is well known, and ﴿وَقِيَامًا﴾, qā'im (one who stands) is also well known, meaning standing. Allah did not mention bowing (rukū') or sitting (qu'ūd). This is because standing is the most noble part of the prayer in terms of its recitation, namely the Qur'an, and prostration is the most noble part of the prayer in terms of state and posture, as in the hadith: "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating."[[Narrated by Muslim (482/215) from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] So He mentioned standing for its nobility through what is recited in it, and He mentioned prostration for its nobility through its posture. This indicates that this is the best state of the prayer, and so it is.

As for His saying ﴿يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ﴾ [al-Furqan 64], someone may say: the apparent meaning of the noble verse is that they stay awake through the night, since it mentions that their description in the state of spending the night is standing and prostrating. Does this mean that standing in prayer through the whole night is prescribed?

We say: if we take the apparent meaning of the verse, then it is so, but...

* Student: The general (...).

* Shaykh: But what the Sunnah has brought indicates otherwise, and that the best practice is that a person sleeps half the night, stands in prayer for a third of it, and sleeps a sixth of it, as was the prayer of Dawud, peace be upon him, and the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, for he would sleep at the beginning of the night and stand in prayer in the middle of the night (ﷺ).[[Al-Bukhari (1131) and Muslim (1159/189) narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud, and the most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud, peace be upon him. He used to sleep half the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and sleep a sixth of it. He used to fast one day and break his fast the next day."]]

* Student: Like the Qur'an, O Shaykh, like the Qur'an in Surat al-Muzzammil.

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. So according to this, its meaning is that they spend most of their night (in worship), or that Allah records for them the reward of prayer and standing even while they are sleeping, so long as they remain upon this intention and this action, as long as they act and intend that when they sleep, they sleep only to strengthen themselves for standing in prayer, and so its reward is recorded for them even though they are sleeping.

* Student: O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: I have some reservation about their praying at night.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: That it is not necessary that it be obligatory at night; perhaps standing is applied to...

* Shaykh: Enough. ﴿يَبِيتُونَ﴾ [al-Furqan 64]: bayāt (spending the night) occurs only at night.

* Student: There is no bayāt during the day.

* Shaykh: No, bayāt does not occur during the day.

(Qur'an 25:65) "And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever-adhering.'" (i.e., lasting, clinging)

This is one of the things they supplicate Allah with.

"And those who say, 'Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell'" [25:65]. In this is evidence of their saying, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell," that they do not rely upon Allah because of their deeds, and that despite their performing this deed, they fear the Fire; therefore they ask Allah, exalted is He, to avert from them the punishment of Hell.

Jahannam (Hell) is one of the names of the Fire, and it was named so because its depth is far and it is dark.

As for His saying, "Indeed its punishment is ever-adhering" (i.e., lasting), it is like the clinging of a creditor to his debtor. This applies to the absolute punishment of the Fire, not to every kind of punishment, because not every punishment is lasting: the believer is punished in the Fire according to his sins, then he comes out of it into Paradise. But its absolute punishment is an adhering, clinging torment. So they ask Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to avert it from them, and they make clear the extent of this punishment, from which they sought refuge in Allah, that it clings to those it seizes.

(﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾ "Indeed, it is evil" [bi'sa] ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ "as a place of settlement and residence" [al-Furqan 25:66] "هي أي موضع استقرار وإقامة" "it is, i.e., a place of settlement and residence").

The author says: "(هي أسيؤه)"? Meaning...

* Student: No, it is "هي أي موضع استقرار وإقامة" (it is, i.e., a place of settlement and residence).

* Shaykh: "هي أي موضع"?

* Student: We do not know "أسيأه."

* Shaykh: It means "أشده سوءًا" (the worst of it in evil), but...

I was even surprised by "أسيؤه," because the known form is "أسوأه."

* Student: So it is as if he said: "بئست المكان" (what an evil place)?

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: "بئست المكان هي," as if it were being said.

* Shaykh: "(﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾ بئست ﴿مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ [al-Furqan 25:66] هي أي موضع استقرار وإقامة)."

﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ﴾ ("Indeed, it is evil"). This sentence may be the speech of Allah, the Exalted, and it may be the speech of the people of the Fire. That is, they sought refuge with Allah from the Fire, and they explained the reason for that by two matters: the permanence of its punishment, and the evil of its place of settlement and residence, "والعياذ بالله" (and we seek refuge in Allah). This motivates them to ask Allah, blessed and exalted, to turn this punishment away from them.

﴿إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ [al-Furqan 25:66] is the opposite of the people of Paradise: ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا﴾ ("The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in their resting place and best in their place of repose") [al-Furqan 25:24].

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: That it is what?

* Student: That the Fire is a settlement for the disbelievers, and in the same surah it is explained as (...).

* Shaykh: As what?

* Student: ﴿أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾ (...) that Paradise is a settlement, but the Fire is not a place of settlement. Here he says the Fire is a place of settlement?

* Shaykh: No (...). In it there is goodness. That is, ﴿خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا﴾ ("better in resting place") may indicate that there is some goodness in the Fire, as the implication of the comparative form (ism al-tafdil, the elative/comparative noun) would suggest, and that is not so.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 67:**

﴿And those who, when they spend,﴾ on their dependents ﴿are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ [al-Furqan 67], with the first letter vowelled with a fatha or a damma, meaning: they do not constrict.

(With a fatha on its first letter) ﴿yaqturu﴾ (and with a damma)?

* Student: ﴿yuqtiru﴾.

* Student: ﴿yusrifu﴾.

* Student: ﴿yusrifu﴾ and ﴿yuqtiru﴾.

* Student: ﴿yusrifu wa-lam yaqturu﴾.

* Shaykh: "With a fatha on its first letter," meaning the last one. Do you have "its first of the two" (ʾawwaluhuma) or "its first" (awwaluhu)?

* Student: "Its first" (awwaluhu).

* Shaykh: Yes, the last one. "With a damma on its first letter." But if we follow the author's wording, it would be ﴿wa-lam yaqturu﴾, (wa-lam yuqturu), because he did not mention the ruling on the *tā'* in the final issue (...). Because *yuqturu* is not clear from the standpoint of morphology (taṣrīf). Rather, ﴿yuqtiru﴾ comes from *aqtara*.

Alright, we will postpone (...). Do you have it?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: It is necessary (...).

﴿When they spend﴾ [al-Furqan 67]. The author's words "on their dependents": restricting it to spending on dependents is open to question, unless he means it as an example, i.e., like spending on dependents. Otherwise, it includes spending on dependents, spending in the way of Allah, spending on the various forms of good, and everything that counts as spending.

So these, when they spend, are not extravagant. Extravagance (isrāf) is exceeding the limit. ﴿And they are not stingy﴾ (they do not constrict).

﴿And it is a moderate course between that﴾ [al-Furqan 67]: (﴿And their spending﴾ is ﴿between that﴾, between extravagance and stinginess, ﴿a moderate course﴾ [al-Furqan 67], balanced).

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: ﴿They spend﴾. The object is not specified. Allah did not say "they spend on their dependents"; He stated it without restriction, so it includes everything they spend on dependents and on others.

His words ﴿and it is a moderate course between that﴾ mean: their spending was between that mentioned, which is extravagance and stinginess.

His words ﴿a moderate course﴾ mean: upright. He said ﴿qawāman﴾, meaning upright, because spending may tend toward extravagance or toward stinginess depending on the circumstances. That is, the position between extravagance and stinginess is a station, but sometimes the situation calls for leaning toward extravagance, and sometimes it calls for leaning toward stinginess. For this reason He said ﴿qawāman﴾ and did not stop at ﴿and it was between that﴾. Rather, He said ﴿qawāman﴾, meaning upright. If the situation requires increasing a little beyond the midpoint, they increase; if the situation requires decreasing, they decrease.

An example: suppose spending in a certain matter of one thousand dirhams is considered extravagance, and spending four hundred dirhams is considered stinginess. Between them there are six hundred dirhams. Sometimes the situation requires making it nine hundred, so the difference is a hundred; sometimes the situation requires making it five hundred, so the difference is a hundred; and sometimes the situation requires it to be seven hundred. The point is that it is ﴿between that, a moderate course﴾, meaning in a manner suited to the situation, whether it rises and comes close to extravagance, or falls and comes close to stinginess. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And it is a moderate course between that﴾ [al-Furqan 67].

* Student: Like spending on the household and food (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: And you respond to requests but do not waste, meaning (...)?

* Shaykh: Do not waste. But sometimes the situation requires that you give more. For example, if someone invites people of rank and standing, these people are given a little more, while for those below that level, wisdom requires that they be given according to their condition.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 68 (part 1 of 3):

And His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ [al-Furqan 68].

Before (the discussion of) spending between extravagance and stinginess, this (verse) falls under His saying: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63], if we take "walking" to mean walking in a figurative sense; for this is figurative walking, gentle, which inclines neither to haste nor to abasement.

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾.

﴿Ilah﴾ means: an object of worship. And does ﴿yad'una﴾ ("invoke") mean supplication of request (du'a al-mas'alah), or supplication of worship (du'a al-'ibadah), or both?

* Student: Both.

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning is both, that is, they do not invoke in supplication of request nor in supplication of worship. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord said, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell in humiliation."﴾ [Ghafir 60].

It is clear that supplication of request is called du'a (supplication), because you say: "O Lord, forgive me." But supplication of worship, how is it called du'a?

We say: because the person who worships Allah is one who calls upon Him by the tongue of his state; for he only hopes for Allah's mercy and fears His punishment. So when a person prays, pays zakah, fasts, performs Hajj, is dutiful to his parents and maintains ties of kinship, what does he intend by that? He intends by it Allah's reward. It is as though he is saying: "O Lord, reward me, give me Paradise, and save me from the Fire," and the like. For this reason worship is called du'a.

As for supplication of request, it is obvious.

But how is supplication of request a form of worship?

Yes, because it indicates humiliation and submission to the one who is called upon, and this is the reality of worship.

And they ﴿do not invoke with Allah another god﴾: neither in supplication of worship nor in supplication of request. This does not preclude that they ask created beings for what they are able to give; for that is because they believe these people being asked are a means and not independent. When a person asks a wealthy man for some dirhams, or a ruler for some dirhams, he believes that this one being asked is merely a means, and not independent in giving and withholding; rather giving and withholding are in the hand of Allah, and this one who gave you or withheld from you is only a means.

Like "binaa'" in the sense of "mabni" (built), "ghiraas" in the sense of "maghruus" (planted), "firaash" in the sense of "mafruush" (spread).

So the form "fi'aal" always comes in the sense of "maf'uul." Thus "ilah" means "ma'luh" (one who is worshipped), and "ma'luh" is the one who is worshipped and drawn near to by worship. On this basis, the idols of the polytheists are regarded as gods in terms of their (worshippers') action; but in terms of reality they are not truly gods, because divinity belongs truly to Allah, Glorified and Exalted.

(﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ its killing, ﴿except by right﴾ [al-Furqan 68]).

﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾: the author's words say that the object is omitted, its estimate being: (its killing). It is possible to make the omitted object merely a pronoun, so that the relative clause lacks its returning pronoun, i.e., "which Allah has forbidden," and the meaning of its prohibition is the prohibition of killing it and harming it.

﴿The soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ refers to four kinds of souls: the Muslim, the dhimmi, the mu'ahad, and the musta'man. These are the souls which Allah has forbidden. Then, the Muslim too may be permitted to be killed by Allah despite his Islam, such as the married adulterer and the one who kills intentionally; for his killing is permitted although he is a Muslim. But we say that the killing of a Muslim for these reasons is incidental, for otherwise the attribute of Islam makes his killing forbidden. So which souls has Allah forbidden?

* Student: The Muslim, the dhimmi, and the mu'ahad.

* Shaykh: The musta'man.

* Student: The musta'man.

* Shaykh: Good. The Muslim is known. And the dhimmi?

* Student: The dhimmi is the disbeliever, or (...) People of the Book, when he is in the lands of the Muslims and works for them, but (...), meaning he has a contract with us, meaning there is a covenant between us and him.

* Shaykh: That is, one with whom a covenant has been concluded in exchange for the jizyah and protection.

Good. And the mu'ahad?

* Student: He is one with whom a covenant has been signed between us and him (...).

* Shaykh: Without protection?

* Student: Without protection.

* Shaykh: And without jizyah.

And who is the musta'man?

* Student: The disbeliever who enters the lands of the Muslims under their safe-conduct.

* Shaykh: Under their safe-conduct, well said. This is the weakest of them, the weakest; for it is a granting of safe-conduct without a contract, and for this reason it is valid from every person; every person may grant safe-conduct to a disbeliever, following the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "We have granted safe-conduct to whomever you have granted safe-conduct, O Umm Hani"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (357), Muslim (336 / 82) from the hadith of Umm Hani, may Allah be pleased with her.]]. But covenant and dhimmah are only concluded by the Imam or his deputy.

* Student: The Prophet's ﷺ saying "We have granted safe-conduct to whom you granted" does it not indicate that it does not drop the safe-conduct until (...)?

* Shaykh: No, it does not indicate this; for if it were so, the Messenger ﷺ would have prevented others from granting safe-conduct afterwards. This does not mean it is an original creation (inshaa'); rather it means a ruling and not an creation. The creation occurred with her first granting of safe-conduct; that is, it is as if he says: "Your safe-conduct has been established by it."

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: No; for how do we know that it becomes established except by this? So this is not a creation, but a statement of a ruling that her safe-conduct has been executed.

* Student: We mentioned that the servants of Allah, the servants of the Most Merciful, have (...) what has come in the Qur'anic verses, such as: ﴿You would recognize them by their mark; they do not ask people persistently﴾ [al-Baqarah 273], and the hadiths.

* Shaykh: But asking people is sometimes praiseworthy, sometimes blameworthy, and sometimes disliked, meaning either disliked or forbidden. But in the case of permissibility: a person may ask in cases of necessity; in necessity he asks, it is permissible for him to ask. That is, if a person became hungry to the point that he would either die or ask, here it is permissible for him to ask.

* Student: Or is it obligatory for him?

* Shaykh: Yes; it is permissible in principle, and it may be obligatory. The discussion is about a state whose doer is not blamed.

﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾ [al-Furqan 68].

From "the right" is what we pointed to: that a Muslim commits adultery while married, and likewise the dhimmi, for he is subjected to the hadd punishment, as the Prophet ﷺ did in stoning the two married adulterers.

Likewise, from the right is that this be by way of qisas (retaliation), and from the right is when he is a highway robber. As for apostasy, it does not enter the exception, but rather enters the implication of: ﴿which Allah has forbidden﴾; for the apostate's blood is permissible, and he is not one whose killing is forbidden except for a cause; rather he is one whose killing is permitted. So the apostate falls within the implication of His saying: ﴿which Allah has forbidden﴾, because the apostate is not forbidden.

And His saying: ﴿nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ [al-Furqan 68]. When He mentioned the violation of lives, He mentioned the violation of honour. Zina is committing the vile act in the front or the rear passage. If it is with a male, it is called lawat (sodomy); if it is with a female, it is zina. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not mention sodomy specifically because it is a matter that is abhorrent and remote, even by nature; nature does not call to it except one whose nature and innate disposition Allah has overturned.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed, (...).

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: No, it is not included in this; in any case it falls under the other sins. But when it is said: "They do not kill the soul," or "whoever kills a soul, upon him is such and such," the intended meaning is the human soul.

* Student: The principle (...)?

* Shaykh: Which one?

* Student: Whatever harms by nature is killed by the law?

* Shaykh: Correct.

* Student: (...) all that which is forbidden?

* Shaykh: Everything that harms by nature, it is killed by the law.

* Student: O Shaykh, if the jinn perform these deeds, how are they not killed?

* Shaykh: (...)?

* Student: No, some of them kill others.

* Shaykh: Their ruling?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Indeed, the apparent view is that their rulings are like the rulings of mankind; for the Messenger was sent to them, and this is transgression. For this reason it is mentioned that Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, when someone afflicted by possession was brought to him, would admonish and rebuke (the jinn) and explain to them that aggression against a Muslim is forbidden, which indicates that they believe this is forbidden and that they are obligated by it. This question has already come up for us: Is the obligation of the jinn like the obligation of mankind?

We said: the apparent meaning of the texts is that they are equal to them, for the Messenger was sent to them all, and we do not know of any legislation specific to them. But whoever considers the wisdom behind legislation finds that Allah legislates for each being what suits it. Accordingly, the obligation of the jinn differs from that of mankind, and they are obligated with what befits them. This is indicated by the fact that Allah made for them every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned to be found fuller of meat[[Muslim (450 / 15) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, the hadith, in which: "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned that falls into your hands, fuller of meat..."]], which indicates that they differ from mankind, since mankind does not obtain that. And also, if mankind differs in obligation according to circumstance, then the obligation of the wealthy with zakah is not equal to that of the poor, because he has no wealth, and the obligation of one able to worship is not equal to that of one incapable of it, because the attribute which made the obligation binding is not present in him.

So the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is to say: as for the fact of worship, there is no doubt that they are obligated to it; but as for the attributes and branches of worship, it is not necessary that they be equal to mankind, for they differ from them in reality, and the Shari'ah requires that every being be legislated for what suits it.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes indeed.

* Student: So He gave them legislations, or (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes, but it does not follow from the fact that this group who came into contact with him had their obligation cut off. They may be obligated by what they hear and learn of the Shari'ah, even if the Messenger did not personally address them; for their statement: ﴿Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an. It guides to righteousness﴾ [al-Jinn 1, 2] requires that they are guided by the whole Qur'an; for ﴿we have heard an amazing Qur'an﴾ does not mean they heard the whole Qur'an, since the surah is Meccan and the Qur'an had not been fully revealed.

* Student: Is it not (...)?

* Shaykh: No, this is not correct. They are without doubt addressed with the branches; but does it follow that they are equal to us? Some scholars say it follows, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to jinn and mankind, and there is no legislation specific to the jinn that we know of; so as long as they are obligated by the message, it binds them generally.

Some scholars say: whoever considers the wisdom in legislation says that every people is legislated what suits them; if mankind differ among themselves in some kind of obligation and it is specified for one, then how much more so for the other kind? This is closer to the wisdom of legislation: that they have legislations specific to them. As for the foundations of religion, there is no doubt that they are like us, meaning like prayer and the principle of zakah and the like.

* Student: O Shaykh, then like prayer for them, like Hajj for them; their actions differ from ours..

* Shaykh: No, the apparent view is that these acts of worship do not differ; for they are able to pray and they are able to perform Hajj.

* Student: (...) for them (...) of light.

* Shaykh: No, is light still? Are they not created from fire?

* Student: Yes, O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: Yes, have you (...) any of them?

* Student: No, I sat with those who read about them. Some people spoke with me saying (...).

* Shaykh: Originally they are not seen; they are not seen, but they are bodies.

* Student: Bodies (...)?

* Shaykh: We do not know. The common people say: they have no bones and no sinews. We do not know about this; is it correct or not? The important point is that they are bodies who eat, drink and urinate. The Prophet said: "That is a man in whose ear Satan has urinated"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3270), Muslim (774 / 205) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]], and he said that if the name of Allah is not mentioned over food, the jinn share it with him, and he informed us: "Every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, you will find it fuller of meat"[[Related by Muslim (450 / 15) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording "For you is every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned that falls into your hands, fuller of meat..." the hadith.]].

* Student: (...) He established them on the earth?

* Shaykh: Yes, He established them on the surface of the earth; but according to what we know from investigation, they always take refuge in empty places; the empty places are where they are always found. This is from Allah's mercy to us and to them; for if they were in inhabited places, they might be harmed, or we might be harmed by them. Sometimes when someone settles in empty places (...), it is said that there is a place with us that is deserted and has (...), so a man came and settled it, and they rose up against him at night and said: you must leave us, or we will kill your children; so he left, went away, and left them.

* Student: They threaten him, O Shaykh?

* Shaykh: By Allah, I thank Allah that I am safe from them; I have never heard a threat from them. But people are known to have this matter. However, they say: the scholars say that it is permissible for one to marry from among them. What is your view?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Some scholars say it is permissible, and some scholars say it is not permissible for a person to marry from among them; for among the conditions of marriage, as Allah said: ﴿He created for you mates from yourselves that you may find tranquility in them﴾ [al-Rum 21]. It is known that mankind cannot: first, they are not of your own selves; and second, one cannot find tranquility with them, for there is utmost aversion between them. So how could one be a spouse to him?

Is it true that the jinn marry, or not?

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 68 (part 2 of 3):**

﴿They say, "Peace" (salaman)﴾. What is the meaning of ﴿salaman﴾?

* **Student:** They are safe thereby from sin and transgression.
* **Shaykh:** From sin and dispute (...). Yes, this is what is meant. It does not mean they said "Peace be upon you," as some common people think, nor does it mean they do not say anything; rather they say a statement by which they are safe from sin with regard to what is between them and Allah, and from (...), enmity and harm in what is between them and these ignorant people.
* **Student:** (...)?
* **Shaykh:** Here the verse does not address it, but one looks to what is beneficial. That is, this is a description that they say a statement by which they are safe from sin. * **Student:** (...)?

* **Student:** The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant﴾ [Al-Qasas 55]. Is this the explicit meaning of the verse (...)?

* **Shaykh:** Only that?
* **Student:** Or (...).

﴿When they spend, they are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾. What is extravagance (israf)?
* **Student:** Exceeding the limit.
* **Shaykh:** Exceeding the limit, in quantity or in quality.
﴿And they are not stingy (lam yaqturu)﴾. Iqtar?
* **Student:** (...).
* **Shaykh:** Yes, good. Here the verse ﴿they are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾ is very clear. Suppose we did not know it by the language (...).
* **Student:** That is (...).
* **Shaykh:** Good, fine. How do you know this meaning?
* **Student:** (...).
* **Shaykh:** Yes, did you understand it from what it is paired with?

The word ﴿thubat﴾ alone, one does not know at all what it means; but when He said: ﴿or go forth all together﴾, we knew that the meaning of ﴿thubat﴾ is "in separate groups." This is one of the ways by which the tafsir of the Qur'an is known: the meaning of a word is known by comparing it with what it is paired with.
Here we mention that the author, may Allah have mercy on him, did not clarify the recitation. He said: "with the first letter fathah and damma." ﴿wa lam yaqturu﴾, ﴿wa lam yuqturu﴾. So the recitations on this are three: ﴿wa lam yaqtiru﴾, ﴿wa lam yaqturu﴾, ﴿wa lam yuqtiru﴾. And iqtar means reducing and restricting.
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And between that [i.e., extravagance and stinginess] was a moderate course﴾ [Al-Furqan 67]. To what does ﴿that﴾ refer?
* **Student:** It refers to (...) extravagance and stinginess.
* **Shaykh:** And stinginess. And what is the benefit of mentioning ﴿qawaman﴾?
* **Student:** The benefit is that ﴿qawaman﴾ (...) its benefit is that it does not require the middle course in His saying, the middle course, meaning (...) in His saying: ﴿between that﴾; rather, steadfastness in that is observed, and it is (...).
* **Shaykh:** Excellent, good.

* **Student:** Supplication of request and supplication of worship.
* **Shaykh:** Supplication of request and supplication of worship. What is the evidence for dividing supplication into these?
* **Student:** (...).

* **Student:** Because (...).

* **Shaykh:** It is like what the brother said. That is, the one who supplicates is hopeful and fearful?
* **Student:** (...) humbled before Allah.

* **Student:** (...) and no one can do this except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic (...).
* **Shaykh:** That is, as if it is praise of Allah?
* **Student:** Yes, because (...).
* **Shaykh:** And praise of Allah is from worship?
* **Student:** Yes.
* **Shaykh:** Good. The point is, we now have three aspects. Do you have anything else?
* **Student:** Because (...) from Allah, the Exalted, that He forgive him what (...), so he combines fear and hope.
* **Shaykh:** Yes, good, this is additional clarification.
This is one aspect of why supplication of request is worship.
Now, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [Al-Furqan 68]. What is ﴿the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾?
* **Student:** (...).

* **Student:** (...).

* **Shaykh:** And the musta'min. Good: four categories: the believer, the dhimmi, the mu'ahad, and the musta'min. These four types of souls are forbidden.
And His saying: ﴿except by right﴾ is an exception from the forbidden souls, because these forbidden souls may be made permissible by right. Example?
* **Student:** (...).
* **Shaykh:** Yes, so this was originally a forbidden soul, but there is a right that makes its killing permissible. Yes.
﴿And they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾ [Al-Furqan 68]?
* **Student:** The apostate (...)?
* **Shaykh:** Yes, because he was not originally among those forbidden. But when he apostatized, his status became what? What became his status?
* **Student:** A disbeliever.
* **Shaykh:** Good, so he does not fall under the four. But the fornicator remains Muslim despite his fornication, and the killer remains Muslim despite his killing.
* **Student:** But with the apostate, do we not say, for example (...)?
* **Shaykh:** No, we say: the attribute of Islam has been removed from him; that is, the attribute has completely departed from him, and he is now not sacred.
* **Student:** If he fornicates and then kills, or for example (...)?
* **Shaykh:** Yes.
* **Student:** The hadith: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in one of three cases."
* **Shaykh:** Yes.
* **Student:** Is there no mention in the hadith of "one who abandons his religion"?
* **Shaykh:** "One who abandons his religion and separates from the community."[[Narrated by Muslim (1676/25) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Some said: what is meant by it is highway robbers, because highway robbery is abandoning the religion; in order for the exception to be connected.
And some said: the one who abandons his religion is the apostate, and the exception with regard to him is disconnected, because one who abandons his religion is not a Muslim, except by considering an additional attribute.
* **Student:** Shaykh (...)?
* **Shaykh:** One who has left faith, meaning?
* **Student:** The one who (...).
* **Shaykh:** Yes, (...).
Yes. Are you saying we have not finished the benefits?
* **Student:** No, we stopped at: ﴿And they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾.
* **Shaykh:** (...) we will complete the verse.
* **Student:** Yes.
* * *
* **Shaykh:** Good. The saying of Allah: ﴿And they do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾. The scholars say in its explanation that zina is committing the immoral act in the front or the rear. And by even greater reason, sodomy (liwat), because it is more vile, and because sodomy is never lawful under any circumstance, whereas intercourse is made lawful by marriage. For this reason, the punishment for sodomy, according to the preponderant opinion, is execution in every case, whether the one committing it is muhsan (married) or not muhsan, because it is an orifice that is never permitted under any circumstance. Moreover, it is a matter that cannot be guarded against, so the society cannot be purified except by executing both the doer and the one to whom it is done.
Likewise, according to the preponderant opinion: fornication with close relatives (dhawat al-mahram) requires execution in every case, because this orifice is not permitted under any circumstance. A hadith on this is found in the Sunan and it is authentic.[[Abu Dawud (2564) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has intercourse with a close relative, kill him; and whoever has intercourse with an animal, kill him, and kill the animal."]] So fornication with close relatives, such as if one commits zina with his sister, may Allah protect us, even if she is a foster sister, it requires his execution in every case, whether he is muhsan or not muhsan.
Allah, blessed and exalted, has described zina as fahisha (an abomination), and He described sodomy on the tongue of Lut as the abomination: ﴿Do you commit the abomination?﴾ [Al-A'raf 80]. So the definite article (al) was attached to it. As for that: ﴿it was an abomination﴾ [Al-Isra 32] among the abominations. But it is as if the abomination became restricted to this because of its magnitude and ugliness.
(﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., one of the three, ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ [Al-Furqan 68].)

The author's statement "(i.e., one of the three)" requires examination. The principle regarding a demonstrative reference is that it returns to everything previously mentioned together. This would require that ﴿وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ refers to all that was mentioned: the three of them, namely calling upon other than Allah, killing the soul, and fornication. ﴿Whoever does that will meet a penalty (athām)﴾ [al-Furqan 25:68]. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾ [al-Furqan 25:68-69].

What we have established, that it returns to all of them, is free from an objection that will come at His words: ﴿and he will abide therein﴾, for fornication does not necessitate eternal abiding in the Fire. As for killing, Allah the Exalted mentioned in Surah an-Nisa' that it necessitates eternal abiding in the Fire, and its mention will come shortly, God willing.

The point is that its return to the three is free from the objection that follows, God willing.

As for when one commits only one of them individually, its ruling is derived from another proof; it is not necessary that we derive it from this verse.

(﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾ means punishment.) The word athām and nakal have the same meaning, and punishment and nakal also have the same meaning. Thus, what is meant by athām here is punishment, and it is a singular noun, not a plural, for the plural is āthām, the plural of ithm (sin). As for this form, ﴿athāman﴾ [athām].

(﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾, and in another recitation ﴿يُضَعَّفْ﴾ with the doubled letter, which is a canonical (sab'i) reading), and both ﴿يُضَعَّفْ﴾ and ﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾ are sab'i readings. Al-mudaa'afah (doubling) and al-tad'if (multiplying) mean repeating a thing. The punishment is doubled for him because he committed three causes of punishment: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul, and fornication (zina). It is known that when causes combine, each one has its own effect. Whoever commits one of the three bears its sin, whoever commits two bears the sins of both, and whoever commits all three bears their sins. This is the meaning of the doubling.

﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ﴾: al-'adhab (punishment) and al-nakal (exemplary punishment) have one meaning, and the punishment is ﴿الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾.

﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ is the day on which people are resurrected, and it is called Yawm al-Qiyamah for three reasons. What are the three reasons?

* Student: The resurrection from the graves.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: And their standing on the day of presentation (al-'ard).

* Shaykh: Is that not included in the first?

* Student: Yes, I mean: the standing of truth on that day.

* Shaykh: Yes, the standing of justice?

* Student: Justice.

* Shaykh: And the establishment of justice. Yes, what else? The third?

* Student: Because they stand and wait (...).

* Shaykh: Do you mean by waiting (al-wuquf)?

* Student: Yes, waiting.

* Shaykh: Do you mean by standing, waiting?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: The standing of the messengers.

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: What is derived from His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 6]?

* Shaykh: Yes, this is from their graves. ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهَادُ﴾ [Ghafir 51]. And because the testimony is established on it, the witnesses stand on it, and they are the angels, the messengers, and likewise the nations. So the Day is called Yawm al-Qiyamah for these three aspects.

﴿وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Furqan 69]: he remains in it, ﴿فِيهِ﴾ meaning in the punishment. (The two verbs are jazm (apocopated) as a substitute (badal), and raf' (indicative) as a resumed sentence (isti'naf).)

Where are the two verbs? ﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾ and ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ﴾.

That is, there are two readings in each: ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ﴾ and ﴿يُضَاعَفُ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ﴾; ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ﴾ and ﴿وَيَخْلُدُ﴾.

As for His saying ﴿يَلْقَ أَثَامًا﴾, there is only one reading, the jazm, because it is the answer of the condition (jawab al-shart), and the answer of the condition must be jazm. But there is a difficulty, namely that it bears a fatha: ﴿يَلْقَ﴾. It is said that it is jazm by the deletion of the alif, and this fatha is not the fatha of i'rab but the fatha of the verb.

As for His saying ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ﴾, this permits two things, and it is an exception to its counterparts: ﴿فِيهِ﴾ with madd, and ﴿فِيهِ مُهَانًا﴾ with silah, that is, with wasl without madd. ﴿فِيهِ مُهَانًا﴾ follows the original rule, while ﴿فِيهِ مُهَانًا﴾ with silah is against the original rule but permissible, meaning it is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ.

It has a parallel, being outside the usual pattern: ﴿وَمَنْ أَوْفَى بِمَا عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهُ اللَّهَ﴾ [al-Fath 10], and in another sab'i reading: ﴿عَلَيْهِ اللَّهَ﴾, which follows the original rule.

So these are two letters in the Qur'an that deviate from the rule followed in the famous reading in the mushafs.

He said: (﴿وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا﴾ hal, a circumstantial clause). This is in truth a shortcoming of the author. (﴿مُهَانًا﴾ is a hal.) I parse it now as a hal from the pronoun in His saying ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ﴾, or from the two pronouns in ﴿يُضَاعَفْ﴾ and ﴿وَيَخْلُدْ﴾, but it is closer to the nearer one. However, he did not explain the meaning of ﴿مُهَانًا﴾, and we need the explanation of the word more than its parsing, because we will read it as it is but not understand its meaning.

So what is the meaning of ﴿مُهَانًا﴾?

Al-muhan is the despised, the humiliated, meaning: despised and humiliated, for whom no weight is given and no honour is shown.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 70 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And He will abide therein in humiliation (69). Except one who repents﴾ [al-Furqan: 69, 70]. Is this exception (istithna') muttasil (connected) or munqati' (disconnected)?

* Student: Muttasil.

* Shaykh: Muttasil. ﴿Except one who repents﴾, so the exception is connected; that is, whoever repents from calling upon anyone besides Allah, and whoever repents from killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and whoever repents from fornication (zina).

As for the first, which is repentance from calling upon someone besides Allah, there is no doubt or difficulty in it, because it is a right of Allah. So when a person repents from it to Allah, He accepts it, if it is a sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah), and there is no need for him to seek permission from anyone. Does he need to ask forgiveness from the idol?

* Student: He does not need to.

* Shaykh: He does not need to.

﴿And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ (...) is clear. Likewise, what is established in the authentic hadith about the story of the man who killed ninety-nine souls, then asked a worshipper whether he had any repentance. The worshipper said: No, you have no repentance. The worshipper was ignorant, and he considered ninety-nine souls to be a great matter, so he said: You have no repentance. He said: We will complete a hundred with you, and he killed him. This is among the burdens that a person brings upon himself when he issues a fatwa without knowledge. Then he asked a scholar: Does he have any repentance? The scholar said: Yes, and who can come between you and repentance? But he guided him to leave his village for another village where righteous people are numerous... until the end of the hadith.[[Muslim (2766) narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There was among those before you a man who had killed ninety-nine souls. He asked about the most knowledgeable people on earth, and he was directed to a monk. He came to him and said: He has killed ninety-nine souls; does he have any repentance? He said: No. So he killed him, completing a hundred with him. Then he asked about the most knowledgeable people on earth, and he was directed to a learned man. He said: He has killed a hundred souls; does he have any repentance? He said: Yes, and who can come between him and repentance? Go to such and such a land, for there are people there who worship Allah, so worship Allah with them, and do not return to your land, for it is a land of evil..." The hadith.]] If this was among the Children of Israel, then what about this Ummah, for whom Allah has removed the burdens and the shackles?!

Now, the repentance from killing a soul which Allah has forbidden: does another right, other than Allah's, become attached to it?

The answer: Yes, two other rights become attached to it. One of them is the right of the slain person who has died, and the second is the right of the heirs (awliya') of the slain. Repentance is not valid except by enabling those with rights to take their rights.

We say: the dead person cannot be reached to take his right, is that not so? It is not possible, because he has died and we do not know of him. Although in reality we may sometimes know, if the slain one did not die until his killer had been pardoned by him; perhaps he may know, but generally it is not known.

As for the heirs of the slain, enabling them to take their right is possible. So he goes to them, surrenders himself to them, and says: You now have the choice. Do you want the blood money (diyah)? Do you want retaliation (qatl)? Do you want pardon (afw)?

So, we say: repentance from killing a soul is attached to two rights other than the right of Allah: a right that can be fulfilled, which is the right of the heirs, the awliya' of the slain; and a right that may or may not be possible, which is the right of the slain. If it can be fulfilled in this world and he discharges it, that is well. Otherwise, when Allah, glorified and exalted, knows of this killer that he has repented to Him with sincere repentance, then part of Allah's accepting his repentance is that He gives the slain person his right, so that nothing is taken from the good deeds of the killer.

* Student: We mentioned that the pronoun in the verse refers to the three acts, and now we have specified each one. With His saying: ﴿except one who repents and believes﴾ there is evidence that (...) ﴿except one who repents and believes﴾ and what follows (...).

* Shaykh: No, in general. But now we want to establish repentance, and what is repentance?

Repentance is returning to Allah, glorified and exalted.

We remain with fornication: ﴿and they do not commit zina﴾. Does another right attach to it besides the right of Allah?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Then, if he repents, does he need to seek the permission and forgiveness (istihlal) of the one he fornicated with, or does he not need to?

* Student: If she was coerced (...).

* Shaykh: Certainly, if it was by her choice, there is no issue; she brought harm upon herself.

* Student: (...).

* Student: If she was married (...).

* Shaykh: Leave aside "if she was married." But if she had no husband? If it was by her choice, she has no right, because she is the one who violated her own honour. If she was coerced, then she has a right, so it is necessary to seek her forgiveness and that she grant him pardon.

It may be said: if the repentance becomes sincere, and he repents to Allah, then there is no need for istihlal, for Allah, the Exalted, accepts his repentance, as is established in the authentic hadith that the legal punishment (hadd) is an expiation (kaffarah) for the sin.[[This is in the hadith narrated by the two Shaykhs: al-Bukhari (18) and Muslim (1709/41), from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit zina, nor kill your children, nor bring slander that you invent between your hands and feet, nor disobey in what is good. Whoever among you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah; and whoever commits any of that and is punished in this world, it is an expiation for him; and whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, it is up to Allah: if He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him."]] The Prophet ﷺ did not mention anything beyond that without istihlal. Whoever considers that this involves a right to violating her honour, forcing her into immorality, and harming her reputation and her family, says: istihlal is necessary in this matter, because it is a grave matter. Whoever considers the general evidences showing that when the zani is subjected to the legal punishment, and when he repents, Allah accepts his repentance, says: Allah, the Exalted, bears on his behalf the right of this woman he fornicated with. Based on this, istihlal is preferable; seeking it is better and more excellent.

So we say: The first is a pure right of Allah with no difficulty; the second is a right of Allah and of others, with no difficulty; and the third is a right of Allah and of others. * Shaykh: Abandoning the sin includes returning the right, because as long as the right is still with you, you have not abandoned it. Yes indeed; for this reason we say: (...) we add a fourth condition, we say: this condition is included in our saying "abandoning."

As for it being in its proper time: for each person, it is that he repents before he witnesses death, based on His saying: ﴿And repentance is not for those who commit evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says: Indeed, I have repented now﴾ [al-Nisa': 18]. And for people in general, it is that it be before the sun rises from the west, for after the sun rises from the west, repentance is not accepted even if a person repents.

﴿except one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds﴾.

* Shaykh: It is said: ﴿There was certainly in their stories a lesson﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not (...); we understand the story only, but we take lessons from it, otherwise it would be idle.

As for whether it is part of an abrogated law, such matters (...) do not. That Allah accepts the repentance of one who repents is one of the attributes that does not change. Furthermore, its abrogation cannot be abrogation toward something worse in this case, because this Ummah is more complete than others; Allah has removed from it the burdens and shackles. If repentance were not accepted from the killer, this would be among the greatest burdens and shackles upon this Ummah. For this reason, the Children of Israel's stories are not related to us except... and neither are the Prophet's, peace and blessings be upon him, except as a warning against what is disliked and an encouragement toward what is loved.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 25, verse 70 (part 2 of 2):

* The Shaykh: It does not disappear; it remains. So the remedy for backbiting is that you praise him in return for the disparagement, you speak well of him in exchange for speaking ill of him. And this is more correct, because in reality, if you go and inform him, he may be seized by pride in sin and say: "No." Then (...) that I said: "By God, so-and-so is stingy," and he said to me: "No, he did not say 'stingy' alone, he said 'stingy, wicked, corrupt and immoral,' because Satan says such-and-such to him," so he imagines the matter is more than this and does not forgive you. So as long as the matter has not reached him, knowledge of it has not reached him.
As for yes: if knowledge of it has reached him, and you know that the man has been told that you backbit him, then here you must seek his pardon (istihlal), do you understand now? So the summary is that it is said: if the one backbitten knows of your backbiting, then something has now stirred against you in his soul, and you must seek his pardon so that what is in his soul is removed. But if, for example, it has not reached him, and you have only spoken of him in a gathering and you know that knowledge of it has not reached him, then here there is no need to go and tell him; rather, you praise him in good in return for your speaking of him in evil. This is the correct view, and the choice of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him. (...)

* A student: "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful (70). And whoever repents and does righteous deeds, then indeed he turns to Allah with (accepted) turning (71). * The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: (("Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds" from among them, "for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds").)
This is an exception from His saying: "he will meet penalty (athaman)," and what is substituted for it, meaning "except for one who repents," who will not meet penalty, nor will his punishment be doubled for him, nor will he abide in it.
It has preceded that the conditions of repentance are five: sincerity to Allah, regret over what occurred, abandoning it, resolving not to return to it, and that it be at the time when repentance is accepted, in its time.
It has also preceded that this exception includes all three sins: shirk, killing a soul, and fornication. As for what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the killer has no repentance,[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4764), and Muslim (3023 / 19).]] if he meant it absolutely, then it is not correct; and if he meant that he has no repentance regarding the right of the one killed, then this is correct. Yet we say: it is not far-fetched that if he repents a sincere repentance, Allah, exalted and blessed, may take upon Himself the right of the one killed and satisfy him.

* The Shaykh: From the Qur'an: "Except those who repent before you have power over them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" [al-Ma'idah 34].
* The student: Is the hadd not established upon him?
* The Shaykh: The hadd is not established upon him if he repents before one has power over him.
