Except the hadd for slander, if we say it is a right of the human being, then it does not fall away except by the pardon of the one slandered.
* The student: (...) his confession?
* The Shaykh: On the matter of repentance, or that the Messenger knew this about him. The point is that if he repents before having power over him, the hadd is established upon him. Yes.
"Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds": repentance has already been discussed. Faith (iman) linguistically means assent and affirmation, but in the Shari'ah it is the assent of the heart that necessarily entails acceptance and submission, not mere assent. Rather, it is an assent that necessarily entails this; if it does not entail it, it is not faith.
We said: necessarily entails what? Acceptance and submission: he accepts what the Shari'ah has brought and submits to it, so he affirms it if it is a report, and acts upon it if it is a command.
* A student: And if the killer does not repent?
* The Shaykh: If the killer does not repent, then he faces the threat that Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned.
* The student: Okay, (...)?
* The Shaykh: Yes, he is under the Will of Allah. But who says that He will forgive him?
And His saying: "and does righteous deeds."
Here He mentioned the deed and described it as righteous, because a deed that is not righteous does not benefit its doer. A righteous deed is that which combines two conditions: sincerity to Allah, and following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If it lacks sincerity it is not accepted, and if it lacks following it is not accepted. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, the Exalted, said: I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his shirk."[[Narrated by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is evidence that what is not sincerely for Allah is rejected.
As for what is not in accordance with the Prophet's way, it is because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does a deed that is not upon our command, it is rejected."[[Narrated by Muslim (1718 / 18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]]
Both are combined in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord" [al-Kahf 110].
And His saying: "(from among them)": from whom? That is, from the doers of these three matters: shirk, killing a soul, and fornication. He restricted it to these because of the context and so that it would not be repeated with what follows.
("Then those, Allah will replace their evil deeds" that were mentioned "with good deeds" in the Hereafter).
"Yubaddilu" (He will replace): substitution is making one thing in place of another. Is this substitution a qadari (decreed) substitution or a jaza'i (recompense) substitution?
The scholars differed on this. Some said it is a qadari substitution, and some said it is a jaza'i substitution.
How so? Those who say it is a qadari substitution say: the meaning of the replacement of evil deeds with good is that when he believed and did a righteous deed, faith came in place of shirk, and righteous deeds came in place of fornication and killing a soul; that is, this faith and righteous deed became a replacement for disbelief, fornication and killing. So the meaning is that his faith and his righteous deed that he performed are the good deeds with which Allah, blessed and exalted, replaced the evil deeds, so this substitution is qadari.
It was said: rather, it is jaza'i, meaning that these sins themselves become good deeds: Allah replaces the previous evil deeds, making them good deeds, in addition to his later good deeds that were decreed for him so that he performed them. And how so? They say: because when he repented of these evil deeds, each repentance from them became a good deed for him, so his evil deeds were replaced by good deeds through repentance from them; and because whenever he recalls his previous evil deeds, he renews repentance, so these past deeds became good deeds through repentance from them.
The correct view is that the verse includes both, and that the verse encompasses both matters: for "whoever repents, believes and does righteous deeds," his previous evil deeds are replaced so that they become good deeds, but they are not the same first deeds; likewise, if he repents from them, he is rewarded for this repentance, so the evil deeds become good deeds through repentance from them.
The author's wording leans toward the second view, that this substitution is jaza'i, because of his saying "in the Hereafter," for if it were qadari it would not be in the Hereafter, since qadari substitution occurs only in this world, as it is his deed.
The correct view is that the verse includes both: by faith and righteous deeds his deeds are replaced with righteous deeds, and by repentance from evil deeds the previous evil deeds become good deeds, because through this repentance he gains elevation and standing with Allah, glorified and exalted.
("And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful"; that is, He has never ceased being characterized by that.)
And "kana" here, as has passed with us, is stripped of time, and what is meant by it is that its subject's attribution of its predicate is a necessary attribute. For this reason he said: "that is, He has never ceased being characterized by that," meaning: by forgiveness and mercy.
Al-Ghafur is an intensive form or an attributive adjective, and both indicate permanence, continuity and abundance. Forgiveness (maghfirah) is covering a sin together with overlooking it, meaning covering the sin and removing its punishment, and not merely covering, because it is derived from al-mighfar (helmet), and by the helmet comes covering and protection.
As for al-Rahim, he is the possessor of mercy that reaches those shown mercy, because it indicates the act together with the attribute as well. Mercy is one of the attributes of Allah, glorified and exalted, by which bestowal and kindness to creation occur, through bringing benefits and warding off harms.
As for one who explained mercy as kindness or as its willing, his statement is mistaken, because willing kindness is an effect of the effects of mercy, and so is kindness itself, and it is not mercy. "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."
* A student: Shaykh, our saying "And Allah is ever Forgiving" here may be an attributive adjective (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: (...) and it was not made plural.
* The Shaykh: It is not necessary that it act or be made possessive; as for its being in the accusative, that is due to the governing word, its accusative is due to the governing word.
* The student: A hadith has come with a meaning like: a servant will continue to see his evil deeds placed in one pan of the scales against his good deeds (...), until he wishes he had committed more evil deeds.[[Something with this meaning is narrated by al-Tabari (19/312) from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of the Fire to enter Paradise. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: Take away his major sins and ask him about his minor ones. He will be told: You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such. He will say: O Lord, I did things I do not see here. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed until his molars showed." He said: It will be said to him: "For you, in place of every evil deed, is a good deed."]]
* The Shaykh: I do not know this hadith, but given that the evil deeds are replaced by good deeds, it is possible in this respect.

(﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ﴾ from his sins, other than those mentioned), and for this reason he said of those previously mentioned: (﴿وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ among them), that is, among these people.

He only said (other than those mentioned) in order to avoid repetition. However, there is nothing preventing us from saying that there is no need for an exception, and that the second verse is general, so that it falls under the category of mentioning the general after the specific. This is because excluding those who went before from the generality of this verse has no basis. The better view is to say that the second verse is general, encompassing those who went before and others.

(﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا﴾ meaning: he returns to Him with a return, and He will reward him with good.)

﴿وَمَنْ تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ ﴿تَابَ﴾ means he turned back from his sin, and ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ means he increased in righteous deeds. So this person has sought to make amends for what he did and has increased in goodness.

He says: ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا﴾; that is, ﴿مَتَابًا﴾ complete. The verbal noun here serves to magnify this repentance; that is, ﴿مَتَابًا﴾ great, because of the perfection of this repentance. Otherwise, someone might say: this is a case of "obtaining what is already obtained" (taḥṣīl ḥāṣil): whoever repents is a penitent! No, the intended meaning is that his repentance is a complete, great repentance. The use of the verbal noun ﴿مَتَابًا﴾ indicates that this repentance has been placed in its proper position and is complete. This is true, for when a man repents and increases in righteous deeds, the soundness and completeness of his repentance become evident.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have differed: is it a condition of repentance that the deed be rectified, or is it not a condition?

Some said: rectifying the deed is a condition for it. On this view it is a sixth condition added to the five conditions, and whoever repents without rectifying his deed is not a penitent.

Some scholars said: rather, repentance is valid even without rectifying the deed.

Others said: if the deed is of the same kind as what he repented from, then it must be rectified; otherwise repentance is not valid.

An example of this: a man repents from fornication but he steals. According to the first view, his repentance from fornication is not valid, because he has not rectified his deed. According to the second view, it is valid, because theft is not of the same kind as fornication. According to the third view, it is all the more so that rectifying the deed is not a condition at all, and whoever repents from a sin, his repentance is accepted.

Another man repents from fornication but persists in forbidden gazing; he continues to look at women in a forbidden way. According to the view that rectifying the deed is not a condition, his repentance from fornication is valid. According to the view that rectifying the deed is necessary, his repentance from fornication is not valid. According to the middle view, which says: if it is of the same kind as what he repented from, it is also not accepted, then it is not valid, because this is the fornication of the eye, as the Prophet ﷺ said[[Ahmad (8356) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The eye commits adultery, and the heart commits adultery; the adultery of the eye is looking, and the adultery of the heart is desire, and the private parts either confirm that or deny it."]].

But the correct view is this: if by repentance is meant describing this man as among the penitents who receive praise, and it is truly said of them that they are penitent, then his repentance cannot be valid, nor can he deserve the description of repentance, except by rectifying the deed, because he has not made absolute repentance, but only a repentance in a general sense.

As for if by repentance is meant repentance from a specific deed, then the correct view is to affirm definitively that his repentance is accepted, because this is what the justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, requires: whoever does good has it for himself, and whoever does evil bears it upon himself. ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7), and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7–8]. So how can we say that this man's repentance from a deed he turned back from and regretted is not valid, merely because he persists in another? That is not acceptable.

So the correct position is this: as for deserving the description of penitents in an absolute sense, the penitent does not deserve it except by rectifying the deed, because how can someone be a penitent to Allah while he persists in disobedience, even if it is of a different kind from what he repented from or of the same kind?!

As for when what is meant is repentance from this specific deed, that is, a repentance of a particular kind and not absolute repentance, then it is valid definitively, because this is what the justice of Allah, glorified and exalted, requires.

* Student: Shaykh, there is a hadith that a man sinned, then repented, then sinned, then repented, then sinned, then repented, and then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: My servant knows that (...)[[al-Bukhari (7507) and Muslim, with his wording (2758/29), narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, relating from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who said: "A servant committed a sin and said: O Allah, forgive me my sin. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: My servant committed a sin, and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes account for sins. Then he returned and sinned again, and said: O Lord, forgive me my sin. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: My servant committed a sin, and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes account for sins. Then he returned and sinned again, and said: O Lord, forgive me my sin. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: My servant committed a sin, and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes account for sins; do what you wish, for I have forgiven you."]]. Is this evidence that if he repents and then returns to the deed, his repentance is not accepted?

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. This deed is not our issue here.

* Student: Perhaps it is another deed?

* Shaykh: No, this is not our question. We say: this man repented from the sin and did not return to it, but he is disobedient to Allah in another respect. That is what they are discussing.

* Student: If we say that (...), there are many rulings that follow from repentance, such as the transformation of evil deeds into good deeds.

* Shaykh: We say: yes, as for this specific deed, if he repents from it, it becomes a good deed.

* Student: It is turned (...)?

* Shaykh: What we said before: is it a recompensatory transformation or a predestined transformation?

* Student: Yes, but this is general?

* Shaykh: No, not at all. But either shirk, adultery, or killing a soul.

* Student: Yes, but he repented a sincere, complete repentance.

* Shaykh: No, he repented from these things. The point is that even one who repents a particular repentance from a particular sin, his evil deeds are changed into good deeds. The evil he repented from becomes a good deed, first because he left it for Allah's sake, and it is established from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that whoever intends an evil deed and then leaves it, a good deed is written for him[[al-Bukhari (6491) narrated from Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, relating from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, who said: "Allah wrote the good deeds and the evil deeds, then explained that. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, Allah writes it for him as a complete good deed with Him; but if he intends it and does it, Allah writes for him ten good deeds up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, Allah writes it for him as a complete good deed with Him; but if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it for him as one evil deed."]]; because he left it for Allah, this is similar to it. Moreover, merely that he repents to Allah and knows that he has a Lord who holds him to account and punishes him, and feels shame before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and modesty before Him, this is among the great good deeds.

* Student: As long as he still has the description of a disobedient person (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, disobedient in one respect, penitent in another.

* Student: Alright, what is the difference between fornication (...)?

* Shaykh: What is the difference?

* Student: For example (...), all of them, for instance?

* Shaykh: The difference between them is that this one is lashed, and that one has his hand cut off, and this one is a sinner in one respect and that one is a sinner in another respect; this is with regard to honor, and that is with regard to property, (...) among the differences. Not all sins are equal, neither in type, nor in degree, nor in sinfulness. For this reason we said that the absolute description of repentance is not valid, because in reality he is not a penitent, since he is disobedient to Allah, glorified and exalted, in one respect. But our saying: your repentance from fornication is not accepted because you steal, this is not correct.

* Student: Alright, can we not distinguish between them in terms of type, and instead distinguish them in terms of degree?

* Shaykh: How in terms of degree?

* Student: For example, there are major sins that are severe, and there are (...)?

* Shaykh: He deserves what he incurred. What he repented from is forgiven him, and what he persisted in remains upon him, whether minor or major, because this is what the justice of Allah requires. Is not this a deed of good by his repentance?

* Student: Perhaps his description is clear, but that it be turned into a good deed (...).

* Shaykh: Alright, we said that turning an evil deed into a good deed through repentance is because merely his return to Allah, glorified and exalted, and his leaving it and repenting from it is a good deed. This is if we say that what is meant by good deed is the recompensatory good deed, that he is rewarded with a good deed for the same evil deed. If we say it is a predestined transformation, meaning that this man's giving up of this sin and his uprightness is (...), then even the recompensatory one has no difficulty at all.

* Student: The predestined one is clear.

* Shaykh: And the recompensatory one too, because the generosity of Allah, glorified and exalted, is swifter and precedes His punishment.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Predestined, from qadar.

* Student: And also the recompensatory is from qadar.

* Shaykh: Yes, but it is a reward. However, this predestined one means that new good deeds other than the first are decreed for him, and the recompensatory one means that he is rewarded good deeds for the very same evil deeds.

* Student: The waw, Shaykh, in the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Except those who repent, believe, and do a deed﴾ (...), how do we parse it? A conjunction?

* Shaykh: Yes, a conjunction.

* Student: If it is a conjunction, we return to the sixth condition, which says rectifying the deed is necessary.

* Shaykh: Yes, but the phrase "and does a righteous deed" — we said that the absolute description of repentance is not deserved except by this, by the righteous deed.

* Student: Shaykh, are there verses of the Qur'an that describe a person as penitent even if he did not do a righteous deed (...)?

* Shaykh: Yes, such as: ﴿Except those who repent before you gain power over them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 34].

* Student: We mentioned that the disobedient person knows about himself that he is weak in faith, and that his enemy will be empowered over him, and that he will return to this disobedience (...) every time he commits a disobedience he repents, otherwise (...)?

* Shaykh: No, he repents. How would he know?

* Student: He will know that he will sin.

* Shaykh: No, but we say: this repentance of his is not valid, yet merely his feeling that he is mistaken may benefit him. As for us saying: he should not continue, that is not permissible.

* Student: He from the outset acknowledges that he is mistaken.

* Shaykh: Alright, he acknowledges he is mistaken, but he says: I want to continue, I am not giving up either in my heart or in my action; whenever the opportunity arises I will do it. This is evil, but that he repents to Allah and feels shame and develops a kind of drawing near to Allah is better than not.

* Student: Even if his repentance is repeated?

* Shaykh: Even if his repentance is repeated. But it is obligatory for the believer to repent definitively. If it is later decreed that the causes of the sin become available to him and his soul overcomes him, that does not invalidate his first repentance; he will be held to account again for the new sin, and then he repents.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: And your seeking forgiveness too...

This is not something that arises, except according to the doctrine of the Jabriyyah (...). Abstaining is easier than doing; for this reason you find, for example, that abstention is rewarded with absolute reward, unlike action; action is harder on the soul, because it is a struggle against the soul in two respects, whereas abstention is in one respect. So the phrase (...) is not correct.

* Student: Alright, Shaykh, the phrase...

* Shaykh: May Allah keep you safe. If the sultan's whip strikes his back once and his belly once, is he unable or not unable?

* Student: No, he is not unable, but (...).

* Shaykh: That is not correct. I testify that he (...); because there are people who repented, were sincere in resolve, repented and gave it up, yes indeed. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, before the prohibition of wine was revealed, were addicted to wine, and abstaining from wine is harder for its drinker than abstaining from tobacco, yet within a single day all of them (...). The matter rests on sincerity of resolve, yes indeed.

Now, outside of fasting, this drinker cannot stop, by his own claim, the whole day; he cannot by his claim refrain from tobacco the whole day, whereas in fasting, since he is resolved...

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes indeed.

﴿And whoever repents and does a righteous deed, then indeed he turns back to Allah with a [complete] return﴾ [al-Furqan 71].

We have said that His words ﴿then indeed he turns back to Allah with a [complete] return﴾ are not like the saying of one who says: the earth is beneath us and the sky above us, meaning mere redundancy. Rather, the meaning is that this is true, sincere, real, complete repentance.

And His words ﴿to Allah﴾ mean: he returns to Allah with a complete, perfect return, as the author said.

﴿ ﴾

(﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾ [الفرقان ٧٢])، هذه معطوفة على قوله؟

* طالب: ﴿وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ﴾ [الفرقان ٦٣].

* طالب آخر: لا، على مجموع الأوصاف.

* الشيخ: على قوله: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ﴾ [الفرقان ٦٣]، وسبق أن الصحيح أن ﴿الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ﴾ خبر وليست صفة كما قال المؤلف.

(﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾ [الفرقان ٧٢] أي الكذب والباطل).

هذا معنى (الزور) من ازورَّ، أي: مال وانحرف، ﴿وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَتْ تَزَاوَرُ عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ [الكهف ١٧]. فالمعنى أن الزور: كل ميل قولي أو فعلي، فإن كان قولًا وُصف بالكذب، وإن كان فعلًا وُصف بالباطل، فكل قول أو فعل مائل عن الطريق فهو زور.

الكذب زور، والشتم واللعن والغيبة زور أيضًا، والغصب والسرقة والزنا وغيرها زور أيضًا.

* طالب: باطل.

* الشيخ: زور، هو زور، لكن قد نسميه باطلًا إذا كان فعلًا.

فالمهم أنهم لا يشهدون الزور، وإذا كانوا لا يشهدون الزور فهل يفعلونه؟

* طالب: لا.

* الشيخ: من باب أولى؛ لأنهم إذا كانوا لا يحضرونه فإنهم لا يفعلونه قطعًا، إذ لو فعلوه لحضروه، فكل فاعل حاضر، وليس كل حاضر فاعلًا على وجه الحقيقة، لكنه فاعل حكمًا؛ لقول الله تعالى: ﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ﴾ [النساء ١٤٠]. فدل هذا على أن القاعد، سواء كان قاعدًا أو مضطجعًا أو واقفًا، والمهم أن المشاهد لفعل العاصي مثل العاصي حكمًا عند الله، نعم، إلا من أُكره على الحضور فهذا شيء آخر لا حكم له، كمن أُكره على الفعل.

* طالب: كل المعاصي يا شيخ؟

* الشيخ: كل المعاصي، نعم.

(﴿وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ من الكلام القبيح وغيره ﴿مَرُّوا كِرَامًا﴾ [الفرقان ٧٢] معرضين عنه).

﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ﴾، (اللغو): الصواب أنه ليس الكلام القبيح؛ لأن الكلام القبيح داخل في ﴿الزُّورَ﴾، لكن المراد باللغو: ما لا فائدة فيه، فكل ما لا فائدة فيه فهو لغو؛ وذلك لأنه لا يُقصد، وما لا يُقصد فهو لغو: ﴿لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمَانَ﴾ [المائدة ٨٩]. فاللغو ما لا فائدة فيه.

* طالب: لو كان مباحًا؟

* الشيخ: سواء كان قولًا أو فعلًا.

وقوله هنا: ﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا﴾ [الفرقان ٧٢]، ما قال مثلما سبق: ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا﴾ [الفرقان ٦٣]؛ لأنه هناك خطاب معين مباشر، فيقولون لا بد أن يقولوا قولًا يسلمون به، لكن هنا يمرون بالشيء بدون أن يُخاطَبوا به، والمراد بالمرور به سواء كانوا مارين هكذا في طريق، أو مارين مثلًا جالسين فجاء شيء لا فائدة فيه، لغو، فإنهم يمرون كرامًا، ومعنى (مر الكرام) هنا أنهم لا يلحقهم منه شيء، بل يحاولون الإصلاح؛ لأن الكريم يعطي غيره، ينفع نفسه وغيره، فهم إذا مروا باللغو يمرون كرامًا، يحاولون أن يفيدوا من وجودهم؛ وذلك بأن ينقلوا هذا اللغو إلى أمر مفيد. ولهذا قال: ﴿مَرُّوا كِرَامًا﴾ ولم يقل: قالوا سلامًا؛ لأنه هناك يُخاطَبون بما يسيء إليهم فيقولون قولًا يسلمون به؛ لأن المقام يقتضي بس أنك تسلم، لكن هنا ما يؤذون، إنما يمرون بلغو لا فائدة منه، فيمرون كرامًا مفيدين ومستفيدين.

﴿وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا﴾، قال: (معرضين عنه)، وهذا ليس بصحيح أيضًا، قد لا يعرضون عنه لكن يفيدون ويستفيدون، والإنسان الموفَّق يستطيع أن يفيد ويستفيد حتى فيما إذا كان المجلس مجلس لغو، يعني كلامًا مباحًا، يستطيع أن يحوله إلى كلام مطلوب؛ وذلك بما يستعرضه مثلًا من كون هذا الشيء الذي يتحدثون به دليلًا على قدرة الله أو على رحمة الله أو على حكمة الله مثلًا، فيفيد ويستفيد. لكن هذه الأمور في الحقيقة تريد رجالًا يعتبرون أنفسهم قادةً مصلحين، ما تريد رجالًا يعتبرون أنفسهم من جنس مجتمعهم يمشون الهوينى بدون إصلاح؛ ولهذا يفوتنا كثيرًا في هذه الأمور، يفوتنا كثيرًا والله من هذه الناحية، نجلس مجالس اللغو لا نفيد ولا نستفيد، غاية ما هنالك إن كان الإنسان استحضر نية التأليف وعدم الانزواء وما أشبه ذلك، وهذا خير، لكن ولو، الخير والأكمل أن تحاول الإفادة والاستفادة.

وبعض الناس أيضًا يريد بالمجالس التسلي فقط، ما يريد معنى وراء ذلك، وهذا فاته خير كثير. فعلى كل حال الناس يختلفون، والمسائل تعود على النيات، وكم من عمل عمله شخص وعمله آخر فصار بينهما مثل ما بين السماء والأرض: السجود يكون شركًا ويكون طاعة، إن سجدت لصنم كان شركًا، ولله كان طاعة، وهكذا جميع الأعمال، في الحقيقة النية لها تأثير كبير في إصلاحها أو إفسادها.

* طالب: (...)؟
